title: Data Engineer
description:
Responsibilities

  • Design data storage solutions, including databases, data lakes, and warehouses, using AWS services such as Amazon S3, Amazon RDS along with Databricks Delta Lake. Integrate Informatica IDMC for metadata management and data cataloging.
  • Create, manage, and optimize data pipelines for ingesting, processing, and transforming data using AWS services like AWS Glue, AWS Data Pipeline, and AWS Lambda, Databricks for advanced data processing, and Informatica IDMC for data integration and quality.
  • Integrate data from various sources, both internal and external, into AWS and Databricks environments, ensuring data consistency and quality, while leveraging Informatica IDMC for data integration, transformation, and governance.
  • Develop ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) processes to cleanse, transform, and enrich data, making it suitable for analytical purposes using Databricks Spark capabilities and Informatica IDMC for data transformation and quality.
  • Monitor and optimize data processing and query performance in both AWS and Databricks environments, making necessary adjustments to meet performance and scalability requirements. Utilize Informatica IDMC for optimizing data workflows.
  • Implement security best practices and data encryption methods to protect sensitive data in both AWS and Databricks, while ensuring compliance with data privacy regulations. Employ Informatica IDMC for data governance and compliance.
  • Implement automation for routine tasks, such as data ingestion, transformation, and monitoring, using AWS services like AWS Step Functions, AWS Lambda, Databricks Jobs, and Informatica IDMC for workflow automation.
  • Maintain clear and comprehensive documentation of data infrastructure, pipelines, and configurations in both AWS and Databricks environments, with metadata management facilitated by Informatica IDMC.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including data scientists, analysts, and software engineers, to understand data requirements and deliver appropriate solutions across AWS, Databricks, and Informatica IDMC.
  • Identify and resolve data-related issues and provide support to ensure data availability and integrity in both AWS, Databricks, and Informatica IDMC environments.
  • Optimize AWS, Databricks, and Informatica resource usage to control costs while meeting performance and scalability requirements.
  • Stay up-to-date with AWS, Databricks, Informatica IDMC services, and data engineering best practices to recommend and implement new technologies and techniques.

Requirements

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in computer science, data engineering, or a related field.
  • Minimum 5+ years of experience in data engineering, with expertise in AWS services, Databricks, and/or Informatica IDMC.
  • Proficiency in programming languages such as Python for building data pipelines.
  • Evaluate potential technical solutions and make recommendations to resolve data issues especially on performance assessment for complex data transformations and long running data processes.
  • Strong knowledge of SQL and NoSQL databases.
  • Proficiency in data modelling and schema design.
  • Excellent problem-solving and analytical skills.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills.
  • AWS certifications (e.g., AWS Certified Data Analytics - Specialty, AWS Certified Data Analytics - Specialty), Databricks certifications, and Informatica certifications are a plus.
  • Knowledge of data governance and data cataloguing tools, especially Informatica IDMC.
  • Familiarity with data visualization tools like Tableau or Power BI.
  • Knowledge of containerization and orchestration tools like Docker and Kubernetes.

title: Bathroom Measurement Technician
description:
Position Overview

Joyce Factory Direct is looking for an experienced Bath Measurement Technician to support our residential bath remodeling projects throughout the Cleveland market, with regular travel to Pittsburgh approximately 1–2 days per week.

This role serves as a critical link between our Sales and Production teams. After a project is sold, you’ll visit the customer’s home to take accurate final measurements, verify that the project can be completed as designed, identify potential installation challenges, and determine the materials needed before the project moves into production.

This is an ideal opportunity for someone with a strong residential construction background who understands how projects come together in the field and can spot potential problems before they become installation problems.

What You’ll Do

  • Visit customers’ homes to take accurate final measurements for bath remodeling projects
  • Review sold project specifications and confirm the proposed project is feasible
  • Identify potential construction, plumbing, structural, access, or installation concerns before materials are ordered
  • Determine and document all necessary materials and project requirements for the Production team
  • Communicate project changes, concerns, and recommendations to Project Managers and Sales Representatives
  • Review project details with homeowners and professionally answer questions about the upcoming installation
  • Maintain clear and accurate documentation, measurements, photos, and jobsite notes
  • Travel throughout the Greater Cleveland area, including locations approximately 1.5 hours from Cleveland
  • Travel to the Pittsburgh market approximately 1–2 days per week as business needs require

You’ll Be a Good Fit If You Have

  • Previous experience in residential construction, remodeling, or home improvement
  • Experience as a crew lead, foreman, project lead, supervisor, or manager strongly preferred
  • Strong understanding of residential construction and the ability to evaluate project feasibility
  • Excellent problem-solving and troubleshooting skills
  • Strong attention to detail and confidence taking accurate field measurements
  • Excellent communication and customer service skills
  • Ability to work effectively with homeowners, Sales Representatives, Project Managers, and installation teams
  • Ability to work independently and make sound decisions in the field
  • Bath remodeling or bathroom installation experience is a plus, but not required
  • Valid driver’s license and willingness to travel throughout the assigned territory

Compensation & Benefits

  • $50,000–$60,000 base salary, based on experience
  • Project completion spiffs, with expected total annual earnings of approximately $70,000–$80,000
  • Company vehicle provided
  • Health, Dental, and Vision Insurance
  • 401(k) with a 25% uncapped company match
  • Paid training and development
  • Employee discounts on home improvement services
  • Employee Referral Bonus Program

Who We Are

Joyce Factory Direct has been helping homeowners improve their homes since 1955. As a family-owned home improvement company, we specialize in windows, doors, baths, and sunrooms while maintaining a strong focus on quality products, professional installation, and an excellent customer experience.

title: Software Engineer, Frontend
description:
THE ROLE:

We're hiring a Software Engineer to join our E-commerce Team and play a pivotal role in shaping the backbone of our innovative Software as a Service (SaaS) products. This isn't a typical frontend role: we're looking for someone who's already adapted to building software in the AI era — who thinks in systems, moves comfortably across the stack, and treats AI tools as part of the craft, not a shortcut around it.

  • Ship iteratively and often, favoring fast feedback loops and continuous improvement;
  • Share knowledge, challenge ideas, and continuously raise the bar for our engineering practices and the team;

OUR EXPECTATIONS:

  • Experience in building reusable, scalable front-end architecture with a clear eye on how that translates into a better customer experience;
  • A genuine feel for UI/UX — instinct for what makes an interface work, not just checklist familiarity;
  • A demonstrated AI-leveraged mindset — you weave AI tools into your daily development flow, paired with the critical eye to not just judge correctness but optimize for it;
  • Ability to break down complex problems and implement practical solutions;
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or the equivalent gained through hands-on experience, open-source work, or a technical write-up sharp enough to speak for itself.

GREAT ADVANTAGE WILL BE:

  • If AI is an output multiplier for you;
  • If you are even more passionate about your work than ever before;
  • If you bring a team-first mindset and care more about solving the problem than proving you’re right;
  • If you get excited at the prospect of shipping tech products that push the web forward.
    • Come and make a difference at SiteGround with people who inspire you to grow!

  • Shorter workday on Fridays – we finish at 3:00 PM;

  • Free breakfast and lunch in our HQ restaurant, or provided by our trusted catering partners in the rest of our offices;
  • Free parking and a metro shuttle for convenient commuting;
  • Fully equipped in-office gym with professional coaches;
  • Sports activities and group classes (yoga, HIIT, table tennis, dancing, and more) - pick whatever gets you moving;

  • Premium additional health insurance coverage and annual medical check-ups;
  • Free massages to help you unwind;
  • Opportunities for professional development through trainings and conferences;
  • Company-backed volunteering, with 2 extra paid days off to support the causes you care about;
  • Memorable team events, internal gatherings, and company festivals;
  • A strong knowledge-sharing culture through regular meetups and internal conferences;
  • We remember milestones — anniversary and company gifts and surprises along the way.
If this sounds like something you’d be interested in, we'd love to hear from you!

title: Data Center Engineering Ops Engineer, DCEO
description:
Description

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

The Infrastructure Operations (Data Center) Team is the backbone of AWS, supporting the rapidly growing AWS business and customers 24/7. We are committed to maintain the physical infrastructure of AWS, ensuring the standards for operational performance in the areas of safety, security, availability, productivity, capacity, efficiency, and cost.

We are looking for a Data Center Engineering Operations (DCEO) Engineer with experience in critical facilities management, and a result-driven individual with strong technical understanding and the drive and vision to take our data center engineering operations to the next level. The DCEO Engineer is responsible for engineering operations including risk management and mitigation, planning, implementation of corrective and preventative maintenance for critical infrastructure and vendor management within our AWS Data Center environment. They are responsible for day-to-day operational excellence, maintenance of the critical infrastructure, supervising specialist vendors, acting as first responders to incidents, and becoming subject matter experts for the facility.

Key job responsibilities

The Data Center Engineering Operation Engineer is responsible for ensuring that all electrical, mechanical, and fire/life safety equipment within the data center is operating within contract parameters within facilities. Often this will be including risk management and mitigation, corrective and preventative maintenance of critical infrastructure, vendor management and metric reporting.

  • Meet daily hours of operations, on call requirements and response during rotations.
  • Manage minor and major planned and unplanned site works for critical infrastructure, with a solid understanding of the works involved, risks, mitigation and seeking approvals within relevant SLA’s as required.
  • Responsible for the on-site management of contractors, sub-contractors and vendors, ensuring that all work performed is in accordance with established practices, procedures & local legislation.
  • Prepare reports on all aspects of the data center facility infrastructure operations and maintenance.
  • Generate change management requests & incident management tickets for DCEO activities.
  • Coordinate with DCO managers (IT), Networking, Logistics, Safety, Security and other business leaders and operating partners to execute projects, manage capacity, and optimize plant safety, performance, reliability, sustainability and efficiency.
  • Review and follow the documentation relevant to technical support of business & facility operations.
  • Implement projects to increase current facility capacity, efficiency, sustainability & reliability.
  • Support operating partners in the resolution of any infrastructure engineering issues

A day in the life

  • Support troubleshooting facility and rack-level events within internal Service Level Agreements (SLA).
  • Perform rack installs, rack decommissioning, and facility management.
  • Provide operational readings and key performance indicators to make sure uptime is maintained
  • Performance and oversight of maintenance and operations on all electrical, mechanical, and fire/life safety equipment within the data center.
  • Work schedule changes depending on specific site needs. Shifts can be up to 12-hours and may rotate on a predefined schedule. Some locations have on-call rotations.

About The Team

About AWS

Diverse Experiences

AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS?

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture

AWS values curiosity and connection. Our employee-led and company-sponsored affinity groups promote inclusion and empower our people to take pride in what makes us unique. Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.

Mentorship & Career Growth

We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Basic Qualifications

  • High school or equivalent diploma
  • 2+ years of electrical or mechanical experience
  • Work any shift pattern within the 24/7/365 operation including days, nights, holidays, and weekends

Preferred Qualifications

  • 2+ years of data center engineering experience
  • Experience leading and managing operations of critical facilities which require in-depth knowledge in electrical, mechanical, and control systems
  • Experience in management of vendors/contractors performing construction, maintenance and upgrading works in large-scale critical environment

Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. If you have a disability and need a workplace accommodation or adjustment during the application and hiring process, including support for the interview or onboarding process, please visit https://amazon.jobs/content/en/how-we-hire/accommodations for more information. If the country/region you’re applying in isn’t listed, please contact your Recruiting Partner.

title: Director of Product Engineering
description:
Join Romac as our Director of Product Engineering, a newly created leadership role driven by continued company growth. In this role, you’ll lead a multidisciplinary team of engineers and technicians while setting the strategic direction for multiple product lines. You’ll play a key role in driving product innovation, strengthening manufacturing processes, and ensuring Romac continues to deliver high-quality, American-made waterworks products that support sustainable water distribution and long-term success.

If you don’t have direct experience in the waterworks industry, that’s okay as long as you’re curious and eager to learn. We welcome candidates with similar backgrounds in metal fabrication, cast products, or related industries.

What You’ll Do

  • Provide strategic leadership and direction for a team of 15–20 engineers and technicians
  • Lead product development initiatives from concept through full-scale production, ensuring cost, quality, and performance objectives are met
  • Apply technical expertise to integrate innovative features, resolve production challenges, and establish engineering standards
  • Drive process improvements, cost reduction initiatives, and ROI analysis for new tooling and equipment
  • Collaborate with sales, operations, marketing, and quality teams to align product development with customer and market needs

What You’ll Bring

  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related field, or equivalent experience
  • 10+ years of engineering experience, including at least 5 years in a people management or leadership role
  • Experience engineering cast, machined, or fabricated metal components in a manufacturing environment
  • Strong problem-solving skills with a proven ability to drive process and organizational improvements
  • Effective communication and collaboration skills, with proficiency in SolidWorks and standard office tools

Base Compensation Range: $146,400-$234,200. Compensation offered will be based on a variety of individual factors, including education and experience, as well as internal equity. Our salary ranges are reviewed and updated each year and employees are eligible for pay increases based on individual performance.

Benefits: At Romac, investing in our people is a top priority. In addition to competitive and equitable pay, employees are eligible for a quarterly discretionary profit-sharing bonus and a year-end bonus. We also provide comprehensive benefits to support employees and their families, including medical, dental, and vision insurance (with a 100% employer-paid medical plan option for employee-only coverage), a 401(k) retirement plan with company match, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, flexible spending accounts (FSAs), an employee assistance program (EAP), paid time off (PTO), paid holidays, and cell phone discounts.

Why Join Romac?

Since 1969, Romac has been dedicated to “connecting people to water” by designing and manufacturing innovative, high-quality American waterworks products. But our mission goes beyond products, it’s about people. We’re proud to create a workplace where employees can grow, contribute, and thrive while making a lasting impact on the communities we serve.

Our culture is built around four Core Values:

  • ONE ROMAC – Through humility, integrity, and determination we work together as ONE, to accomplish the objectives and priorities of the business.
  • PEOPLE FIRST – We care about the well-being and success of every person. Relationship development is central to everything we do.
  • CULTURE OF SOLUTIONS – We are curious, open and flexible as we solve problems and strive to continuously improve.
  • ALL-IN ATTITUDE – We are committed to excellence and fully engaged in moving the company forward.

Romac is an Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate in decisions involving any aspect of the employment relationship based on a protected status or characteristic, as defined by federal, state, or local law.

title: Clinical Director Designee (Alt DON(
description:
Clinical Director Designee (RN) – Home Health | Oahu

$125,000 ANNUALLY

Lead clinicians. Support great care. Step into clinical leadership when needed.

Always Best Care is seeking an experienced Registered Nurse (RN) to join our clinical leadership team as a Clinical Director Designee.

This position combines the hands-on responsibilities of a Clinical Supervisor with an important additional leadership responsibility: serving as the designated backup to the Clinical Director when the Clinical Director is unavailable.

You’ll work closely with the Clinical Director to support our clinicians, oversee patient care, strengthen clinical operations, and maintain high standards for quality and compliance.

This is not strictly a desk position. The Clinical Director Designee remains actively involved in patient care, supervisory visits, clinical problem-solving, and field coverage when needed.

💙 Why Join Our Team?

  • $125,000 annual salary

  • Key clinical leadership position within a growing home health agency

  • Work directly with and support the Clinical Director

  • Opportunity to develop experience in higher-level clinical operations and leadership

  • Mentor and support RNs, LPNs, therapists, and home health aides

  • Remain connected to patients and field clinicians

  • Help shape clinical processes, quality, compliance, and patient outcomes

  • Join a locally operated agency serving patients throughout Oahu

💼 What You’ll Do

Clinical Leadership & Staff Support

  • Supervise, mentor, and support clinical staff

  • Serve as a clinical resource for RNs, LPNs, therapists, and home health aides

  • Provide clinical guidance and help resolve patient-care concerns

  • Assist with staff orientation, training, competencies, and ongoing development

  • Conduct supervisory visits and competency evaluations

  • Promote accountability, communication, and high standards of patient care

Patient Care Oversight

  • Review patient assessments and plans of care

  • Ensure services are delivered according to provider orders and the established plan of care

  • Assist with complex, high-risk, or changing patient situations

  • Coordinate with physicians, providers, facilities, and interdisciplinary team members as appropriate

  • Perform patient visits, including SOCs, ROCs, recertifications, supervisory visits, skilled nursing visits, and other clinical visits as needed

  • Provide field coverage when necessary to maintain continuity of care

Documentation & Compliance

  • Review OASIS and other clinical documentation for accuracy, completeness, and timeliness

  • Help ensure documentation supports medical necessity and skilled need

  • Monitor compliance with Medicare requirements, agency policies, and applicable regulatory standards

  • Identify documentation or clinical deficiencies and assist staff with corrections and education

  • Collaborate with QA staff on audits, trends, corrective actions, and performance improvement

Quality Improvement & Clinical Operations

  • Participate in QAPI and performance improvement initiatives

  • Identify clinical trends and opportunities for improvement

  • Assist with implementation of corrective actions and process improvements

  • Support staffing coordination and continuity of care

  • Help ensure timely completion of clinical documentation, orders, assessments, and required follow-up

  • Support communication between field clinicians, clinical leadership, intake, scheduling, and operations

  • Participate in on-call responsibilities and provide appropriate after-hours clinical availability as needed

⭐ Additional Role: Clinical Director Designee

In addition to the responsibilities above, the Clinical Director Designee serves as the agency's designated clinical leadership backup when the Clinical Director is unavailable.

When functioning in the designee capacity, responsibilities may include:

  • Assume delegated Clinical Director responsibilities during the Clinical Director's absence

  • Provide clinical leadership and decision-making for day-to-day patient-care matters

  • Serve as the escalation point for urgent clinical issues

  • Support clinical staffing decisions and continuity of patient care

  • Provide guidance to clinical staff regarding patient-care and documentation concerns

  • Help ensure clinical operations continue in accordance with agency policies and applicable regulatory requirements

  • Communicate significant clinical, compliance, staffing, or patient-safety concerns to the Administrator and/or Clinical Director as appropriate

  • Exercise only those responsibilities that are within the RN's scope of practice and have been formally delegated by the agency

The designee function does not replace the Clinical Director position. The employee normally performs the Clinical Supervisor-level responsibilities described above and assumes designated Clinical Director responsibilities when coverage is required.

✅ Qualifications

  • Current Hawaii Registered Nurse (RN) license

  • Graduate of an accredited nursing program

  • Current CPR certification

  • Minimum 1 year of home health experience required

  • Supervisory or clinical leadership experience preferred

  • Strong knowledge of home health clinical operations and Medicare requirements

  • OASIS experience

  • Strong clinical judgment and decision-making skills

  • Strong communication and leadership abilities

  • Ability to supervise, coach, and mentor clinical staff

  • Ability to prioritize competing clinical and operational responsibilities

  • Ambulatory care experience preferred

🚗 Hands-On Clinical Leadership

This is an active clinical leadership position, not an exclusively administrative role.

Candidates must have:

  • Valid driver's license

  • Reliable, insured vehicle

  • Ability to travel throughout Oahu

  • Ability and willingness to perform patient visits

  • Ability to provide clinical and field coverage when needed

  • Ability to respond to clinical issues and communicate appropriately after normal business hours when necessary

Ready for Your Next Step in Home Health Leadership?

If you're an experienced home health RN who enjoys supporting clinicians, solving clinical challenges, improving patient care, and developing into a higher level of clinical leadership, we'd love to meet you.

Apply today and help us continue building an exceptional home health team serving Oahu.

title: Senior Software Engineer (Learn)
description:
About Us

Platzi is the largest technology school in the Hispanic world with over 7 million students and 4,000 companies trusting us to deliver effective online education. Our mission is to make Latin America a technology superpower. We do it by training companies and individuals in areas such as AI, Cybersecurity, English, Programming and Leadership.

As an industry leader, our presence is highlighted by our massive and fanatic community, extensive press coverage and a daily stream of success stories from students. We operate mostly remote, with key offices in Bogotá, Medellín and Mexico City.

Summary

As a Senior Software Engineer (Learn) at Platzi you're an engineer first: you build and own systems that hold up in production, and the material you build them with is AI. Orchestration, evals, and the models behind each decision, all serving how millions of students in Latin America learn in the product. You report to the AI Lead. Seniority here means judgment, not distance from the code. You take an ambiguous problem and come back with a decision you can defend, including the decision not to build, and you care about what your code costs to run and to maintain a year from now, not only about getting it merged.

Requirements

Responsibilities

  • Build AI features that ship to students, and own them in production: performance, reliability, cost, and how they recover when they break.
  • Design the orchestration behind them: agents, tools and the flow between them, built to be debugged and not just demoed.
  • Make evals part of how you work, so you know what improved, what regressed, and what you're trading off.
  • Choose the right approach for each problem, whether that's an LLM, a classic model, or plain deterministic code.
  • Make architecture decisions you can defend, and say no to complexity that doesn't pay for itself.
  • Raise the bar around you through code review, standards, and the calls that stop bad decisions early.

Requirements

  • At least 5 years building software in production, including owning a system through real scale or a migration.
  • Strong fundamentals: data modeling, APIs, performance, concurrency and failure modes.
  • You've taken LLM-powered systems to production, not prototypes, and you know where they broke.
  • You move comfortably across frameworks like Pydantic, Agents SDK and A2A, and can explain why you chose each one.
  • Experience with classic machine learning, and the judgment to know when a model beats a prompt.
  • A product you built that we can see and use.
  • Fluent English and Spanish.

Benefits

💻 Hardware

With Platzi's help, you will have 100% of the necessary work tools such as a laptop, smartphone, desk, ergonomic chair, monitor, and other accessories.

📗 Books

We provide you with all the books you need to grow professionally on Kindle, and we give you the Kindle too 😉.

🐣 Maternity/Paternity Leave

At Platzi, we believe in gender equity and the importance of parents in the upbringing and care of their children. We make this a reality for new mothers and fathers through extended maternity and paternity leave.

💸 Option Pool

All members of the Platzi Team have the opportunity to own a part of Platzi and have company shares.

🌴 Vacation

You have 15 days of vacation per year regardless of the country you are in, starting from the moment you join the team.

💆‍♂️ Online Therapy

We care about your emotional health by covering the first four online therapy sessions with specialized companies.

🌐 Team Syncs

Although we are in different parts of the world, Platzi teams meet in person during the year to exchange ideas, build, and strengthen bonds.

🏖️ Villa Platzi

Every year, the entire team gathers somewhere in the world for a week to meet face-to-face, get to know each other, have interesting discussions, and plan ambitious projects.

title: Mortgage Servicing Cashiering Specialist
description:
Mortgage Servicing Cashiering Specialist

📍 Little Rock, AR | 🕒 Full-Time | 🏢 On-Site

Build Your Career in Mortgage Servicing with Bank of England Mortgage

Bank of England Mortgage is looking for a detail-oriented Mortgage Servicing Cashiering Specialist to join our servicing team.

If you enjoy working with numbers, researching discrepancies, solving problems, and making sure the details are right, this may be a great opportunity for you. You'll play an important role in the day-to-day servicing of our mortgage portfolio by processing borrower payments, balancing transactions, researching payment activity, and partnering with our servicing and accounting teams.

We're looking for someone who takes pride in accuracy, works well with others, and can manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced financial services environment.

What You'll Do

As a Mortgage Servicing Cashiering Specialist, you'll help ensure borrower payments and other financial transactions are processed accurately and timely. Your primary responsibilities will include:

  • Process mortgage payments, payoffs, and other monetary and non-monetary transactions within the loan servicing system.
  • Review and process payments received through multiple channels, including lockbox activity, customer requests, mail, internal bank requests, and external partners.
  • Assist with payoff quotes and the posting of payoff funds.
  • Complete daily cash balancing and manual reconciliations to ensure transactions are accurate and accounts are balanced.
  • Research borrower payment histories and resolve payment discrepancies or account questions.
  • Process applicable liquidation transactions, including charge-offs, write-offs, and proceeds.
  • Work closely with Mortgage Servicing and Accounting to research transactions, reconcile accounts, and ensure funds are applied correctly.
  • Maintain accurate records and follow applicable regulatory requirements, bank policies, and servicing procedures.

What We're Looking For

Success in this role requires accuracy, organization, good judgment, and the ability to work with detailed financial information.

You'll be a strong fit if you have:

  • A high school diploma or GED.
  • Strong attention to detail and a commitment to accuracy.
  • Comfort working with numbers and performing mathematical calculations.
  • Strong organizational and time-management skills with the ability to prioritize multiple responsibilities.
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills.
  • The ability to research information, identify discrepancies, and independently work toward solutions.
  • Strong computer skills and the ability to learn financial and mortgage servicing systems.
  • The ability to work both independently and collaboratively as part of a team.

Even better if you have:

  • Previous mortgage servicing, banking, financial services, payment processing, reconciliation, or related experience.
  • Experience with Finastra or another mortgage loan servicing system.
  • Knowledge of mortgage payment processing, payoff transactions, or loan reconciliation.

Mortgage-related experience is preferred, but we encourage candidates with relevant transferable experience to apply.

What We Offer

Bank of England Mortgage offers eligible full-time employees a comprehensive benefits package that includes:

  • Medical and prescription drug coverage with two plan options and HSA eligibility
  • Dental and Vision insurance
  • Company-paid group life and AD&D insurance
  • Short-term and long-term disability coverage
  • Supplemental insurance options, including life, accident, critical illness, and hospital indemnity
  • Employee Assistance Program
  • 401(k) retirement plan with employer matching
  • Paid time off (PTO)
  • Paid company holidays
  • Paid bereavement leave

Most health and welfare benefits are available to eligible full-time employees beginning the first of the month following 30 days of employment. Benefit eligibility and coverage are subject to the applicable plan documents.

Why Bank of England Mortgage?

At Bank of England Mortgage, you'll be part of an organization with a long history in banking and mortgage lending while working alongside teams that are directly connected to the customers and loans we serve.

Our servicing professionals work collaboratively across departments and play an important role in delivering accurate, responsive service throughout the life of a mortgage loan. We value employees who take ownership of their work, pay attention to the details, help their teammates, and look for solutions when challenges arise.

If you're looking for an opportunity to put your attention to detail and problem-solving skills to work while growing your knowledge of mortgage servicing, we'd like to hear from you.

Equal Employment Opportunity & Accommodation

Bank of England/Bank of England Mortgage is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local laws.

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to participate in the application process and perform the essential functions of the position.

title: Sr. Project Manager & Business Analyst [EXE]
description:
ABOUT US

Herschend is the world’s largest family-held themed attractions company, with a portfolio of over 45 family entertainment brands, including destinations, resorts, theme parks, water parks, immersive experiences, and content enjoyed by audiences worldwide.

While each of our family brands offers something unique, all are united by a shared purpose: Bringing Families Closer Together by Creating Memories Worth Repeating®. Our 22,000 passionate hosts make this purpose possible through everyday acts of love and service—what we call Heartspitality®—the intersection of heart and hospitality.

As an equal-opportunity employer, we strive to provide environments where every host, guest, and partner feels welcome, valued, and loved. We firmly believe that words and actions matter, which is why all individuals are to be treated equally and with respect.

For more information, visit .

POSITION SUMMARY

Herschend is seeking a Senior Project Manager & Business Analyst to support technology initiatives across our theme parks, resorts, and attractions in our mission of Creating Memories Worth Repeating®. This role will lead complex projects through successful implementation across various areas of the business to ensure on-time and on-budget delivery of high-quality technology solutions. The ideal candidate brings strong project management discipline, practical business analysis skills, and the ability to translate business needs into clear deliverables that support operational efficiency and guest and host experience.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Lead multiple technology projects and/or workstreams from project discovery and initiation through implementation, ensuring alignment with business objectives, timelines, budgets, and expected outcomes.
  • Partner with business stakeholders to understand operational needs, define business problems, document requirements, and translate them into clear, actionable project deliverables.
  • Facilitate project discovery, requirements gathering, process reviews, and stakeholder workshops to clarify scope, priorities, dependencies, and success criteria.
  • Develop and manage comprehensive project plans, including scope, schedule, resources, milestones, risks, issues, dependencies, communications, and budget tracking.
  • Create, document, and maintain business requirements, functional specifications, process flows, decision logs, meeting notes, and other project artifacts needed to support successful delivery.
  • Analyze current-state processes and systems, identify gaps or opportunities for improvement, and recommend practical solutions that support business efficiency, scalability, and guest and team member experience.
  • Coordinate cross-functional business, technology, vendor, and property teams to drive accountability, remove obstacles, and ensure timely completion of project activities.
  • Manage project budgets, forecasts, vendor estimates, and spend tracking to support financial accountability and informed decision-making.
  • Manage vendor relationships throughout the project lifecycle, including coordination of deliverables, timelines, issue resolution, and alignment to contractual commitments.
  • Identify, track, escalate, and help resolve risks, issues, decisions, and dependencies that may impact project scope, schedule, budget, or quality.
  • Prepare and deliver clear project status updates, executive summaries, presentations, and stakeholder communications using project management best practices and tools.
  • Support solution testing, user acceptance testing, implementation planning, training coordination, change management, and post-implementation stabilization.
  • Serve as a trusted liaison between business and technology teams, ensuring shared understanding of requirements, priorities, tradeoffs, and delivery expectations.
  • Mentor and coach project managers, business analysts, and project contributors by sharing best practices, promoting consistent delivery methods, and supporting professional growth.

EXPERIENCE & EDUCATION

  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, information systems, business administration, project management, or a related field; equivalent relevant experience may be considered.
  • 6–10 years of progressive experience managing technology projects, business initiatives, or cross-functional workstreams in an IT or technology-enabled business environment.
  • Demonstrated experience performing business analysis activities, including requirements elicitation, process documentation, stakeholder interviews, current-state and future-state analysis, and solution definition.
  • Experience leading projects using waterfall, Agile, hybrid, or iterative delivery approaches, with the ability to adapt methods based on project scope, complexity, and business needs.
  • Experience managing IT infrastructure, enterprise systems, software implementations, integrations, vendor-led projects, and/or operational technology initiatives strongly preferred.
  • Strong ability to translate business needs into clear requirements, project deliverables, functional specifications, process flows, acceptance criteria, and implementation plans.
  • Proven ability to build and manage project plans, timelines, budgets, risks, issues, dependencies, communications, and executive-level status reporting.
  • Experience coordinating cross-functional business, technology, vendor, and operational teams in a fast-paced, matrixed organization.
  • Strong analytical, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills with a focus on detail, quality, practicality, and measurable business outcomes.
  • Excellent communication, meeting facilitation, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, including the ability to influence without direct authority.
  • Professional presence with the ability to establish trust, credibility, and productive working relationships with business leaders, technology teams, and external partners.
  • Strong organizational and prioritization skills with the ability to manage multiple competing priorities, shifting timelines, and complex project demands.
  • Experience supporting testing, user acceptance testing, change management, training coordination, implementation readiness, and post-launch stabilization.
  • PMP, PMI-PBA, CBAP, Agile Scrum Master, Product Owner, or related certifications preferred.
  • Experience in entertainment, hospitality, attractions, retail, or other guest-facing industries preferred.
  • Willingness to travel up to 25–30% based on project and business needs.

title: IS Sr. Infrastructure Engineer
description:
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer

Job Summary

The Senior Infrastructure Engineer is a principal technical leader responsible for defining and executing the organization’s infrastructure strategy across enterprise environments. This role drives architectural standards, ensures resilience and security at scale, and leads modernization initiatives such as cloud adoption and automation. The position partners with senior leadership to align infrastructure capabilities with business objectives, manages complex infrastructure programs, and mentors engineering teams to deliver enterprise-class solutions. The Senior Infrastructure Engineer influences technology roadmaps, enforces compliance, and champions innovation through strategic planning and thought leadership.

Essential Responsibilities

Core Infrastructure Architecture & Management

  • Define enterprise architecture standards and oversee implementation across multiple environments.
  • Lead multi-site infrastructure planning, capacity forecasting, and lifecycle management.
  • Govern VMware ESXi/vSphere architecture and advanced automation for disaster recovery and business continuity.
  • Establish standards for Windows Server environments, Active Directory, Group Policy, Intune/Azure Policy, DNS, DHCP, and patch management.

Networking & Security

  • Set strategic direction for network architecture and security frameworks, including zero-trust adoption.
  • Oversee advanced network design (switching, routing, firewalls, IDS/IPS) and enforce encryption and hardening standards.
  • Collaborate with InfoSec leadership on vulnerability management and compliance strategies.

Cloud & Hybrid Identity

  • Drive multi-cloud governance frameworks and cost optimization strategies.
  • Lead cloud migration initiatives and architect hybrid identity solutions with advanced Azure AD integrations.

Backup & Disaster Recovery

  • Establish enterprise-wide backup and disaster recovery policies and ensure compliance through audits and testing.
  • Oversee resilience planning for mission-critical systems.

Enterprise Applications & Services

  • Govern high-availability architecture for Exchange (on-prem and 365), Microsoft 365, SQL Server, and related enterprise systems.
  • Direct strategy for VoIP/telephony and internet services to ensure scalability and reliability.

Automation & Infrastructure-as-Code

  • Define automation standards and enforce Infrastructure-as-Code practices using PowerShell, Python, Terraform, and Ansible.
  • Drive organization-wide adoption of orchestration tools to optimize efficiency and reduce manual intervention.

Documentation & Compliance

  • Ensure comprehensive documentation for architecture, policies, and procedures.
  • Oversee adherence to security standards and regulatory frameworks (ISO, NIST, SOC).

Collaboration & Leadership

  • Provide technical leadership and mentorship to engineering teams.
  • Influence technology roadmap and participate in executive-level strategic planning.
  • Manage vendor relationships, negotiate enterprise contracts, and oversee infrastructure budgets.

Required Qualifications

Education: A bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related discipline is required, along with 4–6 years of relevant experience, or an equivalent blend of education and experience.

  • Technical Expertise:
    • Mastery of enterprise networking, security, and infrastructure architecture.
    • Advanced experience with VMware virtualization and Windows Server environments.
    • Expertise in Active Directory, AAD, Intune, MDM, DNS, DHCP, and patch management.
    • Strong proficiency with Exchange, Microsoft 365, and SQL Server.
    • Advanced scripting and automation skills (PowerShell, Python).
    • Proven leadership in cloud platforms (Azure preferred; AWS or GCP acceptable).
  • Soft Skills:
    • Strategic thinking and ability to influence senior stakeholders.
    • Executive-level communication and leadership skills.
    • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
    • Ability to manage enterprise-scale projects and budgets.
    • Commitment to confidentiality and compliance.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Advanced certifications such as Microsoft AZ-305, AZ-700, Cisco CCNP, VMware VCAP, CISSP.
  • Experience leading infrastructure operations and hybrid cloud architecture.
  • Familiarity with compliance frameworks (ISO, NIST, SOC).
  • Proven ability to manage multi-million-dollar infrastructure budgets.

Nice-to-Have Skills

  • Knowledge of ITIL practices for service management.
  • Experience with emerging technologies (containers, Kubernetes, edge computing).
  • Exposure to advanced monitoring and observability tools.
  • Thought leadership contributions (whitepapers, speaking engagements).

Working for Denver Water offers a rewarding and comprehensive employment experience marked by exceptional benefits and a strong organizational culture. Employees enjoy a robust 401(k) plan with employer contributions, a secure pension fund to support long-term financial well-being, and high-quality benefits that include a generous PTO package as well as medical, dental, and vision coverage.

At the heart of Denver Water’s workplace are its core values: vision, integrity, passion, excellence, and respect. These principles guide every aspect of the organization, fostering a collaborative and purpose-driven environment where employees are empowered to make a meaningful impact on the community and the future of water sustainability.

Position Summary

Under general supervision, manages Denver Water’s Key Accounts, including City and County of Denver and Master Meter accounts. Responsible for the monthly billing and account maintenance of Key Accounts representing more than $3 million in monthly revenue, ensuring billing accuracy, timely account updates, and data integrity within Customer Care and Billing (CCB). Serves as a primary point of coordination with the City and County of Denver, district billing partners, and internal departments to resolve billing and account-related matters and maintain effective working relationships.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Manage Denver Water’s Key Accounts, including City and County of Denver and Master Meter accounts, serving as a primary point of contact for billing, account maintenance, customer inquiries, and operational needs. Maintain effective working relationships with the City and County of Denver, district billing partners, internal departments, and external stakeholders.
  • Manage monthly billing for Key Accounts representing more than $3 million in monthly revenue. Analyze and reconcile account consumption, billing, meter data, and related records; identify and resolve discrepancies; process payments and appropriate billing adjustments; waive fees within established authority; and ensure accurate and timely billing.
  • Maintain Key Account records and billing information in the Customer Care and Billing (CCB) system. Update and verify account information, meter data, billing configurations, service records, ownership information, reports, and other data points to ensure data integrity, accurate billing, and complete and reliable customer records across the Denver Water customer base.

title: MEMS Process and Yield Engineer

title: Production Planner
description:
Who We Are

At BMI Merchandise ®, we’re in the business of fun! And we take it pretty seriously!

BMI Merchandise, founded in 1986 has evolved to become the amusement industry's leader in redemption technology and a top distributor of products. We source and distribute trendy toys, electronics, candy, gifts, and novelty items to amusement and family entertainment centers worldwide.

Production Planner

The Production Planner owns the daily and weekly production schedule and the information that drives it. This role extracts demand and order data from the ERP and business intelligence reporting environment, builds a production plan that sequences work against customer due dates and available capacity, and ensures that the commercial and operational sides of the business are working from the same picture.

The position sits between customer commitments and shop-floor capability. The person in it must be comfortable stating what the line can realistically produce and by when, and then holding that plan accountable through consistent measurement. Success is defined less by the production of reports than by the quality of the decisions those reports enable.

Responsibilities/Duties:

  • Assemble and maintain the recurring reporting set that supports production planning — open order backlog, due-date exposure, material availability, and line output — drawing from the ERP system and business intelligence tools, and own the accuracy of that reporting at the source
  • Sequence production orders against customer due dates, available capacity, and material readiness using the organization's planning tools
  • Identify scheduling conflicts early, present trade-offs, and escalate promptly when a commitment cannot be met without a decision above the Planner's authority
  • Rebalance the plan as priorities, material shortages, or unplanned downtime change conditions during the week
  • Publish the production plan on a fixed cadence to both sales and operations, in a format each audience can act on
  • Lead or contribute to the recurring production review, covering what is scheduled, what is at risk, and what has changed since the prior cycle
  • Define, build, and maintain the KPI set that describes line performance, including schedule attainment, run time and uptime, changeover time, output per labor hour, and on-time delivery to promise
  • Establish baselines, report trends, and provide enough interpretation of KPI data for leadership to act on
  • Partner with sales administration to align production commitments with customer demand, including reviewing incoming order volume for feasibility, communicating realistic lead times, and coordinating expedites, partial shipments, and date changes
  • Serve as trained back-up for sales order entry, providing coverage during absences and periods of peak volume

Qualifications/Skills:

  • 3+ years of experience in production planning, scheduling, materials planning, or a closely related operations role within a manufacturing environment
  • Working proficiency in an ERP system, including order, inventory, routing, and bill-of-material data structures
  • Strong Excel skills and practical experience with a business intelligence platform, including building and maintaining reports rather than only consuming them
  • Demonstrated ability to define, baseline, and report operational KPIs
  • Clear written and verbal communication, with the judgment to know what each audience needs to hear and when
  • Ability to operate effectively amid competing priorities and incomplete information
  • Bachelor's degree in supply chain, operations management, business, industrial engineering, or a related field preferred; equivalent experience such as military service in a planning, logistics, operations, or maintenance role will be considered
  • Exposure to lean manufacturing, Six Sigma, or other structured continuous improvement methodologies preferred
  • Experience supporting or participating in a sales and operations planning process preferred

Measures of Success:

  • Within the first ninety days: own the weekly production plan end to end, with the recurring reporting set running reliably and without manual rework
  • Within six months: a defined KPI package in place with established baselines, and a measurable, trackable trend in both schedule attainment and run-time performance

Work Environment/Physical Requirements:

  • Operates in both an office and a manufacturing plant environment, with regular presence on the production floor
  • Exposure to noise, moving machinery, and varying temperatures; personal protective equipment required in designated areas
  • Prolonged periods of computer work and occasional lifting of up to 25 lbs.

Department: Operations

Location: Cinnaminson, NJ

Job Type: Full-time, exempt

Salary: Based on experience

Benefits: We offer a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, and vision insurance, paid vacation, life insurance, FSA, and a 401(k) retirement plan.

Diversity: All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, or disability status.

Sprout is built on characters, and attitude matters.

As a Team Leader, you help set the tone for the whole restaurant. You’ll support your Restaurant Leader, lead great shifts, develop the people around you and help make sure our food, service and standards stay high every day.

This is a role for someone who enjoys taking ownership, loves working with people and wants to keep growing as a leader.

Reporting to: Restaurant Leader
Contract: Full-time
Pay: €16.35–€18 per hour, depending on experience and role

What you get

  • Guaranteed hours

  • Career pathway - 90% of our Restaurant Leaders were promoted from within

  • Learning & development through Sprout University

  • Free food on every shift, plus 50% off for you and three friends when you're off

  • Online GP access

  • Wellbeing and mental health support

  • Recognition that means something - Team Spotlight fund and Star Performer of the Month

  • Regular team socials and celebrations

  • The chance to help shape the culture and performance of your own restaurant

What you’ll do

Lead the team

Support your Restaurant Leader and help set the team up for success. Lead from the front, communicate clearly and make sure everyone knows what’s expected.

Develop people

Support new starters, coach people day to day and give clear, useful feedback. Spot potential in others and help them build confidence and take their next step.

Create a great place to work

Build strong relationships across the team, encourage open communication and help create a culture where people feel supported, recognised and included.

Deliver brilliant hospitality

Make sure customers feel genuinely welcome and looked after. Step in when something goes wrong and help turn difficult moments into positive ones.

Protect our standards

Keep a close eye on food quality, portioning, prep, presentation, cleanliness and restaurant procedures so standards stay consistent throughout the day.

Run great shifts

Own the daily shift plan, make sure everyone knows their role and keep things moving when it gets busy.

Support the restaurant

Work closely with your Restaurant Leader on stock, waste, rostering, recruitment, retention and the day-to-day things that keep the restaurant running well.

Champion safety

Make sure food safety, hygiene and health & safety standards are understood and followed by everyone.

You’ll probably love being a Team Leader at Sprout if...

  • You naturally take ownership and don’t wait for someone else to sort things out

  • You enjoy helping other people learn and grow

  • You’re comfortable giving honest, useful feedback

  • You like being in the middle of a busy restaurant and leading from the front

  • You care about food, service and getting the details right

  • You’re organised, reliable and someone the team can depend on

  • You enjoy building relationships and bringing people together

  • You’re curious and want to keep developing as a leader

If you’re looking for a leadership role where you can stay in the background, avoid difficult conversations or leave the team to figure things out themselves, this probably isn’t the one.

A little about experience

We’d ideally like you to have around 2 years’ experience in hospitality or another fast-paced, high-standard environment, with some experience leading people or taking responsibility for shifts.

You’ll need to communicate confidently, stay organised when there’s a lot happening and be comfortable holding standards across food, service, safety and the team.

More than anything, we’re looking for someone who genuinely cares about people, takes responsibility and wants to become a stronger leader.

If that sounds like you, we’d love to hear from you.

title: Senior Software Engineer
description:
The Senior Software Engineer is responsible for designing, developing, delivering, and supporting complex capabilities across the iT1 Nucleos AchieveDXP platform. This position serves as a senior individual contributor with broad full-stack ownership and is accountable for translating ambiguous business and technical requirements into secure, reliable, production-ready solutions. The role supports the continued scale of a digital experience platform used by education, workforce, and justice-sector programs and is expected to expand in technical scope, mentorship, and leadership responsibility as the engineering organization grows.

Essential Functions:

  • Design, develop, test, deploy, and support production features across the full technology stack, including a React and TypeScript front end, Node.js and Express APIs, PostgreSQL, a Rust network-proxy layer, and the AchieveDXP content-integration framework.
  • Own significant platform components and technical initiatives from architecture and design through implementation, deployment, monitoring, reliability, and ongoing improvement.
  • Develop and operationalize AI-enabled capabilities, including large language model features, agentic workflows, retrieval-augmented generation, evaluations, model selection, guardrails, and secure data-handling patterns.
  • Maintain secure and reliable services for multi-tenant, per-facility deployments in Azure Kubernetes environments using technologies such as Helm, Terraform, ArgoCD, containers, and CI/CD pipelines.
  • Contribute to architecture decisions, engineering standards, code reviews, testing practices, technical documentation, and the identification and resolution of platform risks.
  • Partner with product, implementation, customer-facing, and engineering stakeholders to clarify requirements, explain technical tradeoffs, and deliver solutions that address user and business needs.
  • Participate in the redesign and continued scaling of AchieveDXP to support increased usage and expansion into adult education and workforce development programs.
  • Mentor engineers, share technical knowledge, and help strengthen a distributed, high-trust engineering culture.
  • Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

Requirements

  • Minimum of six years of professional experience building and supporting production software, including substantial full-stack development responsibility.
  • Demonstrated experience independently owning complex or ambiguous technical problems from definition through production delivery.
  • Demonstrated experience delivering AI or large language model capabilities to production, including experience with agents, retrieval-augmented generation, evaluations, and pragmatic model selection.
  • Advanced proficiency with TypeScript, JavaScript, React, Node.js, relational database design, API design, and PostgreSQL.
  • Experience with cloud-native development and operations, including containers, Kubernetes, and CI/CD practices.
  • Ability to communicate technical concepts and tradeoffs clearly to technical and nontechnical stakeholders.
  • Ability to work effectively with customers and internal partners in a distributed work environment.
  • Must be based in and authorized to work in the United States.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Experience with Rust, Tokio, or Actix, or demonstrated ability and willingness to learn Rust.
  • Experience with browser automation, browser extensions, Manifest V3, proxy technologies, or network filtering.
  • Experience working with distributed or India-based engineering teams.
  • Experience in education technology or in secure, regulated, restricted, or air-gapped environments.
  • Experience mentoring engineers or assuming technical leadership responsibilities.

OTHER SKILLS / ABILITIES:

  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.
  • Ability to balance product outcomes, user needs, security, reliability, and delivery priorities.
  • Ability to work independently, manage competing priorities, and exercise sound judgment with limited oversight.
  • Collaborative approach, professional communication style, and commitment to documentation and knowledge sharing.
  • Interest in expanding access to education and economic opportunity through technology.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS:

  • Ability to remain in a stationary position and work at a computer for extended periods during the workday.
  • Frequent keyboarding and use of standard computer and office equipment.
  • Ability to communicate and exchange information with coworkers, customers, and other stakeholders through virtual meetings, telephone, and written channels.
  • Near-vision ability sufficient to review detailed information on computer screens and in technical documentation.

WORK LOCATION AND SCHEDULE:

  • Remote position within the United States. Remote is defined as your home location when hired.
  • Full-time schedule. Work hours may vary based on business needs and collaboration across time zones.

title: ACT Team Program Manager
description:
Lead a Team That Changes Lives

We’re seeking a dynamic, mission-driven leader to oversee our Assertive Community Treatment (ACT) team—an evidence-based program supporting individuals with serious mental illness in the community.

As an ACT Program Manager, you’ll guide a multidisciplinary team delivering high-impact, community-based care that reduces hospitalizations and helps people build stable, independent lives.

This role is ideal for a leader who thrives in fast-paced environments, values teamwork, and is passionate about improving systems of care.


POSITION OVERVIEW

Oversee Assertive Community Treatment Team Services that provide advocacy, service coordination, resource procurement, counseling, and support for clients in the program. Ensure high quality and high fidelity ACT services are provided to all clients. Responsible for hiring, supervising and training ACT personnel in addition to the overall management, evaluation, and budget of ACT programs.

REPORTING STRUCTURE

Reporting to this position are: Psychiatrist, Psychiatric Nurse, Case Manager, Mental Health Professional, Vocational Specialist, Housing Specialist, Addictions Counselor, and Peer Support Specialist.


SPECIFIC RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Hire, supervise, and train staff members; perform evaluations and initiate disciplinary actions as required.
  • Direct the day to day clinical operations of the team including scheduling and adherence to agency policies. Lead the morning meetings and the weekly clinical review meeting to assure all clients’ needs are being attained. Evaluate the status of clients and assure that intensity of contact matches the client needs.
  • Direct and coordinate the admission and discharge process of clients on and off the team. Assign clients to individual team members for primary responsibility. Monitor and coordinate the referral, intake, and orientation processes for new clients.
  • Provide clinical supervision of staff and weekly individual supervision of all staff.
  • Review the quantity and quality of services provided and documentation generated by the staff.
  • Perform crisis intervention and assistance as necessary.
  • Conduct regularly scheduled staff meetings to address concerns.
  • Ensure that documentation contained in client records meets accreditation requirements outlined by regulatory agencies.
  • Collaborate with the Core Service Agency and other community service organizations to promote the Agency’s mission and procure resources.
  • Communicate with other community agencies in regards to clients concerns or needs; schedule and/or attend community meetings as required.
  • Assure that all documentation in charts is being delivered and compliant with all necessary regulations and requirements.
  • Monitor medication and health concerns for all clients in the ACT program.
  • Monitor the budget as well as billing and grant expenditures for the program.
  • Become an expert of the ACT philosophy and follow and maintain high fidelity to the ACT Model of Care.
  • Assure the quality of services matches high fidelity of the ACT Model of Care.
  • Assure on call duty with on site response occurs on nights and weekends.
  • Assure that the ACT Office is operating efficiently and is clean and maintained.
  • Develop departmental policies as required.

PRINCIPAL ACCOUNTABILITIES

Staff supervision and development

Ensure client documentation satisfies regulatory agencies requirements

Coordinate ACT services to provide quality services

Client well being (clinically and physically)

Outside agency participation as required

Program billing and budget management


EDUCATION, WORK EXPERIENCE AND JOB REQUIREMENTS

Education: Master’s Degree in Social Work, Psychology, Counseling, Nursing, or related field.

Skill Requirement: At least three years' experience working with adults with chronic mental illness. License in a Mental Health Profession in the State of Maryland required. One to six months OJT required for efficient job performance.

Job Requirements: Excellent communication, problem solving and organizational skills.

At least two years of supervisory experience. Must have a valid driver’s license. Must have a clean driving record. Must have the ability to work independently with minimum supervision


COMMENTS

Must exhibit knowledge of mental health treatment.

NOTE: INFORMATION CONTAINED IN THIS DESCRIPTION IS A SUMMARY OF THE ASSIGNED DUTIES AND NOT INCLUSIVE OF ALL REQUIREMENTS THAT MAY BE ASSIGNED. ADDITIONAL DUTIES MAY BE ASSIGNED ON AN AS NEEDED BASIS

title: Computer Analyst ON SITE

Job Title: Laboratory Technician

Reports To: Primary Care Nurse Supervisor


Areas of Responsibility: Assists with laboratory operations, including specimen collection, processing, preparation, and handling for in-house and outside laboratory testing. Maintains laboratory quality, supplies, equipment, and workflow requirements while following applicable regulatory standards and outside laboratory requirements, including Labcorp procedures.


Major Duties:

  1. Play an active role in patient care using the provider led, team-based Patient Centered Medical Home Care Model
  2. Utilize the Electronic Medical Record (EMR) to assist in the delivery of quality care and to track on-going care for patients.
  3. Functioning as an integral team member, assist the medical provider in the provision of care, helping put patients at the center of the health care system, and assist with providing primary care that is “accessible, continuous, comprehensive, evidence-based, family-centered, coordinated, compassionate, and culturally effective.”
  4. Following policy, safely and consistently utilize Personnel Protective Equipment (PPE) at all times.
  5. Maintain a positive and professional attitude, striving to openly communicate with co-workers and patients, breaking down communication barriers when necessary.
  6. Function as the assistive testing personnel for the daily operations of the Lab following policies and procedures to ensure acceptable levels of analytical performance are met.
  7. Maintain phlebotomy skill to include venipunctures, capillary draws, and arterial punctures. As required, draw blood specimens from patients following standard operating procedures for identification of patients, specimen collection, labeling and handling.
  8. Follow current Labcorp requirements and standards for specimen collection, processing, labeling, handling, storage, packaging, and transport, utilizing Labcorp Link and other available Labcorp resources to verify test requirements and ensure specimens are appropriately prepared for testing.
  9. Work closely with the Laboratory Coordinator, Labcorp representative, and other members of the care team to address specimen processing questions, resolve issues, and ensure specimens are accurately and appropriately prepared for testing and transport.
  10. Assist with maintaining efficient laboratory workflows, including timely processing and preparation of specimens, monitoring pending laboratory work, and preparing specimens for scheduled courier pickup.
  11. Adhere to Lab quality control policies and procedures, documenting all quality control activities, instrument calibration and maintenance.
  12. Follow established corrective action policies and procedures whenever test systems are not within the Lab’s defined acceptable level of performance.

Physical Requirements:

Grade: 5

  1. Meet the minimum qualifications above with:

2. Four years of experience in phlebotomy and laboratory work.

Grade: 6

  1. Meet the minimum qualifications in Grade 4 above with:
  2. Seven years of experience in phlebotomy or laboratory work OR
  3. Phlebotomy certification by ASCP or other accrediting agency.

title: Full Stack Engineer - Ruby on Rails
description:
We are FeedbackFruits, an edtech company on a mission to make active, engaged, and personal learning the norm in education worldwide. We build tools that help universities and colleges turn passive lectures and content into collaborative, skill-building learning experiences, partnering closely with instructors and institutions to make that shift practical at scale. We're a hybrid team headquartered in Amsterdam, working with people across different countries who care deeply about the impact of our work on students and educators. If you're excited about improving education through thoughtful technology, we'd love to have you on board.

We're currently hiring a senior full-stack engineer to help us build the next version of FeedbackFruits. We are located in Amsterdam, and we have a hybrid work set-up with 2-3 anchor days at our Amsterdam HQ!

  • We believe in engineers who stay close to the product: domain experts who pay attention to how users actually behave and use the platform.
  • Most of the work comes down to one thing: making the product better. We rethink each feature from the user's perspective and rebuild it on stronger foundations, together with our designers and product managers.
  • We modernise the stack as we go, moving from Rails + Ember.js to Rails + Hotwire. There's deeper technical work alongside it, on performance, stability, and the platform, all in service of a product that feels faster and more reliable.
  • Stabilisation and simplification are our top concerns, from both a product and an engineering standpoint. We'd rather fix root causes for the long term than patch symptoms, even when patching would be quicker.
  • Our long-term aim is to get closer to our users by shipping faster, moving from one monthly release with regular hotfixes toward continuous delivery.
  • We've also adopted agentic coding and integrations to sharpen how we work, and we value multipliers: engineers who raise the people around them and put the team before their own output.

What you'll do:

  • Join one of our engineering squads and own full-stack delivery on the roadmap, from backend logic and database design to the server-rendered UI it connects to
  • Lead the migration of Ember features to Rails + Hotwire, which means understanding the existing functionality, redesigning it thoughtfully together with PMs/designers, and shipping something better than what was there before
  • Handle support escalations and legacy bug-fixing as part of the mix alongside feature work. The balance will depend on which squad you join, but keeping the codebase healthy and customers unblocked is part of the job
  • Contribute to improving our CI/CD practices and deployment pipeline as we work toward more frequent, more reliable releases
  • Keep performance in mind across the stack
  • Build and maintain integrations with Learning Management Systems using LTI and partner APIs
  • Participate in code reviews and technical design discussions, bringing both quality standards and a pragmatist's sense of what's worth the effort

What you bring:

  • You have 5+ years of professional software engineering experience and Ruby on Rails is your home stack: you've shipped production code with it, you know its conventions, and you're comfortable in its edges
  • You write tests as a matter of course, not as an afterthought. RSpec and Capybara are part of your regular toolkit, and you write tests that actually catch things rather than just confirm the happy path
  • You are user-oriented: when you're deciding how a feature should work, your first instinct is to think about the person using it, not the implementation that's most convenient
  • You've worked in a legacy codebase before and come through it well. You know what to fix, what to leave, and how to leave things better than you found them without getting stuck in a refactoring spiral
  • You understand CI/CD well enough to work within good practices and to nudge a codebase toward them when they're missing
  • You communicate clearly, give honest feedback in code reviews, and take it just as well. You’re collaborative without needing everyone to agree with you
  • You are pragmatic and document your decisions; you'd rather make a thoughtful trade-off and write it down than chase the perfect solution indefinitely
  • Familiarity with Ember.js or migration scenarios from it to Hotwire is a genuine advantage here; experience with AI dev tooling, Azure, or observability practices would serve you well too

What you get:

  • Gross yearly salary between €65.000 and €92.000 (incl. 8% holiday allowance)
  • 25 paid holidays per year
  • A day off for your birthday
  • Advantageous pension scheme
  • 3 days of volunteering leave per year
  • €550 Learning & Development budget per year + 3 days paid leave for learning
  • Commuting allowance and Swapfiets subscription
  • Free access to our office gym
  • Unlimited access to mental health support via OpenUp (EU, US, and AUS)
