Qualifications and Skills Required

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions.

Education and/or Experience

  • High school diploma or equivalent required; undergraduate degree preferred in HR, business administration, psychology, or a related field.
  • Three to five (3-5) years of experience in human resources, with direct experience in benefits administration, leave management, and HRIS are a must.
  • Experience with HRIS systems required; ADP Workforce Now strongly preferred.

  • Proficient in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint) and Smartsheet.

Other Skills and Abilities

  • Ability to run and interpret ADP reports of all types and translate data into clear, actionable analysis.
  • Strong ability to establish and maintain effective relationships with management, employees, service providers, and the general public.
  • Ability to present facts, training content, and recommendations effectively in oral and written form, including in front of large audiences.

location: Washington, District of Columbia, United States
description:
2027 SEIU LAW STUDENT PROGRAM

Service Employees International Union (SEIU) has openings for full-time law clerks for Summer 2027.

SEIU is a progressive, dynamic, and growing labor organization of over two million members in the United States, Puerto Rico, and Canada, united by the belief in the dignity and worth of workers and the services they provide. We are dedicated to improving the lives of workers and their families and creating a more just and humane society. Law clerks are paid $25/hour. Externs who receive academic credit can also receive compensation if allowed by their law school.

We are interested in candidates with a demonstrated commitment to workers’ rights and social change. The successful applicant will have a strong academic background with excellent writing and researching skills. Completion of a basic labor law course is preferred but not required. Please note clerk positions are open only to current law students.

Applications should include a cover letter, resume, short writing sample, references, and law school transcript.

SEIU is an equal opportunity employer.

title: Sesame Trader - Japan & South Korea Markets
description:
Job Title: Sesame Trader – Japan & South Korea Markets

Location: Singapore

Company: Torq Group

Role Overview

We are seeking an experienced Sesame Trader to develop and grow our physical sesame business in Japan and South Korea. The role combines customer acquisition, origin sourcing and end-to-end trade execution, with responsibility for delivering profitable growth and building long-term supplier and buyer relationships.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and execute a sesame trading and business development strategy for Japan and South Korea.
  • Build relationships with importers, distributors, processors and food manufacturers, including sesame oil producers.
  • Identify customer requirements for natural, hulled, black and other sesame grades, and secure suitable supply.
  • Develop sourcing relationships across relevant African and Asian origins, assessing supplier reliability, quality and competitiveness.
  • Negotiate purchase and sales contracts, pricing, payment terms and delivery conditions.
  • Manage the trading book, including volumes, margins, positions, inventory exposure and working capital.
  • Monitor crop developments, supply and demand, competitor activity and price movements to identify trading opportunities.
  • Coordinate with operations, logistics, finance and quality teams to ensure timely shipment, accurate documentation and collection of receivables.
  • Ensure products meet contractual specifications and applicable destination-market food safety, traceability and import requirements.
  • Manage supplier and customer claims, including quality discrepancies, shipment delays and contractual disputes.
  • Provide regular reporting on commercial performance, market developments, risks and the sales pipeline.

Requirements

Candidate Requirements

  • Demonstrated experience in physical sesame trading, with direct sales exposure to Japan and/or South Korea.
  • Established relationships with buyers in at least one of these markets and the ability to develop the other.
  • An existing sesame sales book in Japan and/or South Korea.
  • Strong understanding of sesame origins, grades, processing requirements, quality specifications and pricing.
  • Proven ability to originate business, negotiate contracts and deliver profitable trades.
  • Experience managing international shipments, trade documentation, payment structures and commercial risk.
  • Fluent business English; Japanese or Korean language skills would be an advantage.
  • Eligible to work in Singapore and willing to travel regularly to destination markets and sourcing origins.

title: Environmental & Sustainability Engineering Intern
description:
Your Story.

Would you like to learn how environmental regulations are applied in a manufacturing facility? You will have an opportunity to develop your skills and experiences as an environmental and sustainability professional. You will learn more about energy and water conservation, wastewater treatment, waste reduction, responsible sourcing, and sustainability reporting. The environmental & sustainability engineering intern will work under the corporate environmental engineer to help identify and implement sustainability and environmental improvements across the company.

Your Passion. Our Culture.

At Sargento, you work for a company you believe in, with a family of people who believe in you. Our culture stems from a simple premise: Hire good people and treat them like family. At Sargento, you can make decisions based on how they affect people as well as the long-term health of our company. You will be encouraged to make a meaningful difference in the community, in the company and in your career. With diverse experiences and tools to learn and develop, you can transform your aspirations into reality. If you’re ready for the right place to belong and grow your career, you can find it here.

  • Lead and own real and relevant projects aligned with business objectives
  • Gain valuable skills and experiences to be prepared for entry level opportunities
  • Mentorship and career development to learn and grow personally and professionally
  • Volunteer in community service activities
  • Social professional networking experiences
  • Flexible work week onsite Mondays through Thursdays and optional remote Fridays; plus, half day Fridays
  • Nationally competitive compensation
  • Paid relocation and housing
  • 5 unpaid days off for interns and 10 unpaid days off for co-ops
  • 401(k) employer contribution top 1% in the nation

  • Communication
  • Critical Thinking
  • Collaboration
  • Cross-Functional
  • Professionalism
  • Leadership
  • Technology
  • Time Management

What You Do.

  • Identify and prioritize continuous improvement opportunities that reduce water and energy use while delivering cost savings at manufacturing and corporate facilities.
  • Validate effectiveness of waste stream management channels. Perform waste stream audits, assist in diversion projects, and measure impact.
  • Investigate opportunities for grant funding, quantify applicable project benefits, and support the preparation and submission of grant applications.
  • Research new and emerging environmental and sustainability regulations documenting proposed next steps.
  • Present findings and recommendations to organizational leaders supporting the implementation of approved projects.
  • Create standard operating procedures and visual indicators to ensure successful initiative implementation.
  • Assist with tracking wastewater treatment costs and metrics at each production facility.
  • Perform hazardous waste, stormwater inspections, air emission, chemical and / or other environmental audits alongside the corporate environmental engineer.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams and business units to collect, analyze, and support sustainability data requests.
  • Support the evaluation, analysis and quantification of sustainability practices and performance across our supply chain.
  • Other projects or duties as assigned.
  • Maintain confidentiality with respect to Sargento’s proprietary information.

    Your Education and Qualifications.

    • Pursuing a bachelor’s degree in energy, environmental or earth science, physics, chemistry relevant engineering, technical based studies program, or a relevant life sciences area, having completed sophomore year prior to the start of internship.

    Our Story.

    With over 2,400 employees and net sales of $1.8 billion, Sargento Foods is a family-owned company that has been a leader in cheese for more than 70 years. We created the world’s first, successful pre-packaged sliced and shredded natural cheeses. Sargento is based in Plymouth, Wisconsin, where we manufacture and market shredded, sliced and snack natural cheese products, as well as ingredients and sauces. Sargento is known for the exceptional quality of our products and for product design, packaging and merchandising innovations that have transformed our industry.

Overview:

Serving the Yellowstone County community and south-central Montana for nearly 50 years, RiverStone Health is an essential provider of personal and public health services. Health, Education, Leadership and Protection – HELP is what we do. From medical, dental and behavioral healthcare; home care and hospice; public health services like immunizations, WIC, health promotion and restaurant inspections; and educating the next generation of health professionals, our expertise spans all ages and stages of life. Underlying principles of access, affordability, compassion and quality in all interactions, RiverStone Health improves life, health and safety for all of the communities we serve.

Job Summary:

Works with patients and community members to provide education and assistance related to insurance options and enrollment in Medicaid, Healthy Montana Kids, Health Insurance Marketplace and Medicare.

Essential Functions/Major Duties and Responsibilities:

A. Insurance Navigation 70%

  • Educate and assist individuals to enroll in Medicaid, Healthy Montana Kids (HMK), Health Insurance Marketplace, and Medicare.

  • Maintain knowledge of eligibility requirements for Medicaid, HMK, Health Insurance Marketplace, and Medicare.

  • Maintain accurate documentation in the electronic medical record (ECW) for insurance assistance and enrollment encounters.

  • Maintain a caseload of individuals that have applied for health insurance to facilitate completion of application and submission of required documentation.

  • Schedule and monitor daily insurance appointments to ensure individuals are seen in a timely manner.

  • Monthly outreach at RSH Satellite Clinic locations to provide insurance enrollment in underserved populations (Worden, Bridger, Joliet, WOW bus) and other locations as identified by the supervisor.

B. Patient Outreach 25%

  • Keep immediate supervisor and designated others accurately informed regarding work progress, including present and potential issues, as well as suggestions for new or improved ways of addressing such concerns.

  • Attend meetings, conferences, workshops, and training sessions to remain current on principles, practices, and new developments relevant to assigned work areas.

  • Return calls and respond to patients’ questions and comments in a courteous and timely manner.

  • Ensure that patients have access to primary medical and dental services by assisting them to understand the role of a primary care provider, select a provider, and make appointments or other necessary connections.

  • Educate staff on the importance of a team approach to patient care, emphasizing the collaborative effort between clinical and nonclinical staff (including physicians, nurse practitioners, physician assistants, nurses, medical assistants, educators, front desk staff, schedulers, etc.) to achieve stated objectives.

Non-Essential Functions/Other duties as assigned ≥5%

Education and Experience:

Minimum Qualifications

  • High School diploma or equivalent

  • Experience working in customer service environment, in person and on the phone

  • Any combination of experience and training which provide the equivalent scope of knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to perform the work.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Insurance enrollment experience

  • Experience working with underserved population

Certificates, Licenses, Registrations:

  • Successful completion of annual Certified Application Counselor for Health Insurance Marketplace (can obtain after hire)

  • Successful completion of annual Medicare SHIP Counselor Training (can obtain after hire)

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

  • Ability to work collaboratively and maintain a positive work environment.

  • Ability to prioritize and perform a wide range of tasks under pressure of continuous interruptions.
  • Ability to perform job duties with integrity and innovation to ensure completion and a high level of quality.
  • Ability to understand and adhere to required administrative policies and procedures.

Customer Service Excellence:

  • Showing respect for each customer.

  • Helping and going the extra mile.
  • Responding quickly.

  • Taking ownership of your attitude toward Service Excellence.

Systems Analysts (Robotic Algorithms and Controls Engineers) at Intuitive Surgical strive to create the safest and highest quality robotic system for minimally invasive surgery though rigorous and robust technical analysis. title: Financial Access Specialist
description:
Our Mission

All of us, for each of you, every time.

Our Vision

Together, serving as the trusted regional healthcare partner.

Our Values

Listen~Love~Respect~Excel~Innovate

At Samaritan, we do more than deliver healthcare—we make a meaningful difference in the lives of our community every day. We’re committed to creating an exceptional workplace where professionals feel valued, supported, and inspired to provide outstanding care to every patient we serve. The Financial Access Specialist serves the Hospital and Clinic by performing pre-service financial screening and clearance of scheduled patients, including benefit verification and price estimation. This position will maintain a proficient understanding of insurance plans, including State Medicaid, employer-sponsored plans, Medicare Advantage plans and Qualified Health Plans offered via the State Exchange. The Financial Access Specialist will determine benefit coverage levels and connect patients with alternate assistance resources as needed. The Financial Access Specialist interacts in a customer-focused and compassionate manner to ensure patients’ needs are met, and that they understand the hospital and clinic policies for the resolution of patient financial responsibilities and various payment options, including Financial Assistance. In all encounters with patients and families, the Financial Access Specialist will strive for the highest level of customer service.

This is a full-time position working Monday-Friday within the hours of 9:00am-5:30pm PST.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

  1. Review schedules for future dates of service on a revolving basis.
  2. Answer patient financial inquiries via phone and in-person regarding scheduled and/or future planned visits.
  3. Identify patients’ financial needs and align with appropriate resources.
  4. Communicate patient financial obligation, provide estimate, and pursue pre-service deposit.
  5. Collects from patients who have ability to pay, including past balances, down payments, co-payments and/or deductibles.
  6. With the assistance of person(s) responsible for pre-authorization and/or Pre-Registration Specialists, ensures authorization is secure prior to services and maintain accurate record of authorizations.
  7. Verify service-specific insurance benefits and provide benefit/coverage review. Accurately explain concepts such as deductible, coinsurance and/or co-payments and how they may affect the cost of care.
  8. Explain payment expectations for non-covered and out-of-network services.
  9. Review and explain all forms prior to obtaining signatures from patient or appropriate representative.
  10. Ensures appropriate forms are signed prior to services (i.e., sterilization permit, No Surprises Act, non-covered waiver, ABN, etc.).
  11. Collaborate with Case Management, Billing, Admitting, person(s) responsible for pre-authorization, and pre-registration with the goal of securing payment for services provided.
  12. Discuss financial arrangements for newborn(s); informs patients of the timeframe for enrolling a newborn in coverage, provides any documentation or guidance for the patient to enroll their child prior to or after the anticipated delivery date.
  13. Keep current with specific insurance rules and changes, including State Exchange.
  14. Aid patients in completion of Medicaid application via Washington Healthplan Finder.
  15. Promptly notifies insurance company of admissions and discharges per insurance company requirements.
  16. Communicate via phone, email, mail, and in-person regarding payment expectations.
  17. Comply with HIPAA regulations, maintaining confidentiality and utilizing information only as necessary to complete work.
  18. Utilizes appropriate strategies, including phone calls and online databases to verify the insurance coverage of scheduled patients to ensure services are provided and reimbursements are ultimately obtained.
  19. Documents all information obtained during patient financial screening to ensure a streamlined process for financial assistance needs.
  20. Strong organizational skills, ability to work independently and prioritize tasks.
  21. Ensures patient have logistical information necessary to receive their service (e.g., appointment place, date and time, directions to facility).
  22. Performs other duties as assigned. Ensures additional accountabilities, as may be required by management, be handled in a manner necessary to meet organizational standards.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

The professional in this position reports to the Director of Revenue Cycle. This position works closely with Scheduling (Hospital and Clinic), Financial Counselors, Case Management, Billing, Admitting professionals and Physician offices to ensure completion of all pre-service financial clearance functions.

EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE

  • Education:
    1. Minimum High School Diploma or equivalent required.
    2. Associate’s degree in healthcare administration or equivalent college coursework preferred.
  • Experience:
    1. 1-3 years of work experience with insurance verification, revenue cycle functions, hospital/physician offices or related area’s preferred.
    2. 1-3 years customer service experience required.
  • Skills/Competencies:
    1. Demonstrates competency on equipment listed on department specific checklist.
    2. Critical thinking skills: Seeks resources for direction when necessary.
    3. Performs independent problem solving. Decision-making is logical and deliberate.
    4. Performs actions that demonstrate accountability. Exercises safe judgement and practices within legal and ethical guidelines.
    5. Demonstrates competency in ability to care for customers/patients across the age continuum.
    6. Demonstrates strong organizational skills.
    7. Provides high quality customer service.
    8. Familiarity with statutes and regulations that can impact financial conversations with patients (e.g., 501(r).

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

  1. Occasional standing, walking, lifting, reaching, kneeling, bending, stooping, pushing and pulling.
  2. Light physical work, but mostly sedentary.
  3. Prolonged periods of sitting.
  4. Able to list up to 25 pounds.
  5. Good reading eyesight.
  6. Ability to communicate using verbal and/or written skills for accurate exchange of information with physicians, nurses, health care professionals, patients and/or family, and the public.

As a Samaritan professional, you will be asked to commit to being part of a culture grounded in our Mission, Vision, Values, and Strategy that brings service and operational excellence to life each day while creating an exceptional experience for our patients, professionals, physicians, and students. Additionally, how we present ourselves matters, and adherence to our Professional Appearance Policy reflects the pride, respect, and professionalism we bring to those we serve.

title: Assembly Supervisor
description:
Assembly Supervisor

Working Supervisor • Custom Automation Equipment • On-Site

The Opportunity

Fusion Incorporated, a family-owned leader in brazing and soldering automation since 1933, is seeking a talented Assembly Supervisor to keep our innovative Machine Division running smoothly in Willoughby, Ohio.

With nearly a century of excellence, Fusion delivers cutting-edge automation solutions, custom brazing/soldering pastes, and precision equipment to manufacturers across automotive, aerospace, HVAC, and beyond—right here just outside Cleveland. We are looking for a hands-on Assembly Supervisor who can lead a shop-floor team, keep builds on schedule, and still pick up a wrench when the job calls for it.

This is a working supervisor role. You will assign work, develop builders, order materials, coordinate with Engineering, Purchasing, Test, and Shipping, and stay close to the machine from first sub-assembly through crate and ship.

What You Will Do

  • Lead the floor. Supervise Assembly and Applicator teams. Assign work by skill, cross-train builders, and raise the overall capability of the department.
  • Build with the team. Jump in on machine builds, sub-assemblies, machining support, wiring, painting, and other assembly work when the schedule needs it.
  • Keep material moving. Order electrical, plumbing, hardware, tooling, lumber, and other supplies. Work with Purchasing to expedite purchased and vendor-machined parts.
  • Protect quality at the door. Oversee incoming inspection of vendor items and coordinate with Shipping/Receiving on outside finishing of machined parts. Oversee any in-house machining needs.
  • Partner across the building. Work with Engineering before and during builds. Sit in design reviews before final quotation. Attend weekly production meetings and Move-to-Test meetings. Support Test on debug, process, and lab samples when needed.
  • Finish the job. Confirm machines are complete through Assembly. Package and crate finished equipment. Coordinate shipment with Shipping/Receiving.
  • Support the customer and the business. Help Customer Service with component ID and recommendations. Keep Sales current on build status and new-machine potential. Work with HR to keep staffing at the right level.
  • Work safely. Follow prescribed safety rules and set that example for the team. Perform other duties as assigned.

What You Bring

We care more about a proven machine-builder who can lead people than about a perfect checklist. Strong candidates typically have:

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Hands-on background in machining, electrical wiring, pipe bending and fitting, pneumatics and hydraulics, and reading blueprints — usually developed through applied training and shop time
  • Experience supervising a shop-floor team (about 5 years is a solid benchmark; equivalent leadership on the floor also counts)
  • Experience building electrical panels (about 5 years is typical)
  • Deep time as a machine builder on automated equipment such as rotary or single-station machines (about 10 years is typical)
  • Ability to read and markup drawings, wiring diagrams, and written instructions
  • Comfort with hand tools and frequent lifting and moving of 20–30 lb. material
  • Clear, direct communication with builders, engineers, purchasers, and customers

Basic MIG or TIG welding is a plus. Combinations of education, training, and experience that add up to the same capability are welcome.

Who Thrives Here

  • You would rather solve a build problem on the floor than talk about it in a conference room
  • You develop people — you notice who is ready for more and you teach
  • You keep a schedule honest: material, people, and Engineering all stay in the loop
  • You take pride in a machine that is complete, wired, tested-ready, and packed to ship

What we Offer:

  • Medical, Dental, Prescription and Vision Coverage benefits
  • Paid Vacation, Sick Days, Holidays, Bereavement, and Jury Duty
  • 401(K) with Company Match and Discretionary Profit Sharing
  • Company Paid Life and Accidental Death and Dismemberment Insurance
  • Company Paid Short- and Long-Term Disability Insurance
  • Discretionary Company Bonus programs

This is a working supervisor role for someone who has built machines, led people, and still wants both. If you take pride in a build that is complete, on schedule, and ready to ship, we want to hear from you!

SiTime is the Precision Timing company.


Timing is the heartbeat of all electronics, ensuring performance, resilience and scalability. For decades, quartz devices, non-silicon technology, have kept systems in sync, but they struggle in harsher, more demanding environments. MEMS-based Precision Timing delivers greater accuracy, smaller size and resilience. Today, MEMS timing powers over 400 applications, including high-growth ones in AI datacenters, automated driving, industrial and humanoid robots, wearables and IoT.


Our semiconductor MEMS programmable solutions offer a rich feature set that enables customers to differentiate their products with higher performance, smaller size, lower power, and better reliability. description:
DELIVER SOLUTIONS THAT MATTER.

EVERY EXPERT STARTED SOMEWHERE.

Start here. Build something real.

DuraServ is looking for mechanically-minded problem-solvers ready to learn a trade, earn while they grow, and build a career with their hands.


This Is Where a Trade Career Begins.

DuraServ installs, services, and maintains the commercial dock and door systems that keep warehouses, distribution centers, and industrial facilities running. Behind every system that works flawlessly is a technician who knew what to look for — and fixed it right the first time.

As a Technician Apprentice, you won't be watching from the sideline. You'll be on the job, learning from experienced technicians, getting hands-on with mechanical and electrical systems, and building the skills that define a career in the trades. DuraServ's ADVANCE training program gives you a structured path to grow — and the income keeps coming while you do it.

If you're mechanically curious, physically capable, and ready to work for something you can be proud of — this is your starting point.

What You'll Do

Learn the Craft

  • Assist with the installation, service, and maintenance of commercial dock and door equipment under the direct guidance of experienced technicians
  • Participate in basic mechanical and electrical troubleshooting tasks — rolling doors, sectional doors, levelers, and dock equipment
  • Learn to safely use hand tools, power tools, and basic fabrication equipment to support installation and repair tasks
  • Study and apply technical manuals, wiring diagrams, and documentation alongside experienced teammates

Build the Standard

Who You Are

You don't need to know everything yet. You need the right instincts, the work ethic to show up every day, and the drive to get better than you were yesterday.

  • Mechanically curious — you take things apart to understand them, and you're not satisfied until you know why something works
  • Safety-conscious — you follow protocols without cutting corners, because you understand that safety isn't a suggestion on a job site
  • A learner — you absorb feedback, apply it, and come back the next day sharper than before
  • Physically capable — comfortable with frequent standing, bending, ladder use, and lifting up to 50 pounds regularly

Preferred

What's in It for You

  • Competitive hourly pay from day one — you earn while you learn
  • Structured advancement through the ADVANCE training program — your career progression is defined, not vague
  • Full benefits package: medical, dental, vision, and 401K with company match

  • A team of experienced technicians who take mentorship seriously and take pride in building the next generation of the trade
  • Autonomy as you grow — the better you get, the more you own


A Note to the Right Candidate.

If you've been looking for a career — not just a job — one where what you build with your hands matters and your work has a visible impact every single day, the trades are where that happens. And DuraServ is where that career starts.

Deliver solutions that matter. Start here.

The CDL Program Director analyzes student population data, working with faculty and staff to identify students who may be at risk, and contacting students to identify barriers to success and to provide support and information concerning student services. Finally, the CDL Program Director is responsible for continuous improvement of the program. Actively engaged in the development and maintenance of the campus effectiveness plan, the CDL Program Director collects data for purposes of analyzing program performance.

Key Responsibilities

I. Provides Services to Students

  • Supplements Driver Trainer advising for students receiving failing assessments.

  • Provides academic advising as needed to students. Provides referrals to outside resources when counseling needs go beyond the scope of the school. Provides or arranges for student tutoring when needed.

  • Leads student retention initiatives for students in the program who experience barriers to success.

  • Maintains regular contact with all students within the program area and responds to their questions and/or concerns in a timely manner. Posts office hours for students.

  • Refers students to appropriate staff for non-academic problem resolution.

  • Contacts students who miss days from class or whose absence during the week results in more than four absences during the course.

  • Maintains records of interactions and correspondence with students (i.e. phone calls, emails, mail).

  • Monitors contact, and results of contact, from Driver Trainers to students in assigned program area(s). Makes calls weekly to students who (a) were not called or could not be reached; (b) did not return as promised; or (c) did not offer plans to return by a specific date. Offers appropriate academic advice and demonstrates genuine interest in students.

  • Identifies students needing tutoring.

II. Oversees Status of Quality of Curriculum, Instructional Materials, Equipment, and Facilities

  • Serves as a subject matter expert regarding academic curriculum for program area.

  • Actively participates in the curriculum development/revision process led by the Home Office Executive team.

  • Provides leadership in the implementation of new and revised curriculum.

  • Provides input into creating the master schedule regarding course sequencing, offerings, room assignments, and Driver Trainer teaching assignments.

III. Oversees Faculty Performance and Development

  • Assists the Area Manager/Regional Program Director in the recruitment, interviewing, and hiring of faculty for program of study.

  • Orients, monitors, supervises, mentors, and assists new Driver Trainers.

  • Ensures that all program area Driver Trainers adhere to required administrative and classroom delivery duties and requirements as outlined in the job description for CDL Driver Driver Trainer.

  • Ensures completeness of faculty files and documentation of official transcripts, professional development, observations, and performance reviews.

  • Provides leadership and supports all Driver Trainers and supervises their instructional and program needs.

  • Observes classes within the program area and coaches Driver Trainers to continually improve instructional presentation and classroom management skills.

  • Conducts performance appraisals of department faculty members, including areas of strength and recommendations for improvement and future skillset development.

  • Conducts regular weekly day and evening faculty meetings. Meeting topics may include improvement of course offerings, methods of instructional delivery, selection of texts, and such other purposes which serve to improve the quality of the instructional program. Documents all meetings.

  • Provides departmental product knowledge training to Account management and Career Services personnel as requested.

  • Provides information to all departments as trends and changes in program specialty areas occur.

  • Assists account management personnel with student recruitment as requested.

  • Promotes faculty participation and provides leadership in the professional development activities of program faculty members and the documentation of those activities.

  • Participates actively in a minimum of one professional organization within the community.

  • Attends faculty meetings and in-service programs. Maintains a record of professional development activities.

  • Maintains current personal knowledge of federal and state institutional regulations, and accreditation standards related to program area.

  • Participates in preparation of government and accreditation reports and ensures their timely submission and accuracy.

  • Assists the Area Manager/Regional Program Director in evaluating data collected from student questionnaires and conducts faculty conferences when necessary to discuss the results and provides recommendations for improvement.

  • Maintains regular office hours each week to ensure consistency between day and evening policies, procedures and instruction.

  • Collaborates with peers and associates to ensure coordination of interdepartmental activities.

  • Intervenes in and works to resolve any personnel issues that arise among program area Driver Trainers.

  • Assists the Area Manager/Regional Program Director in planning program budgetary needs if and when applicable.

  • Performs all duties of a full-time Driver Trainer.

IV. Leads and Develops Others

  • Provides clearly defined roles and objectives for driver trainers, monitors performance, provides feedback, and meets regularly to discuss priorities.

  • Resolves individual and group performance opportunities in a timely manner to motivate and foster teamwork.

  • Identifies opportunities to involve others in new and challenging work assignments that advance the skills and capabilities of individuals and the organization.

Experience and Education Required

  • High school diploma or GED.

  • Industry certification in the field of instruction if required by industry, or demonstrated knowledge equivalent to the certification.

  • Class A CDL license with at least 2 years driving experience.

  • 5 years of industry experience in the field of instruction.

  • 2 years of experience in a management or supervisory role.

  • Knowledge regarding faculty development, including requirements, delivery methods, and reporting.

  • Ability to show sensitivity to the needs and requirements of adult learners.

  • Knowledge of industry standards and requirements within the field of instruction.

  • Knowledge of and ability to facilitate learning on course content within the field of instruction. .

  • Superior verbal and written communication skills.

  • Interpersonal relationship skills necessary for positive interactions with students, alumni, faculty, and employers.

  • Excellent creative and problem solving skills in dealing with students, alumni, employers, faculty, and staff.

  • Excellent presentation skills and ability to present ideas effectively to individuals or groups in a formal setting.

  • Management skills in planning, organizing, controlling and evaluating programs and policies in a dynamic and changing environment.

  • Knowledge of the federal FMCSA and state Department of Motor Vehicle standards.

Experience and Education Preferred

  • Associate’s Degree or higher, documented specialized competency within the field of instruction, or equivalent work experience in the field of instruction.

  • 5 years of experience in academic instruction in a post-secondary environment.

  • 10 years of experience in the field of instruction.

  • Working knowledge of federal/state government education regulations.

  • 3 years of experience in a management or supervisory role.

  • Previous experience as an academic program director.

  • Experience in student guidance, or related fields.

  • Working knowledge of federal/state government regulations.


Physical Demands

  • Mobility & Balance: Ability to frequently climb in/out of the cab, bend, squat, kneel, twist and reach to perform pre/post-trip inspections and navigate tight spaces.

  • Strength: Ability to crank trailer landing gear (often 100+ lbs), handle training and safety equipment, and potentially assist with loading/unloading (if applicable).

  • Endurance: Ability to sustain physical activity and be alert during extending driving and instructional periods, including exposure to varying weather conditions such as heat, cold, wind, rain, ice or snow.

  • Sensory Acuity and Overall Health: Must possess and maintain a valid DOT Medical Examiner’s Certificate and meet DOT physical qualifications required to hold a CDL, with or without reasonable accommodations, as required by Federal regulations.

Specific Tasks & Considerations:

  • Demonstrating Skills: Physically showing students how to couple/uncouple trailers, perform inspections, and maneuver the large vehicle.

  • Environmental Exposure: Working outdoors in various conditions including extreme heat, cold, rain, or snow while training.


Work Environment

Work environment characteristics described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is usually not exposed to weather conditions. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.


Note

This is not necessarily an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, skills, duties, or requirements associated with the job. While this is intended to be an accurate reflection of the current job, management reserves the right to revise the job or require that other or different tasks be performed when circumstances change.

title: Instrumentation Technician
description:

description:

title: Survey Assistant
description:
If you are looking for a place to grow your career and make a difference – RICK is the place for you! As a Land Survey Assistant and part of a land survey crew in Tucson, AZ you will have an opportunity to work with a multi-disciplinary team on meaningful, landmark projects in the Tucson region. As a RICK team member, you will help clients and communities turn their dreams into reality. You will learn from and work alongside industry-leading experts and together shape the future of tomorrow. At RICK you will find an abundance of opportunities for mentorship, growth, and (of course) fun! Learn more by visiting

The Land Survey Assistant is an entry-level field position supporting a modern land surveying crew performing boundary, topographic, construction staking including grading, building, site, and utility layout surveys. Working under the direction of a Crew Chief or licensed land surveyor, this position assists with field measurements, monument searches, construction layout, equipment operation, documentation, and site safety.

This position is well suited for someone who enjoys working outdoors, solving practical problems, using technology, and contributing to civil engineering and land surveying projects. Previous surveying experience is helpful but not required. Experience in construction or a related skilled trade will be considered relevant experience.

Duties

  • Assist the Crew Chief with boundary, topographic, ALTA/NSPS, right-of-way, utility, as-built, and construction-staking surveys.
  • Set up, operate, and properly store modern survey equipment, including robotic total stations, GNSS/GPS receivers, levels, data collectors, field tablets, rods, and prisms.
  • Hold and position survey rods, prisms, targets, and GNSS equipment accurately at designated locations.
  • Assist with construction staking for buildings, roads, grading, utilities, drainage improvements, curb, sidewalk, and other civil improvements.
  • Set and clearly mark stakes, hubs, lath, nails, whiskers, control points, and monuments with required offsets, elevations, stationing, and cut-and-fill information.
  • Read construction plans, grading plans, staking diagrams, and field sketches, and perform basic calculations involving distances, elevations, slopes, grades, and offsets.
  • Search for, expose, identify, and document property corners, survey monuments, benchmarks, utilities, and other physical evidence using appropriate hand tools and locating equipment.
  • Collect accurate field measurements, feature codes, descriptions, photographs, sketches, and notes for existing improvements and site conditions.
  • Maintain survey equipment, vehicles, batteries, tools, supplies, and organized electronic field files.
  • Communicate effectively with the survey crew, contractors, equipment operators, engineers, inspectors, and property owners while following company safety procedures and remaining alert to traffic, construction equipment, utilities, terrain, weather, and other field hazards.
  • Ability to lift 50 lbs
  • Stand for eight (8) to ten (10) hours per day
  • Swing an 8 lb. sledgehammer.
  • Work is performed primarily in outdoor environments, construction sites, roadways, and often in remote and rugged locations and subject to varies weather conditions.
  • Physical demands include standing for extended periods, walking on uneven/steep terrain, and carrying equipment.

Qualifications

Preferred candidate will have one (1) year of technical survey training, plus one (1) year of experience or equivalent work experience of two (2) years. High school diploma or equivalent.

No prior surveying experience is required for an entry-level candidate who demonstrates reliability, mechanical aptitude, attention to detail, and a willingness to learn. This is a great entry point to a land surveying career.

Previous experience in land surveying, construction staking, civil construction, or site development is preferred.

Experience in any construction trade will be considered relevant, including experience in:

  • Grading and earthwork
  • Underground utilities
  • Concrete and masonry
  • Carpentry and framing
  • Roadway or paving construction
  • Plumbing, electrical, or mechanical trades
  • Equipment operation
  • Landscaping or site work
  • General labor or construction inspection

Ability to understand measurements and perform basic arithmetic.

Ability to read a tape measure and recognize feet, tenths, hundredths, fractions, slopes, and elevations.

Basic computer, tablet, or mobile-device skills.

Ability to follow instructions, ask questions, and work effectively as part of a two- or three-person field crew.

Strong attendance, punctuality, and dependability.

Valid driver’s license with an acceptable driving record is required.

Knowledge and Skills Developed in This Position

The Land Survey Assistant will receive practical experience in:

  • Modern surveying equipment and field software
  • Boundary and topographic surveying
  • Construction staking and grade calculations
  • Survey control and leveling
  • Civil engineering and land-development plans
  • Field coding and electronic data collection
  • Survey documentation and quality-control procedures
  • Construction-site coordination and safety

What We Offer

  • Generous Benefits Package
  • Medical, Dental, Vision, Profit Sharing, 401K, and Life and Disability Insurance and Personal Leave
  • Company Events
  • Holiday Parties, Team Building Activities and Events and Alternative Work Schedule

RICK is an Equal Opportunity / Affirmative Action Employer

RICK employees are protected by laws designed to protect employees from discrimination on the bases of race, religion, color, sex, pregnancy, gender identity, sexual orientation, parental status, national origin, age, disability, family medical history or genetic information, political affiliation, military service, or any other non-merit-based factor. These protections extend to all management practices and decisions, including recruitment and hiring practices, appraisal systems, promotions, and training and career development programs. RICK employees are also protected against retaliation if they engage in a protected activity, whistleblowing, or the exercise of any appeal or grievance right provided by law.

title: Contract - Technical Designer
description:
Hybrid’s humble beginnings started in 1997 in the back of a print shop designing, selling, and printing tee shirts. Today, Hybrid is a global apparel industry powerhouse in brand and licensing management. Hybrid provides its expertise and fully vertical operations capability – design, merchandising, development, sourcing, production, and distribution – to a broad suite of branded, licensed, generic, and private label partners. Hybrid’s full-service apparel design and manufacturing expertise extends across the apparel category, including knits, woven tops, bottoms, tees, and accessories.

As our organization has evolved, so has our philosophy of doing business. We have made concerted efforts to remove ourselves from the antiquated approach of other apparel manufacturers and doing things differently has been our focus. We are building a company ethos that breeds innovation, collaboration, integrity and excellence in customer service.

What is my role?

As an Apparel Technical Designer, you will take ownership of the technical design process from concept to final production, ensuring high-quality construction, fit, and performance for apparel products. With minimal supervision, you will lead the technical development of designs across multiple accounts and product categories. You will work independently while collaborating with cross-functional teams, including design, merchandising, and production, to deliver exceptional products that meet brand standards and exceed customer expectations.

What You'll Do

  • Lead Technical Design Process: Independently manage the creation of detailed technical specifications (tech packs), including measurements, construction details, fabrics, trims, and stitching instructions for a variety of accounts and products.
  • Fit Sessions & Adjustments: Lead fit evaluations, assess samples, provide fit corrections, and manage fit comment reviews. Ensure that all adjustments align with design vision and quality standards.
  • Sample Development: Oversee the development of samples, from initial concepts to final samples, ensuring timely delivery, accurate execution, and adherence to design and quality standards.
  • Garment Construction & Detailing: Conduct thorough evaluations of garment construction, recommending improvements for design, functionality, and cost optimization. Provide technical guidance to improve manufacturing processes.
  • Account-Specific Management: Lead and manage the own private label process per account, ensuring that all account-specific requirements—including product specifications, branding, and timeline expectations—are met with precision.
  • Grade Rule Validation: Independently double-check and validate grade rules per account, ensuring sizing consistency, accuracy, and adherence to account-specific standards.
  • Vendor and Factory Liaison: Serve as the primary point of contact with vendors and factories for technical adjustments, ensuring that all products meet quality expectations and production timelines. Troubleshoot any issues related to construction, fit, and materials.
  • Pattern Review & Modification: Oversee the review and modification of patterns, ensuring they align with tech specs and meet the necessary design standards. Implement changes as needed to improve fit or functionality.
  • Collaborative Work: Act as a technical liaison between design, production, and merchandising teams, ensuring clear communication and alignment of product goals.
  • Quality Assurance & Control: Take ownership of the quality control process, identifying any issues during development, production, or fitting stages, and implementing corrective actions.
  • Project Management: Independently manage multiple projects, ensuring all deadlines are met, and products are delivered to specifications. Coordinate with various teams to ensure smooth workflow and problem resolution.

What You’ll Need

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Apparel Design, Fashion Design, Textile Design, or a related field.
  • Experience:
    • 5+ years of experience in technical design or a senior-level role within the apparel industry.
    • Proven experience managing private label development and working with multiple accounts.
    • Strong background in garment construction, patternmaking, grading, and fitting processes.
  • Skills:
    • Advanced knowledge of garment construction, pattern-making, and technical design processes.
    • Proficient in technical design software (e.g., Adobe Illustrator, Adobe Photoshop, Gerber, or similar).
    • Expertise in managing and overseeing multiple product development projects.
    • Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to work independently and prioritize tasks effectively.
    • Excellent problem-solving, troubleshooting, and critical-thinking skills.
    • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Personal Traits:
    • Ability to work independently and take ownership of projects with minimal supervision.
    • A proactive approach to challenges and a solution-oriented mindset.
    • Strong leadership and interpersonal skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across teams.
    • Highly detail-oriented with a focus on delivering high-quality, market-ready products.
    • Maintain, develop and implement data bases and systems (as required) which pertain to the technical information of products
    • Fosters open communication and team environment with all business partners; receives constructive feedback professionally
    • Holds self and others accountable for work commitments and outcomes
    • Ability to prioritize workflow based on deadlines
    • Must be detail oriented with strong organizational skills

title: Welding Trainer
description:
Welding Instructor – NJ Transit Bus Maintenance Welding Program
Lincoln Tech | WorkForce Lincoln Partnership programs

Position Overview

Lincoln Tech is seeking a skilled and experienced welding professional to serve as an in-house Welding Instructor for our training program preparing students for Special Mechanic – Welder roles with NJ Transit. This instructor will draw on deep hands-on experience in bus maintenance and multi-process welding to deliver practical, safety-focused instruction that gets students field-ready.

Key Responsibilities

  • Deliver hands-on instruction in a full range of welding processes including soldering, brazing, gas welding (steel, aluminum, cast iron), arc welding (DC electric, AC electric, MIG, TIG), and plasma cutting.
  • Teach students to lay out, fabricate, and assemble components, and to weld in all positions including sheet metal work.
  • Instruct students in bus body repair, including the removal, replacement, and alignment of body parts and components across multiple bus types (MCI, NABI, New Flyer, and coaches).
  • Train students in body filling, sanding, and fiberglass repair techniques.
  • Teach proper use of tools and equipment including hydraulic pistons, come-a-longs, porta-powers, and frame straightening devices.
  • Incorporate all relevant safety rules, regulations, and shop safety policies throughout instruction.
  • Instruct students in reading and interpreting blueprints, sketches, parts manuals, and technical drawings.
  • Teach students to accurately complete daily time tickets and required documentation.
  • Assess student progress through practical evaluations and provide constructive, forward-looking feedback to support skill development.
  • Maintain a clean, organized, and safe instructional environment

Required Qualifications

  • Minimum 5 years of hands-on experience in the welding field, with demonstrated proficiency across multiple welding processes.
  • Certified welder with the ability to provide copies of prior certifications.
  • Proficiency in reading blueprints, sketches, and technical drawings.
  • Strong knowledge of shop safety policies, welding safety regulations, and OSHA standards.
  • High school diploma or GED required.
  • Commercial Driver License (CDL) or Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP) required at time of hire.
  • Ability to pass pre-employment physical and background checks.

Preferred Qualifications

  • ASE certification.
  • Experience working on transit or fleet vehicles, particularly NJ Transit bus types.
  • Prior experience training, mentoring, or supervising welders in a shop or field setting.

Why Join Us?

At WorkforceLinc, we’re committed to empowering technicians and partners through innovative training solutions. Learn more about our team and approach at .

  • Join an established Skilled Trades education team with proven outcomes
  • Modern training facility with industry-standard equipment
  • Professional growth and advancement opportunities
  • Stability of a 75+ year institution

title: Team Lead-Technical Scrum
description:
Position Summary


The Technical Scrum Leader facilitates agile delivery for one or more Scrum teams, combining strong Scrum facilitation skills with hands-on technical fluency to bridge Product Managers, Business Analysts, and engineering teams. This role runs effective ceremonies, maintains backlog readiness, and proactively removes technical and organizational blockers impacting delivery. The Technical Scrum Leader partners closely with engineering leads to surface technical risks, dependencies, and trade-offs in terms the broader team and stakeholders can act on, driving predictable, high-quality delivery within an agile environment.



Primary Duties & Responsibilities

Scrum Ceremony Facilitation

  • Facilitate daily standups, sprint planning, sprint review, and retrospectives for one or more Scrum teams.
  • Ensure ceremonies are effective, time-boxed, and action-oriented.
  • Maintain backlog readiness above target thresholds, partnering with Product Owners and Business Analysts on grooming and refinement.
  • Act as a single source of priority for the team, resolving competing or unclear directives.

Technical Delivery Enablement

  • Partner with engineering leads to understand technical dependencies, architecture constraints, and technical debt affecting sprint commitments.
  • Translate technical risks and blockers into terms the broader team and business stakeholders can act on.
  • Support technical story refinement, ensuring acceptance criteria and definition of done are clear, testable, and complete.
  • Coordinate technical spikes and proof-of-concept work within sprint planning.

Blocker Removal & Escalation

  • Proactively identify and remove obstacles impacting team velocity and delivery commitments.
  • Coordinate user acceptance testing (UAT) and cross-team dependencies.
  • Escalate unresolved technical or organizational blockers to appropriate leadership.
  • Represent the team in the weekly Scrum Leader SOS to surface team status and cross-team dependencies.

Metrics & Reporting

  • Monitor and report team velocity, sprint burndown, and delivery predictability.
  • Ensure timely capture of Tempo time and consistent cataloging of scrum artifacts in Confluence.
  • Identify trends and process improvement opportunities from sprint and delivery data.

Agile Coaching & Continuous Improvement

  • Coach team members and Product Owners on Agile and Scrum best practices.
  • Champion continuous improvement initiatives within the team and across the broader delivery practice.
  • Support onboarding of new team members to agile processes and tooling.

AI Adoption & Innovation

  • Identify and pilot AI tools and practices that improve backlog grooming, reporting, and delivery efficiency.
  • Share learnings and best practices with the broader Scrum Leader community.

Other

  • Perform other duties as assigned.



Qualifications


  • Required:
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Business, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • 3-5 years of experience as a Scrum Master, Scrum Leader, or technical delivery lead.
  • Working technical knowledge of software development practices (e.g., APIs, databases, CI/CD, cloud environments) sufficient to engage credibly with engineering teams.
  • Proficiency with agile tooling (e.g., Jira, Confluence, Tempo, Azure DevOps, or similar).
  • Strong facilitation, communication, and conflict-resolution skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to translate technical concepts for non-technical stakeholders and vice versa.
  • Experience managing backlog health and sprint metrics.
  • Preferred:
  • Certified Scrum Master (CSM), Professional Scrum Master (PSM), or equivalent Agile certification.
  • Prior hands-on experience as a developer, QA engineer, or technical analyst.
  • Experience coordinating UAT and release readiness activities.
  • Experience evaluating or adopting AI tools to improve backlog grooming, reporting, or delivery efficiency.

The Move My Money Squad sits at the heart of ASB's digital banking experience, helping customers move money simply, securely and confidently. The squad owns and enhances key payments and transfer experiences across ASB's digital channels, ensuring customers can manage their money whenever and wherever they need to.

  • Contributing to architecture, design decisions and continuous improvement initiatives
  • Supporting the delivery of reliable, scalable and high‑performing digital banking solutions

About You

You take pride in delivering quality software, enjoy working collaboratively, and understand how strong engineering practices contribute to outstanding customer experiences.

  • Experience designing and building responsive, accessible and high‑performing web applications, with a strong understanding of modern front‑end architecture and user experience principles
  • Solid full‑stack capability, including experience building and consuming REST APIs and working with .NET‑based services and applications

  • Proven ability to provide technical leadership, mentoring and coaching, while working effectively with engineers, designers, product teams and stakeholders

Nice to have:

  • ASP.NET and MVC development experience
  • Experience working within large‑scale, customer‑facing digital platforms
  • Experience contributing across both front‑end and backend codebases

Working at ASB

At ASB, we're committed to helping our people get one step ahead as well. We know that meaningful careers are built through challenging work, continuous learning, genuine flexibility and the support of great people around you.

You'll have the opportunity to work on technology that impacts New Zealanders every day while being part of a culture that values collaboration, inclusion, wellbeing and growth.

Some of the benefits of working with us include:

  • Hybrid and flexible working options
  • Five days of lifestyle leave each year
  • Learning and development opportunities to grow your technical and professional skills
  • Internal mobility and career growth across ASB
  • Health, wellbeing and employee assistance support
  • Banking, insurance and partner benefits
  • Generous parental leave provisions
  • Access to engineering communities, mentoring and knowledge‑sharing networks

title: Inventory Specialist
description:
The Inventory Specialist is responsible for tracking and managing warehouse inventory to ensure data accuracy, proper stock rotation, and product availability. This role involves maintaining records in the Warehouse Management System (WMS), conducting inventory counts, and supporting inbound and outbound operations. It plays a vital role in upholding inventory accuracy and supporting supply chain effectiveness through detailed monitoring and reporting.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

  • Inventory Accuracy & Control: Maintain accurate, real-time inventory records in the WMS; track product movements and stock levels; initiate and document inventory adjustments when discrepancies arise.

  • Physical Inventory: Participate in or lead cycle counts and full physical inventory counts; investigate and resolve discrepancies caused by miscounts, damage, or data entry errors.

  • Receiving & Putaway Verification: Ensure incoming products are correctly labeled, documented, and stored; partner with receiving teams to address quantity, quality, or labeling issues.

  • Order Fulfillment Support: Ensure inventory availability to support outbound operations; monitor low-stock items and assist in initiating restocking processes.

  • Inventory Reporting: Generate and share regular inventory reports, including stock levels, turnover rates, and aging inventory; provide insights to assist purchasing, planning, and demand forecasting.

  • Process Improvement & Compliance: Recommend and help implement improvements to inventory procedures and practices; ensure compliance with company standards and regulatory guidelines.

  • System & Technology Use: Operate scanners, tablets, computers, and WMS tools; assist with maintaining item master data and troubleshooting inventory-related system issues.

  • Cross-Functional Communication: Work closely with warehouse, purchasing, planning, and customer service teams; communicate inventory concerns promptly and train team members as needed.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

  • Knowledge of inventory management principles (FIFO, LIFO, FEFO) and best practices

  • Experience using Warehouse Management Systems (WMS) and barcode scanning tools

  • Basic understanding of supply chain operations (receiving, storage, shipping)

  • Data analysis skills using Excel or Google Sheets

  • Strong attention to detail and organizational skills

  • Basic math and analytical problem-solving abilities

  • Effective communication and teamwork

Education & Experience

  • Degree Required: Not required

  • Technical Skills: Basic analytics and data tracking; operation of handheld scanners and tablets

Licenses/Certifications

  • None required

Job Scope

  • Decision-Making: Contributes to key operational decisions affecting departmental inventory management

  • Problem-Solving: Resolves varied inventory-related issues through interpretation and application of best practices

  • Independence: Operates with autonomy under broad direction; sets personal goals and determines methods

  • Fiscal Responsibility: None

  • Internal/External Contact: Frequent interaction with cross-functional teams and occasional external coordination

Physical & Work Requirements

  • Physical Requirements: Seeing, color perception, listening, lifting/carrying/pushing/pulling up to 40 lbs

  • Environment: Warehouse setting; exposure to dirt, dust, mechanical and electrical equipment, and moving objects; team-focused atmosphere; high noise levels

  • Mental Requirements: Basic reading and math, analytical thinking, decision-making

  • 2nd Shift: Afternoon start – evening finish

  • 3rd Shift: Evening start – morning finish

title: Clinical Specialist - East
description:
OrganOx is a commercial stage organ technology company dedicated to developing technologies to improve outcomes for patients with acute or chronic organ failure. The company was established as a spin out of the University of Oxford in 2008 and is now part of the Terumo Group. OrganOx is a pioneer in normothermic machine perfusion (NMP). It's flagship platform, the metra®, is available for use in the U.S., Europe, Canada, and Australia. It has been utilized in over 7,000 liver transplants to date to keep donor livers in a metabolically active state outside the body enabling longer preservation times and functional assessment of the organ prior to transplant, leading to an increased number of organs available for transplant. Founded in 1921, Terumo Corporation (TSE:4543) strives to fulfill its mission of “Contributing to Society through Healthcare” by providing a comprehensive range of solutions in the fields of therapeutic procedures, hospital operations, and life sciences in more than 160 countries and regions.

Position Summary

The Clinical Specialist will be primarily responsible for training and supporting users of our products. This includes teaching and training users in the correct manner to ensure our products are used safely and effectively - both for the preservation of organs prior to transplant, and for various clinical and non-clinical research studies. The role of Clinical Specialist will involve global travel, primarily within North America, visiting leading sites of transplantation surgery. This means the Clinical Specialist will be required to work after business hours, including nights, weekends and some very long days, which is the norm due to the unpredictable nature of organ donation and transplantation.

Requirements

Responsibilities may include the following and other duties may be assigned:

  • Train and support organ retrieval and transplant teams in the use of the OrganOx metra according to OrganOx’s policies and procedures.
  • Generally, on-call 24/7 for about 15 days a month (including holidays and weekends) for remote and onsite support.
  • Organize Site Initiation & Refresher Visits, training sessions (in person and remote) and centralized training events.
  • Effective and timely communication with transplant teams, internal management and coworkers.
  • Create and write case study review with guidance for senior colleagues.
  • When not on call, the clinical specialist will support managers, directors and other internal staff in various assignments, either remotely or onsite.
  • May participate in R&D activities in lab settings under the direction of management.
  • Work with the liver transplant teams to collect data on livers perfused and preserved on the metra to build up a database of product performance and use.
  • Ensure vendor credentialing requirements are current and able to pass routine background checks and drug screens.
  • Attend local, regional, national, and international meetings and conferences, in person or virtually, on behalf of OrganOx as a supporter, participant, or presenter as needed.
  • Develop and maintain positive working relationships in connection with end users of all levels.
  • Perform administrative tasks related to expenses, email, and other communication activities.
  • Ensure personal understanding of all quality policy/system items that are personally applicable.
  • Follow all work/quality procedures to ensure quality system compliance and high-quality work.
  • Other duties as assigned by Director of Clinical Support.

Qualifications and Requirements

Essential Requirements:

  • BS degree in combination with equivalent medical experience, with 3+ years’ experience in ICU, ECMO, Cath Lab, OR, Transplant, and ED
  • Regardless of professional background, must possess the following qualifications:
  • Must be highly flexible and willing to support sites as needed within and across North America
  • Must be detail oriented with strong organizational skills
  • Strong problem-solving skills
  • Outstanding interpersonal and communication skills; able to work collaboratively and build rapport with internal and external contacts
  • Excellent customer facing skills.
  • Ability to work calmly and professionally under pressure
  • Must be able to enthusiastically work at fast pace in dynamic environment and manage multiple priorities
  • Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint proficiency

Preferred Requirements:

  • A licensed RN, RT, RD and/or a health science-related degree
  • Industry experience in pharmaceutical or medical device

Other Qualifications:

  • Travel: Must be able to travel up to 50% of the time for training, investigator meetings, monitoring responsibilities, corporate meetings, and educational seminars.
  • Physical Demands: While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk, hear, and speak. The position may require sitting for significant periods of the day while working on the computer. The employee must occasionally lift or move items weighing up to 50 pounds.

title: DoD SkillBridge:
description:
DoD SkillBridge Internship: Lapping Technician
 SkillBridge Host Company: Bravo Ordnance
 SkillBridge Provider: Vets2PM LLC
Location: Cedar Creek, Texas (onsite)

Compensation Target if hired after internship (Estimate): $52K - $72K per year​


Applicants must be active-duty U.S. Military Members who qualify for the DoD SkillBridge Program.


To Apply: Complete this application and then go to and complete the SkillBridge interest form.

About this role:
Lapping is the precision finishing step that decides whether critical components meet the tolerances Bravo's warhead systems demand. As a Lapping Technician you will operate lapping equipment to bring components to specification, working under the Lapping Lead as the function scales with the production line. The work rewards patience, a steady hand with measurement tools, and the discipline to follow a written procedure exactly, every part, every shift.

At Bravo Ordnance, you are not a cog in a massive defense conglomerate. You are a builder. Founded by combat veterans and industry experts with backgrounds in the U.S. Navy, Army PSYOP, and nuclear engineering, we operate with startup speed and military discipline. We are backed by venture capital to build the tools of deterrence that protect the United States and its allies. Ideal candidate for this internship would be at the E5 level or below.

What success looks like in this role:
DAY 30 Trained and independently operating your assigned lapping equipment to specification under normal supervision.
DAY 60 Running a full shift's queue independently and consistently meeting tolerance and surface finish targets.
DAY 90 Cross-trained on additional part families or equipment, and contributing quality and process feedback to the Lapping Lead.

What you'll do:
Operate lapping equipment to bring components to specified tolerance and surface finish requirements. Inspect finished parts against specification using precision measurement tools, flagging discrepancies immediately rather than passing them down the line. Follow written work instructions and safety procedures exactly, and say so when a procedure does not match what the part is doing. Perform routine equipment maintenance and manage slurry, plates, and other consumables. Track production quantities and quality results against shift targets, with records clean enough to support lot traceability. Support the Lapping Lead on process improvement and on the written documentation the cell runs on.

Qualifications:
Required:
  • High school diploma or equivalent.
  • Technical or vocational training in machining or precision manufacturing is a plus.
  • Experience operating precision manufacturing equipment, or strong mechanical aptitude and the willingness to be trained from the ground up.
  • Comfortable using precision measurement tools including micrometers, calipers, and gauges.
  • Able to follow detailed written procedures exactly, and to stop and escalate when something is out of tolerance.
  • Must be a U.S. person as defined by ITAR (22 CFR 120.62), or otherwise eligible under an applicable export authorization.

Preferred:
  • Prior experience in lapping, grinding, honing, or another precision finishing process.
  • Experience in a regulated, high-hazard, or defense manufacturing environment.
  • Familiarity with reading engineering drawings and basic GD&T.
  • Military experience in a maintenance, machinist, ordnance, or other hands-on technical rating.

Where Unmanned Systems Become Weapons of Tomorrow:
Bravo Ordnance is a defense engineering company focused on the most decisive and most often overlooked element of modern warfare: the warhead. Headquartered in Cedar Creek, Texas, we close the gap between drones and munitions by designing and manufacturing high-performance, custom warhead systems for the next generation of autonomous platforms.

What we do:
The traditional defense industry moves in years. We move in days. Using industrial-grade additive manufacturing, advanced fluid dynamics, and in-house energetics research, we have compressed the development cycle from months to under two weeks. Our team takes a mission requirement from a napkin sketch to a combat-ready, tested system on a timeline the field is not used to seeing.

Why join us?
At Bravo Ordnance, you are not a cog in a massive defense conglomerate. You are a builder. Founded by combat veterans and industry experts with backgrounds in the U.S. Navy, Army PSYOP, and nuclear engineering, we operate with startup speed and military discipline. We are backed by venture capital to build the tools of deterrence that protect the United States and its allies.

Our culture:
  • MISSION FIRST. We understand the weight of our work. Our systems are designed so that the people who go into harm's way have the most effective tools possible.
  • RAPID INNOVATION. We value fail fast, fix faster. Our engineers have the freedom to prototype, test, and iterate in our in-house explosives facilities.
  • CLOSE COLLABORATION. You will work alongside forensic investigators, explosive chemists, and retired Navy weapons officers in an environment where technical excellence meets field-tested practicality.

  • Load, operate, and perform required reagent management on automated tissue processors.
  • Embed tissue into paraffin blocks.
  • Cut tissue using an automated or manual rotary microtome, producing 2–5-micron thick paraffin sections of excellent quality. Will also section control tissue as required by the department.
  • Understand the complex interactions of various pre-analytic, analytic, and post-analytic processes and how each one can affect the results of specialized immunohistochemical tests for predictive markers. Recognize and react to indicators of malfunction. Locate and implement corrections. Obtain analytical data, convert to a prescribed unit of reporting, as necessary, and correlate data to verify results.
  • Conduct quality control procedures on equipment, reagents and products and maintain proper records for quality control and quality assurance reports.
  • Prepare specimens for transport to MTF laboratory or for mail out.
  • Prepare biological waste for proper disposal.
  • Maintain regular and punctual attendance.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Requirements

Minimum Qualifications

  • Must be a graduate from a histology technician training program accredited by the National Accrediting Agency for Clinical Laboratory Sciences (NAACLS) or the Accrediting Bureau of Health Education Schools (ABHES) or educational program acceptable to the American Society for Clinical Pathology (ASCP).
  • Must have a certification/registration as a Histotechnician/ Histotechnologist from the American Society for Clinical Pathology (HT-ASCP/HTL-ASCP).
  • Must have at least one (1) year of experience within the last three (3) years as a Histotechnician.
  • Must have extensive knowledge of histochemical and immunohistochemical principles, theory, and methods to perform, such complex procedures as special staining and immunohistochemical techniques, and quality control for which there are standards.
  • Must have expert skill and knowledge in the use and general standard maintenance of specialized histological equipment such as microtomes, tissue processors, balances, automated staining devices and microscopes.
  • Ability to troubleshoot and perform minor repairs of above equipment.
  • Must have professional knowledge of human anatomy and physiology to allow for the appropriate gross descriptions and handling of tissue specimens.
  • Must have knowledge of the protocols, procedures, and reagents to produce special stains for specific tissue components or microbiological organisms.
  • Must have an Active BLS Certification.
  • Must obtain and maintain any necessary security access and/or background checks.

Desired Qualifications & Skills

  • Full knowledge and understanding of various tissue types and which require specialized embedding techniques.

Work Schedule

Full-time. May be required to work additional hours as needed to complete assignment or project.

Work Environment

Work is performed primarily in a clinical laboratory setting with exposure to biological specimens, chemicals, reagents, laboratory equipment, and biological waste. Position requires frequent interaction with laboratory personnel and adherence to established safety, quality control, and infection control procedures.

Physical Demands

Position requires frequent standing, walking, sitting, bending, reaching, and repetitive use of hands for handling tissue specimens, laboratory instruments, and equipment. Employee may be required to lift and carry laboratory supplies and equipment weighing up to 20 pounds. Position requires close visual attention and fine motor skills when embedding and sectioning tissue and operating laboratory equipment. It is Katmai’s business philosophy and practice to provide reasonable accommodations, according to applicable state and federal laws, to all qualified individuals with physical or mental disabilities.
