title: Clinical Coordinator_ 5196
description:
BronxWorks helps individuals and families improve their economic and social well-being. From toddlers to seniors, we feed, shelter, teach, and support our neighbors to build a stronger community. In all aspects of our work, we strive for the highest ethical and performance standards and are guided by the belief that people are to be treated with dignity and respect regardless of their present situation or past experiences.

Across our 60+ locations, we provide programs in a variety of service areas, including workforce development, children, youth, families, seniors and homeless prevention.

BronxWorks provides permanent supportive housing with an array of social services to more than 400 formerly chronically unhoused individuals and families throughout the Bronx. We strive to break the cycle of homelessness with personalized, wraparound support, empowering individuals and families to rebuild their lives with stability, dignity, and hope.

Position Summary

The Brook Supportive Housing Program is seeking a Clinical Coordinator to join an established multidisciplinary team. The Brook permanently houses 189 residents, the majority are formerly street homeless and have serious mental illness, chronic medical conditions (including HIV/AIDS) and substance misuse challenges. Reporting to the Program Director, the Clinical Coordinator is a vital member of our team. The position involves a unique blend of staff management and direct service provision. LMSW is required (MSWs are welcome to apply- however must obtain license within 3-6 months of hire). Clinical Coordinators provide psychosocial support, medication monitoring, financial management, crisis intervention, treatment planning and other supportive case management services and oversight to single adults in a community environment. With opportunities to further develop the clinical skills required to effectively manage the case management needs of a triply diagnosed population.

Ideal candidates can demonstrate the ability to work in partnership with our residents from a strengths-based perspective, overcoming stigma, and navigating complex systems. Additionally, the ideal candidate can adapt to an active environment, is exceptional with time management, has strong writing and communications skills, exhibits excellent attention to detail and remains a team player. Opportunities for group work are also available as are LCSW qualifying hours.

Qualifications

  • LMSW (Licensed Master Social Work)
  • Minimum of two years' experience working with homeless populations
  • Experience with providing behavioral health services

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Contribute towards the ongoing development and quality of services provided
  • Adhere to the agency and funder policies, principles, and procedures (DOHMH, HASA and DHS)
  • Hold ongoing clinical and task supervision with social services staff.
  • Supervise documentation of progress notes and ongoing assessments in AWARDS
  • Maintain physical case records and statistics for program to analyze trends and improve service delivery
  • Ensure all programs meet contractual goals and reporting requirements
  • Administer personnel policies and procedures under the guidance of the program director
  • Assist the program director in recruiting and training direct service staff
  • Participate in, and encourage staff to become involved in agency events
  • Act as Liaison with medical clinic staff on and off-site as needed
  • Coordinate clinical services for Residents including discharge planning
  • Provide crisis management and on-going clinical assessments
  • Provide supportive counseling and behavioral health services
  • Remain on call after hours and on weekends to assist with resident medical and psychiatric incidents
  • Assist with financial management for residents enrolled in our representative payee program
  • Complete Medication Monitoring Training within 3-6 months of hire
  • Perform additional duties as assigned

Program Specific Skills

  • Strong writing and oral communication skills
  • Excellent organizational, teambuilding, and leadership skills
  • Demonstrated skills to work within a team model and provide team leadership in team meetings
  • Experience supervising case management staff preferred
  • Strong presentation skills and ability to represent the agency at functions and meetings
  • Ability to handle complex challenges and balance multiple demands on time and attention
  • Community minded, patient, creative, flexible, and compassionate
  • Demonstrated proficiency with MS Office, electronic databases and prolonged use of a computer

Skills/Abilities

  • Ability to occasionally lift and/or move up to 10 pounds
  • Ability to stand, walk, or sit for long periods of time
  • Ability to conduct home visits and/or fieldwork
  • Ability to bend and retrieve objects and/or documents

title: Quantitative Research Analyst
description:
This is a technical, behind-the-scenes role responsible for supporting the execution and quality of the organization's quantitative research.

You will work across studies to ensure surveys are programmed correctly, data is clean and accurate, and reporting outputs are client-ready. This includes program checking, data scanning and cleaning, data processing, report population, and rigorous numerical QC.

This is an ideal role for someone who enjoys the technical and operational side of quantitative research, has exceptional attention to detail, and naturally notices when something in the data doesn’t look right.

Duties and Responsibilities

Survey Programming & QA

  • Review programmed surveys against questionnaires for accuracy and consistency
  • Test survey logic, skips, piping, randomization, quotas, calculations, and respondent flow
  • Conduct soft-launch data checks and identify potential programming or fieldwork issues
  • Partner with researchers and programming vendors to troubleshoot and resolve issues

Data Quality & Processing

  • Scan and clean respondent-level data throughout fieldwork and at study close
  • Identify poor-quality respondents, inconsistent responses, suspicious open ends, speeders, straightliners, and other data-quality concerns
  • Investigate unexpected data patterns and troubleshoot potential programming, sampling, or data-processing issues
  • Support recodes, derived variables, banners, crosstabs, weighting, and significance testing
  • Review data tables and other outputs for accuracy and consistency

Reporting & Analysis Support

  • Populate PowerPoint reports with survey data, including charts and tables
  • Check bases, percentages, significance, calculations, and data labels
  • Conduct rigorous numerical QC of client deliverables
  • Troubleshoot discrepancies across raw data, tables, and reporting outputs
  • Prepare clean, analysis-ready data and outputs for research teams

Operational Excellence

  • Serve as a centralized resource for quantitative research quality and technical execution
  • Develop and improve standardized processes for program checking, data cleaning, reporting, and QC
  • Identify opportunities to automate or streamline repetitive quantitative workflows
  • Learn and leverage AI-powered tools and platforms to improve efficiency and quality

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree (market research, psychology, sociology, business, communications, or related field preferred)
  • 0–2 years of experience (internships count)
  • High attention to detail
  • Strong analytical and writing skills
  • Proficiency in Excel and PowerPoint (experience with survey or analytics tools a plus)
  • Ability to manage multiple deadlines in a remote environment

The purpose of this entry-level, full-time position is to install and maintain billboards, including the installation of advertisements, maintenance of structures, and the construction upkeep of billboard cosmetics. This position most often works alone and must be able to manage work schedules effectively.

Why Lamar?

Want a career that takes you above the everyday? As part of Lamar’s billboard construction and operations crew, you’ll experience the city from a bird’s-eye view while building and maintaining the structures that keep communities informed. Join a team that values safety, teamwork, and adventure—every single day. See our operations crew in action over on YouTube.
Lamar is a certified Great Place to Work, with 88% of employees in agreement. Lamar Advertising has also been named as a “Best Company to Work For” in U.S. News & World Report’s annual ranking.
  • Learn more about us on our official YouTube channel.
  • Check reviews and company updates on our Glassdoor page
  • Learn more about our Great Place to Work certification.

      What you can expect from us:

      • A Monday - Friday 7am - 3:30pm work schedule
      • An hourly range of $16 - $18/ hour, dependent on relevant experience and qualifications
      • 120 hours of paid time off (PTO) that increases with tenure
      • 12 paid company holidays, including President's Day and Juneteenth
      • A comprehensive training program
      • Career advancement opportunities
      • Ongoing professional development and internal leadership programs to maximize your career potential
      • Multiple medical plan options and health savings account
      • Hospital, Critical Illness, and Accident coverage
      • Short & long-term disability and paid parental leave

      A Day in the Life:

      As an Installer, you can expect to work alongside the Operations team to install and maintain billboards while prioritizing the safety of yourself and others. Installation most often includes handling a large advertisement printed on vinyl and ensuring it is properly assembled to the billboard structure. The tallest billboard structure in the company is around 200 feet, so comfort with heights is a must.

      Maintenance of our billboards includes construction work such as tightening bolts, painting steel structures, repairing trim and various parts of a billboard sign face and structure, changing light bulbs, and more. As for power/manual tools: you bring the experience, we bring the equipment!

      In this role you'll be expected to:

      • Remove and hang flexes from billboards, remove and hang vinyls, cut and prepare flexes and vinyls for installation, cut, prepare and install copies on Tri-Visions
      • Build and install extensions on billboards, cut brush/weeds, conduct storm damage repairs and minor electrical repairs, and maintain a clean workshop area
      • Use power/manual tools while adhering to safety regulations
      • Attend installer and construction safety meetings as required
      • Maintain operation vehicles; maintain construction tools, equipment, and machinery
      • Take completion photos for proof of performance of installations

      What we're looking for in YOU:

      • Ability to work alone and manage your work schedule effectively
      • Willingness to work at heights up to 100 feet above the ground
      • Strong communication skills. Ability to speak and read English fluently.
      • Willingness to work and get along well with others
      • Basic computer skills, including Internet navigation and Microsoft Word & Excel.
      • Ability to work from ladders and to carry a ladder and/or other tools to the worksite from vehicle.
      • Working knowledge of electrical skills and techniques.
      • Working knowledge of fabrication skills and techniques.
      • Skill in reading technical documents, such as blueprints and diagrams.
      • General knowledge of Lamar, Department of Transportation (DOT), and Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) safety regulations
      • Ability to safely use construction equipment
      • Ability to climb heights and work at heights above ground safely
      • Ability to document installations through photographs and written logs
      • Skill in the practical applications of mathematics, in relation to construction and operations tasks
      • Skill in setting priorities that accurately reflect the relative importance of job responsibilities

      Education and Experience Requirements:

      • A high school diploma or equivalent is required
      • A valid driver’s license is required.
      • Ability to complete OSHA 10-hour Construction course required
      • CDL and Non-CDL licenses are a plus, but not required!
      • Previous experience working at heights up to 200 ft. above ground preferred
      • Construction and/or billboard installation experience is a plus, but not required

      Please note: Upon submitting your application, you will be asked to complete an 8-15 minute personality assessment. This assessment compares your professional soft skills to the skills required for success in this role. Please answer honestly; this is not a test! Not completing this assessment could result in disqualification from consideration for this position.

      Candidates with a disability in need of an accommodation to fulfill our application requirements should email recruiting@lamar.com.

      Physical Demands and Work Environment:

      • The primary work environment for this position is outdoors, requiring the ability to work in adverse weather conditions and climb to heights up to 200 ft.
      • The physical demands for this position include heavy lifting (up to 100 pounds), extensive bending, pushing, reaching, seeing (with a focus on reading, color distinction, acuity, depth perception, and peripheral vision), sitting less than 50% of the time, standing, stooping, talking, turning, walking, driving, and climbing.
      • Nights spent away from home traveling are less than 10%.
      • On-call shifts may be required.

      Who we are:

      Founded in 1902, Lamar Advertising Company is one of the largest outdoor advertising companies in the world. With over 360,000 displays across the United States and Canada, Lamar is dedicated to helping both local businesses and national brands reach broad audiences every day.

      We provide ad space through:

      • Billboards

      • Handpainted murals
      • Transportation and airports
      • The largest network of digital billboards in the United States

We are open with our employees, transparent with our customers, and loyal to the communities in which we serve. While Lamar is a large company, each office has its own culture and family atmosphere, making employees feel connected both locally and nationally.

      We are committed to sustainable and environmentally friendly business practices and use a number of innovative strategies to reduce our environmental impact. Please click here to learn more about Lamar's green initiatives.

title: Construction - Billboard Installer
location: Sioux Falls, South Dakota, United States
description:
Would you like to see a different part of your city every day from a bird ’s-eye view? This job is action-packed, and we provide all the training and equipment to start your full-time career. Our Lamar office in Sioux City, South Dakota is now hiring a new Operations crew member to help us bring outdoor advertising campaigns to life for brands in Sioux City, SD and the surrounding areas.

The purpose of this entry-level, full-time position is to install and maintain billboards, including the installation of advertisements, maintenance of structures, and the construction upkeep of billboard cosmetics. This position most often works alone and must be able to manage work schedules effectively.

Why Lamar?

Want a career that takes you above the everyday? As part of Lamar’s billboard construction and operations crew, you’ll experience the city from a bird’s-eye view while building and maintaining the structures that keep communities informed. Join a team that values safety, teamwork, and adventure—every single day. See our operations crew in action over on YouTube.
Lamar is a certified Great Place to Work, with 88% of employees in agreement. Lamar Advertising has also been named as a “Best Company to Work For” in U.S. News & World Report’s annual ranking.
  • Learn more about us on our official YouTube channel.
  • Check reviews and company updates on our Glassdoor page
  • Learn more about our Great Place to Work certification.

      What you can expect from us:

      • A Monday - Thursday, 7:00 am - 5:00 pm work schedule
      • An hourly range of $20- $23/ hour, dependent on relevant experience and qualifications
      • 120 hours of paid time off (PTO) that increases with tenure
      • 12 paid company holidays, including President's Day and Juneteenth
      • A comprehensive 6-week training program
      • Career advancement opportunities
      • Ongoing professional development and internal leadership programs to maximize your career potential
      • Multiple medical plan options and health savings account
      • Hospital, Critical Illness, and Accident coverage
      • Short & long-term disability and paid parental leave
      • Employee Stock Purchase Plan
      • 401k plan with company match
      • Up to $1,200 value in employer-paid HSA contributions and cash rewards for engaging in our wellness program
      • A people-first culture that invests in connection, community involvement, and transparency around employee feedback.

      A Day in the Life:

      As an Installer, you can expect to work alongside the Operations team to install and maintain billboards while prioritizing the safety of yourself and others. Installation most often includes handling a large advertisement printed on vinyl and ensuring it is properly assembled to the billboard structure. The tallest billboard structure in the company is around 200 feet, so comfort with heights is a must.

      Maintenance of our billboards includes construction work such as tightening bolts, painting steel structures, repairing trim and various parts of a billboard sign face and structure, changing light bulbs, and more. As for power/manual tools: you bring the experience, we bring the equipment!

      In this role you'll be expected to:

      • Remove and hang flexes from billboards, remove and hang vinyls, cut and prepare flexes and vinyls for installation, cut, prepare and install copies on Tri-Visions
      • Build and install extensions on billboards, cut brush/weeds, conduct storm damage repairs and minor electrical repairs, and maintain a clean workshop area
      • Use power/manual tools while adhering to safety regulations
      • Attend installer and construction safety meetings as required
      • Maintain operation vehicles; maintain construction tools, equipment, and machinery
      • Take completion photos for proof of performance of installations

      What we're looking for in YOU:

      • Ability to work alone and manage your work schedule effectively
      • Willingness to work at heights up to 100 feet above the ground
      • Strong communication skills. Ability to speak and read English fluently.
      • Willingness to work and get along well with others
      • Basic computer skills, including Internet navigation and Microsoft Word & Excel.
      • Ability to work from ladders and to carry a ladder and/or other tools to the worksite from vehicle.
      • Working knowledge of electrical skills and techniques.
      • Working knowledge of fabrication skills and techniques.
      • Skill in reading technical documents, such as blueprints and diagrams.
      • General knowledge of Lamar, Department of Transportation (DOT), and Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) safety regulations
      • Ability to safely use construction equipment
      • Ability to climb heights and work at heights above ground safely
      • Ability to document installations through photographs and written logs
      • Skill in the practical applications of mathematics, in relation to construction and operations tasks
      • Skill in setting priorities that accurately reflect the relative importance of job responsibilities

      Education and Experience Requirements:

      • A high school diploma or equivalent is required
      • A valid driver’s license is required.
      • Ability to complete OSHA 10-hour Construction course required
      • CDL and Non-CDL licenses are a plus, but not required!
      • Previous experience working at heights up to 200 ft. above ground preferred
      • Construction and/or billboard installation experience is a plus, but not required

      Please note: Upon submitting your application, you will be asked to complete an 8-15 minute personality assessment. This assessment compares your professional soft skills to the skills required for success in this role. Please answer honestly; this is not a test! Not completing this assessment could result in disqualification from consideration for this position.

      Candidates with a disability in need of an accommodation to fulfill our application requirements should email recruiting@lamar.com.

      Physical Demands and Work Environment:

      • The primary work environment for this position is outdoors, requiring the ability to work in adverse weather conditions and climb to heights up to 200 ft.
      • The physical demands for this position include heavy lifting (up to 100 pounds), extensive bending, pushing, reaching, seeing (with a focus on reading, color distinction, acuity, depth perception, and peripheral vision), sitting less than 50% of the time, standing, stooping, talking, turning, walking, driving, and climbing.
      • Nights spent away from home traveling are less than 10%.
      • On-call shifts may be required.

      Who we are:

      Founded in 1902, Lamar Advertising Company is one of the largest outdoor advertising companies in the world. With over 360,000 displays across the United States and Canada, Lamar is dedicated to helping both local businesses and national brands reach broad audiences every day.

      We provide ad space through:

      • Billboards
      • Interstate logos
      • Handpainted murals
      • Transportation and airports
      • The largest network of digital billboards in the United States

      We live by the Golden Rule, and we operate with honesty and integrity in every aspect of our business. We are open with our employees, transparent with our customers, and loyal to the communities in which we serve. While Lamar is a large company, each office has its own culture and family atmosphere, making employees feel connected both locally and nationally.

      We are committed to sustainable and environmentally friendly business practices and use a number of innovative strategies to reduce our environmental impact. Please click here to learn more about Lamar's green initiatives.

title: Senior Engineer
description:
Schnabel is an employee-owned, professional engineering and consulting firm that focuses on solving problems related to the earth and environment through specialization in geotechnical, geostructural, tunnel, and dam engineering. Schnabel’s high standards for quality, business ethics, and concern for the communities in which we live are a vital part of who we are. Schnabel is an ENR Top 500 Design Firm with 700+ employees in over 32 offices throughout the United States.

Recognized by CE News as one of the Best Engineering Firms to Work for, Schnabel provides employees with a competitive benefits package including maternity leave, tuition reimbursement for continuing education, health, dental, life and disability insurance and a wellness program. As an employee-owned company, through the Employee Stock Ownership Plan, Schnabel employees directly benefit from the success of our growing firm.

Benefit options include:

  • Medical insurance
  • Dental insurance
  • Flexible spending accounts
  • Employee life & ADD insurance (100% company-paid)
  • Short-term disability (100% company-paid)
  • Long-term disability
  • Supplemental life insurance
  • 401(k) and profit-sharing plan
  • Employee stock ownership plan (ESOP)
  • Bonus program
  • Paid time off
  • 9 Paid Holidays
  • Wellness program
  • Professional development and tuition reimbursement

Job Description:

Our Honolulu, Hawaii office is seeking a Senior Engineer to support our tunnel, geotechnical, and dam engineering group which will help expand our growing presence in the Pacific island region. In this role, you will provide technical support and leadership for a variety of multidisciplinary teams to deliver infrastructure projects in this region and across the country for other Schnabel offices based on workload balance and resource availability. As an employee-owner, you will have a say in how our business operates and will benefit from our financial success through the allocation of company stock. This role will primarily support projects in Hawaii. Periodic travel will be required.

Job Responsibilities:

  • Analyze and design components of challenging multidisciplinary infrastructure projects. Experience in the design of underground structures (tunnels, shafts, stations, etc.), trenchless, pipelines, reinforced concrete, geotechnical investigations and evaluation, hydrological analyses, slope stability, or retaining walls preferred.
  • Develop engineering recommendations and write technical reports.
  • Assist project managers with project coordination and administrative tasks.
  • Manage multidisciplinary infrastructure projects through concept, investigation, design, and construction phases including budget, schedule, coordination, and task scope.
  • Collaborate with and lead multidiscipline teams through the design process.
  • Manage, execute, and provide technical support, in a team setting and on a variety of challenging infrastructure projects.
  • Manage the preparation of calculations and design reports, plans, specifications, technical memorandums, and other project contract documents.
  • Communicate effectively with clients, business partners, subconsultants, and Schnabel team members.
  • Perform management duties related to obtaining signed contracts, verification of time sheets, reviewing and approving invoices, developing, and tracking project schedules and budgets for subconsultants.
  • Work as a team member across Schnabel offices to effectively balance workload among available resources.
  • Develop proposals for new work including scope of work, fee estimates, and client coordination.
  • Support marketing and business development across the country.
  • Manage and mentor junior engineers, commensurate with experience level.
  • Participate in the development of a cohesive, positive culture company-wide to cultivate a best-in-class environment that allows our people to realize their full potential.
  • Develop and maintain client relationships, contribute to project meetings, and apply sound engineering judgment to deliver practical, innovative solutions for complex infrastructure projects.

Required Skills/Experience:

  • A Bachelor's degree in Civil engineering from an ABET-accredited institution
  • 8+ years of design- and/or construction-oriented consulting engineering experience
  • A Professional Engineering license or the ability to obtain one within 6 months of hire
  • Project management experience
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills
  • Attention to detail and well organized
  • Familiarity with heavy civil construction means and methods
  • Willingness and ability to perform field work and travel
  • Be physically able to navigate construction sites, enter trenches, climb ladders and work outside in various weather conditions.
  • Strong work ethic and the desire to perform professionally at a high level
  • Positive attitude and ability to work as part of a multi-person team

Preferred Skills/Experience:

  • A Master’s degree in Civil, Geotechnical, Structural, or related fields

Other Requirements:

  • Provide a resume and cover letter articulating why you are interested in joining Schnabel and our Honolulu office.
  • Ability to pass a background check which may include criminal history, motor vehicle record, and credit check.
  • Ability to pass a pre-employment employment drug screening.

The compensation range for this position is between $115,000 to $140,000. Compensation for this position may vary based on geographic location and other factors. We remain committed to providing competitive and equitable compensation to all employees, regardless of their location.

SiTime is the Precision Timing company.

Timing is the heartbeat of all electronics, ensuring performance, resilience and scalability. MEMS-based Precision Timing delivers greater accuracy, smaller size and resilience. Today, MEMS timing powers over 400 applications, including high-growth ones in AI datacenters, automated driving, industrial and humanoid robots, wearables and IoT.

title: Behavioral Supports Program Manager
description:
Summary:

The Program Manager is responsible for the oversight, development and routine management of quality psycho-social care to students served in a school setting. This position works with ICAN and the Utica City School District staff to ensure that overall needs of the student client are met. Responsible for leading a team that will work to address the social, emotional and educational needs of students in pursuit of academic success. The Program Manager will promote the philosophy and mission of the agency by performing the following duties.

Duties & Responsibilities:

  • Provides administrative support, supervision and direct oversight of Behavior Specialist(s), Clinical Care Coordinators, and other ICAN staff hired to work within various school-districts across the region. (Time Sheets, Time off requests, Scheduling, etc.)
  • Responsible for monitoring program budget and spend down lines (Supplies, So etc) and all related paperwork.
  • Serves as the program liaison with identified program administration within the school.
  • Provides programmatic support to program staff including but not limited to: crisis debriefing, training, daily support, etc.
  • Provides oversight to ensure consistent application and implementation of established processes for key program elements such as home visitations, medication reviews, CAFAS tracking, etc.
  • Coordinates with school personnel and mental health professionals to assure that the youth’s mental health needs are considered in academic planning.
  • Provides supportive consultation services to school personnel as needed, including, classroom observation, peer mediation, school wide events, etc.
  • Assists team members in providing outreach to engage students and assist families with an understanding of program philosophy and policies.
  • Assists team members to help link clients and their families to appropriate resources and services in a timely and coordinated manner.
  • Completes all required documentation in a comprehensive and timely manner as required by ICAN and/or School Districts.
  • Maintains statistics for analysis and reporting purposes.
  • Other duties may be assigned, on an as-needed basis.

Education/Experience:

  • Master's degree in Social Work, Mental Health Counseling or related field preferred. ∙ NYS
  • Professional License in area of study preferred or must be license eligible upon hire. ∙ At least
  • 1-3 years of experience as a supervisor/manager preferred.
  • Candidates must have thorough knowledge of services provided, well developed advocacy skills, and a knowledge and understanding of educational supports.
  • Experience working with students with severe emotional and behavioral problems required.

title: Director, Customer Journey & Audience Design
description:

Customer Journey Strategy & Experience Design

  • Develop and evolve the end-to-end customer journey across all audiences, touchpoints, and channels—from acquisition through retention, loyalty, and advocacy
  • Develop and implement integrated journey frameworks and lifecycle strategies aligned to organizational goals
  • Map and optimize key audience journeys, identifying friction points and opportunities to improve conversion, engagement, and satisfaction
  • Lead cross-channel planning to align messaging, cadence, and experiences over a 12-month roadmap

Audience Insights & Data-Driven Strategy

  • Lead the development of a best-in-class audience insights function, behavioral data, and advanced analytics
  • Translate complex data into actionable insights that inform strategy, segmentation, and decision-making
  • Develop audience segmentation, personas, and lifecycle models to personalize engagement at scale
  • Design and oversee the governance of audiences across campaigns and brands

Voice Of The Customer & Experience Advocacy

  • Serve as the enterprise customer advocate, ensuring decisions are grounded in audience needs and behaviors
  • Establish mechanisms (research, feedback loops, satisfaction measurement) to continuously capture and act on audience voice
  • Identify and address pain points across the customer experience, driving continuous improvement

Cross-Functional Leadership & Operating Model

  • Partner across Marketing, Product and Analytics to align strategies, priorities, and execution
  • Shape and evolve the operating model to enable a more agile, insight-driven marketing organization
  • Collaborate with Customer Relationship Management, analytics, and technology teams to advance data infrastructure and marketing capabilities
  • Lead agency and vendor relationships to support integrated execution and innovation

Team Leadership & Capability Building

  • Lead a high-performing, multidisciplinary team spanning journey strategy, lifecycle marketing, and insights
  • Develop talent, foster innovation, and instill a culture of experimentation and continuous learning
  • Establish scalable processes, governance, and best practices for journey orchestration and insights activation

Note: This job description is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or activities required of the role. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the position.

title: CNC Lathe Programmer
description:
If you’re a lathe programmer who enjoys figuring out how to make difficult parts, this is the kind of role that gives you that opportunity.

We’re hiring an experienced CNC Lathe Programmer for a high-end precision manufacturer producing specialty, tight-tolerance components for aerospace and defense programs.

A major part of this position is NPI and new job development. You won't spend your day maintaining the same production programs. You'll regularly be handed new, challenging parts and have the freedom to determine how they should actually be machined.

Why This Role Is Different:

  • Heavy focus on NPI and new programs
  • Complex aerospace & defense components
  • High-mix, specialty machining instead of repetitive production
  • Opportunity to own the entire machining process
  • Challenging tight-tolerance and GD&T-heavy work
  • Work directly with engineering, quality, and experienced machinists
  • Up to $50/hr + overtime (10 hours/week)
  • Take home pay up to $140k+
  • Strong company-paid benefits

What You'll Own:

You'll develop CNC lathe programs in Mastercam and determine the best way to manufacture new components from the ground up.

That includes:

  • Programming complex CNC turning operations
  • Developing machining strategies from CAD models and prints
  • Selecting tooling, inserts, speeds, and feeds
  • Developing workholding and setup strategies
  • Programming OD/ID turning, boring, threading, grooving, drilling, and other complex features
  • Supporting setups and hands-on program prove-outs
  • Working through first articles and dimensional issues
  • Troubleshooting tooling, workholding, and machining problems
  • Optimizing programs for cycle time, tool life, quality, and process stability

Requirements

We're looking for someone who has actually built CNC lathe programs from scratch and understands machining beyond the CAM software.

Strong candidates will have:

  • CNC lathe/turning programming experience
  • Mastercam programming experience
  • Experience with NPI or new job development
  • Strong knowledge of tooling, workholding, speeds, and feeds
  • Strong blueprint and GD&T knowledge
  • Experience with tight-tolerance precision machining
  • Ability to support programs through setup, prove-out, and first article

Experience in aerospace, defense, medical, or other high-precision machining environments is highly valued.

Benefits

  • 90% of employee medical premiums covered
  • 100% of eligible deductibles covered
  • Company-paid dental and vision
  • Company-paid short-term and long-term disability
  • Company-paid life insurance
  • Overtime opportunities

Audit Support & Reporting

title: Corporate Director, F&B Development
description:
Proper Hospitality is seeking a Corporate Director, F&B Development to lead the concepting, design development, technical planning, and commercial structuring of food and beverage experiences across our growing portfolio of hotels, resorts, residences, and clubs. Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, this role will translate ambitious F&B concepts into thoughtfully designed, financially sound, and operationally executable businesses.

Position Overview
The Corporate Director, F&B Development will concept and reconcept F&B across the portfolio, carry those concepts through design and technical development to approved plans and specified equipment, and shape partner deals so that what gets signed can actually be operated. The seat carries no operating P&L on purpose, which is what allows it to underwrite partner economics independently of the team that will run the outlet.

Responsibilities

Concepting and Reconcepting

  • Develop F&B concepts for new properties and new outlets
  • Reconcept underperforming existing outlets, including positioning, format, service model, and daypart strategy
  • Build the concept narrative and positioning that carries through design, brand, and PR

Design and Consultant Coordination

  • Work closely with the VP of Design on layout, kitchen and bar design, back of house adjacency, and buildout
  • Serve as the F&B point of contact for the kitchen consultant, OS&E consultant, and specialty consultants including acoustics, lighting, AV, and MEP where F&B is affected
  • Translate concept and service model into the operating requirements consultants design against: production volume, menu format, service sequence, storage and receiving, waste flow, and staffing positions
  • Review and comment on kitchen and bar drawings at each milestone, and hold consultants to the operating program
  • Own the F&B design intent through plan approval

Equipment and OS&E

  • Drive F&B equipment specification with the kitchen consultant, including make, model, capacity, utility requirements, and lifecycle cost
  • Review and approve F&B OS&E specifications and quantities against the concept and cover assumptions
  • Validate specification against the F&B equipment and OS&E budget, and flag variance early rather than at buyout
  • Coordinate with the purchasing agent and procurement on F&B packages, including long lead items and delivery sequencing against the construction schedule
  • Verify installed equipment against specification at turnover, and log punch items

Plan Review and Pre Opening

  • Lead F&B plan review at each design milestone
  • Build the operating assumptions behind each concept: labor model, cover assumptions, average check, cost of goods targets
  • Deliver F&B pre opening design and technical workstreams through plan approval and equipment turnover, then hand to Openings and Transitions

Partner Deal Shaping

  • Shape partner operator and licensing structures, including fee structure, term, exclusivity, non compete, and IP treatment
  • Build and stress test pro formas, including a Proper operated counterfactual on every partner deal
  • Present recommendations with the operating case and the risk case stated separately

Decision Rights

  • Decides: Concept direction, narrative and positioning, F&B design intent through plan approval, the operating program consultants design against, F&B equipment specification recommendations, pro forma methodology and assumptions.
  • Requires Approval: No concept or partner term sheet advances to LOI without written sign off from the Senior Corporate Director, F&B on labor model, pro forma assumptions, and opening staffing plan. Equipment and OS&E specification requires sign off from the Corporate Director, Culinary on kitchen equipment and the Corporate Director, Beverage on bar equipment, since they own the SOPs those specs have to support.
  • Budget: Specifies within the approved F&B equipment and OS&E budget. Overage requires COO approval.
  • Handoff: At plan approval and equipment turnover, execution and opening staffing transfer to Corporate Director, Openings and Transitions. Development stays available as a consulting resource, not as an owner.
  • Escalation: Unresolved disagreements with the VP of Design or a consultant escalate to the COO.

Year One Measures

  • Concepts delivered on schedule for the active pipeline, including Lake Tahoe, Shelborne, Montauk Yacht Club, Avalon, and Cal Neva
  • F&B plans approved on the construction schedule with no F&B driven delay to permit or buyout
  • Equipment and OS&E specified within budget, with variance flagged before buyout rather than at it
  • No F&B equipment change orders traceable to an operating requirement that was known at design
  • Every partner deal presented with a Proper operated counterfactual, not only the partner case
  • Pro forma assumptions on approved concepts tracking within a defined tolerance against actuals at ninety days post opening
  • Clean handoff to Openings at plan approval on every project, with no duplicated pre opening ownership

Qualifications

  • Eight or more years across F&B concept development and hotel or restaurant operations, with real operating time; pure agency or pure design backgrounds do not fit this seat
  • Has opened multiple F&B outlets from concept through opening, including at least two ground up or full renovation projects
  • Has managed kitchen consultants and OS&E consultants directly, and can hold them accountable to a program
  • Reads and redlines architectural, kitchen, and MEP drawings competently
  • Working knowledge of commercial kitchen and bar equipment, utility requirements, and health department and code requirements across multiple jurisdictions
  • Has run an F&B equipment and OS&E budget through specification, buyout, and installation
  • Has negotiated or structured operator, licensing, or management agreements, and can defend a pro forma line by line
  • Comfortable being the only person in the room arguing against a deal that is popular

Salary

  • $175,000-225,000 base

Proper Perks & Benefits

Culture of Growth & Belonging

  • Culture of Growth: A collaborative, design-forward environment that values creativity, intelligence, and curiosity — where learning and excellence are a daily practice.
  • Guided Skills Development: Access to training, leadership programs, mentorship, and cross-property mobility to encourage achievement and discovery.
  • Diversity, Equity, Inclusion & Belonging: We honor individuality while fostering a culture of respect and belonging across all teams.
  • Community Engagement: Opportunities to give back through local volunteerism, sustainability, and charitable partnerships.

Health & Wellness

  • Comprehensive Health Coverage: Medical, dental, and vision plans through Aetna, designed to fit a range of personal and family needs.
  • Wellness Access: Company-subsidized memberships with Equinox and ClassPass, plus wellbeing workshops and mental health resources.
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP): Confidential support for emotional wellbeing, financial planning, and life management through Unum.

Time Off & Flexibility

  • Paid Time Off: Flexible PTO plus 11 paid holidays each year for corporate team members.
  • Paid Parental Leave: Paid time off for eligible employees welcoming a new child through birth, adoption, or foster placement.
  • Flexible Work Practices: Hybrid schedules for eligible roles and an emphasis on work-life balance.

Financial Wellbeing & Core Protections

  • 401(k) Program: Company match of 50% of employee deferrals, up to the first 4% of eligible compensation.
  • Employer-Paid Life & Disability Insurance: Core protections with optional additional coverage.
  • Financial Education: Access to planning tools and workshops to support long-term stability and growth.

Lifestyle & Travel Perks

  • Hotel Stay Benefits: 75% off BAR (floor of $100) across the Proper portfolio.
  • Design Hotels Partnership: 50% off participating Marriott Design Hotels.
  • Dining Discounts: 75% off food & beverage at all Proper Hospitality outlets.
  • Lifestyle Perks: Complimentary or subsidized parking, cell phone reimbursement, and exclusive hospitality and retail discounts.

Why Join Proper Hospitality
At Proper, we build experiences that move people — and that begins with the team behind them. As a best-in-class employer, we’re committed to creating one of the Best Places to Work in hospitality by nurturing a culture where creativity, excellence, and humanity thrive together.

Everything we do is grounded in the belief that hospitality is more than a profession - it’s an opportunity to care for others and make lives better. Guided by the Pillars of Proper, we show up with warmth and authenticity (Care Proper), strive for excellence in everything we do (Achieve Proper), think creatively and resourcefully (Imagine Proper), and take pride in the style and culture that make us who we are (Present Proper).

We believe our people are our greatest strength, and we invest deeply in their wellbeing, growth, and sense of belonging. From comprehensive benefits to meaningful development programs, Proper is designed to help you build a career, and a life, that feels as inspiring as the experiences we create for our guests.

Our Commitment: Building the Best Place to Work
Our Best Place to Work initiative is a living commitment — a continuous investment in our people, our culture, and our purpose. We listen, learn, and evolve together to create an environment where everyone feels empowered to imagine boldly, achieve confidently, care deeply, and present themselves authentically.

At Proper, joining the team means more than finding a job — it means joining a community that believes in building beautiful experiences together, for our guests and for one another.

WE'LL TRAIN YOU!

12 Hr Shift / 6A-6P

title: Market Research Analyst
description:
This is a technical, behind-the-scenes role responsible for supporting the execution and quality of the organization's quantitative research.

You will work across studies to ensure surveys are programmed correctly, data is clean and accurate, and reporting outputs are client-ready. This includes program checking, data scanning and cleaning, data processing, report population, and rigorous numerical QC.

This is an ideal role for someone who enjoys the technical and operational side of quantitative research, has exceptional attention to detail, and naturally notices when something in the data doesn’t look right.

Duties and Responsibilities

Survey Programming & QA

  • Review programmed surveys against questionnaires for accuracy and consistency
  • Test survey logic, skips, piping, randomization, quotas, calculations, and respondent flow
  • Conduct soft-launch data checks and identify potential programming or fieldwork issues
  • Partner with researchers and programming vendors to troubleshoot and resolve issues

Data Quality & Processing

  • Scan and clean respondent-level data throughout fieldwork and at study close
  • Identify poor-quality respondents, inconsistent responses, suspicious open ends, speeders, straightliners, and other data-quality concerns
  • Investigate unexpected data patterns and troubleshoot potential programming, sampling, or data-processing issues
  • Support recodes, derived variables, banners, crosstabs, weighting, and significance testing
  • Review data tables and other outputs for accuracy and consistency

Reporting & Analysis Support

  • Populate PowerPoint reports with survey data, including charts and tables
  • Check bases, percentages, significance, calculations, and data labels
  • Conduct rigorous numerical QC of client deliverables
  • Troubleshoot discrepancies across raw data, tables, and reporting outputs
  • Prepare clean, analysis-ready data and outputs for research teams

Operational Excellence

  • Serve as a centralized resource for quantitative research quality and technical execution
  • Develop and improve standardized processes for program checking, data cleaning, reporting, and QC
  • Identify opportunities to automate or streamline repetitive quantitative workflows
  • Learn and leverage AI-powered tools and platforms to improve efficiency and quality

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree (market research, psychology, sociology, business, communications, or related field preferred)
  • 0–2 years of experience (internships count)
  • High attention to detail
  • Strong analytical and writing skills
  • Proficiency in Excel and PowerPoint (experience with survey or analytics tools a plus)
  • Ability to manage multiple deadlines in a remote environment

  • Dedicated coaches offer an extra channel of support and skill-building

title: Registry Coordinator
description:
A Day in the life

Your day begins by reviewing clinical registry submissions and monitoring data collection activities for orthopedic, neurosurgical, and bariatric service lines. You ensure registry information is complete, accurate, and submitted within required deadlines, helping support quality reporting, accreditation standards, and regulatory compliance. Throughout the day, you work within multiple databases and the electronic medical record to abstract, validate, and analyze patient care data, ensuring valuable clinical insights are captured and reported accurately.

As a Registry Coordinator, you play a key role in quality improvement initiatives. You analyze trends and outcomes, identify opportunities for performance improvement, and develop reports, dashboards, and scorecards that help physicians, leaders, and clinical teams make informed decisions. Your ability to translate complex data into meaningful information supports improved patient care and service line excellence.

Throughout the day, you collaborate with providers, nurses, department leaders, and multidisciplinary teams to promote accurate clinical documentation and adherence to registry standards. You provide education on documentation requirements, quality measures, and performance metrics while supporting evidence-based clinical practices across the organization.

Quality, compliance, and confidentiality guide everything you do. You maintain HIPAA compliance, prepare for audits and accreditation reviews, and ensure all registry activities align with established specifications and reporting requirements. Whether working independently on data analysis projects or partnering with teams to improve outcomes, you bring strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and a commitment to advancing quality patient care. At the end of the day, you know your work contributes directly to improving healthcare outcomes for the patients and communities we serve.

Qualifications

Education

  • High school diploma or GED required.
  • Associate degree or certification in a healthcare-related field preferred.

Experience

  • Knowledge of medical terminology highly preferred.
  • Expertise in database management preferred.
  • Three to five years of clinical healthcare experience required.
  • Registry abstraction and quality improvement experience preferred.
  • Knowledge of orthopedic, neurosurgical, or bariatric patient populations preferred.

Why Join Regional West?

  • Mission-driven organization focused on quality patient care.
  • Opportunity to directly influence patient outcomes through quality improvement and clinical reporting.
  • Collaborative work environment partnering with physicians, nursing leaders, and multidisciplinary teams.
  • Commitment to professional growth and staff development. Tuition assistance is available after six months of employment.
  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage with benefits beginning the first of the month following 30 days of employment.
  • Generous 401(k) employer match.

Kooth is on a mission to remove the barriers that prevent people from accessing the mental health support they need. title: Claims Specialist
description:
We are looking for a Claims Specialist to join our team and help our business continue to grow.

Job Description:

The Claims Specialist is responsible for accurately processing medical insurance claims, ensuring compliance with industry regulations and guidelines, and resolving any claim-related issues. The Claims Specialist will be a detail-oriented individual who will be responsible for preparing claim forms, verifying information, and corresponding with agents and beneficiaries. Will also handle client inquiries, review policies, determine coverage, calculate claim amounts, and process payments. To be successful as a claim processor, you should have excellent organizational and interpersonal skills. This role requires a strong attention to detail, excellent organizational skills, and a solid understanding of medical billing procedures and insurance policies.

Primary Responsibilities:

· Claims Processing: Review and process medical insurance claims accurately and efficiently, ensuring all necessary information is complete and accurate.

· Coding and Documentation: Ensure proper coding of medical procedures and diagnoses using appropriate coding systems (e.g., ICD-10, CPT) to facilitate accurate claims processing.

· Verification: Verify patient insurance information, including eligibility, coverage, and benefits, before processing claims.

· Documentation Review: Review medical records and documentation to ensure that claims are supported by appropriate and valid documentation.

· Claim Status Follow-Up: Communicate with insurance companies and healthcare providers to follow up on the status of claims, resolve claim discrepancies, and provide necessary information for claim processing.

· Denials and Appeals: Investigate and resolve claim denials by identifying discrepancies, addressing coding or billing errors, and preparing appeals when necessary.

· Billing Accuracy: Review and reconcile billing statements to ensure accuracy in charges and payments.

· Regulatory Compliance: Stay updated on relevant industry regulations, insurance policies, and coding guidelines to ensure claims processing follows legal and regulatory requirements.

· Customer Service: Provide excellent customer service to healthcare providers and insurance companies by addressing inquiries and concerns related to claims processing.



Requirements

Skills & Qualifications:

· High school diploma or equivalent; healthcare administration, medical billing, or a related field (or equivalent experience) is a plus.

· Proficiency in medical billing software and electronic health record (EHR) systems.

· Knowledge of medical coding systems (ICD-10, CPT, HCPCS) and insurance claim submission processes.

· Strong attention to detail and accuracy in claims processing.

· Excellent communication and interpersonal skills for effective collaboration with team members, healthcare professionals, and insurance representatives.

· Problem-solving skills to resolve claim discrepancies and denials.

· Knowledge of insurance regulations and compliance standards in the healthcare industry.

· Ability to work independently and manage a high volume of claims efficiently.

· Familiarity with medical terminology and healthcare documentation.

· Computer literate and proficient in MS Office.

· Excellent critical thinking and decision-making skills.

· Strong customer service skills.


Experience:

Previous experience in medical billing, claims processing, or a related role is preferred. Familiarity with insurance policies and reimbursement procedures is an asset.



Benefits

Benefits:

· 401(k)

· 401(k) matching

· Dental insurance

· Health insurance

· Life insurance

· Paid time off

· Vision insurance

title: Director of Software and Electronics Engineering
description:
Director of Software and Electronics Engineering

Location: Coventry, United Kingdom
Employment: Permanent, full-time
Working model: Primarily office-based, with reasonable flexibility
Reporting to: Chief Product Officer, currently the CEO acting
Travel: Approximately quarterly travel to India, with occasional travel to other company locations

Role Overview

The Director of Software and Electronics Engineering will lead the organisation responsible for power electronics, electronic systems, embedded firmware, cloud and server software, web applications, platform engineering, development infrastructure and automated testing.

The Director will turn product strategy into practical engineering plans, production-ready designs and dependable product releases. The role is accountable for engineering leadership, technical quality, delivery schedules, design reviews and the successful introduction of new products into manufacturing.

This is primarily a leadership and management role. The Director must have sufficient technical breadth to assess risks, challenge assumptions and make informed decisions, but is not expected routinely to act as the principal architect, electronics designer or software developer.

Key Responsibilities

Engineering Leadership

Lead Engineering Managers and senior technical leaders.

Establish clear accountability for delivery, technical quality, people management and risk.

Build an effective engineering organisation across the United Kingdom and India.

Develop the management structure, specialist leadership and technical capabilities required for growth.

Recruit, develop and retain strong engineering talent.

Reduce dependence on individual employees and improve succession planning.

Integrated Engineering

Lead the development of power electronics, electronic hardware, embedded firmware, connectivity, cloud services, web applications and platforms infrastructure.

Ensure that electronics, firmware and software are developed as parts of one integrated product system.

Manage dependencies between electronic design, firmware, communications, software services, manufacturing and field support.

Ensure designs address performance, reliability, safety, cybersecurity, component availability, configuration control, manufacturability and testability.

Delivery and Time to Market

Establish realistic engineering plans covering requirements, architecture, design, prototyping, verification, release and introduction to manufacturing.

Meet agreed product-development and new-product-introduction schedules.

Ensure that resources, dependencies, validation activities and manufacturing readiness are included in delivery plans.

Identify risks early and establish clear recovery plans.

Provide accurate and transparent reporting of progress, risks and forecast completion dates.

Coordinate hardware, firmware and software releases for major product launches.

Establish and continuously improve design and development processes that support efficient, high-quality product delivery.

Design Review Process

Own a formal design-review process covering software, electronics and power electronics.

Design reviews will involve the relevant representatives from:

· Product Management;

· Programme Management;

· Advanced Manufacturing;

· Quality Assurance;

· Systems, Mechanical and other engineering disciplines;

· Supply Chain and Operations, where appropriate.

Reviews will take place at defined stages, including:

· Requirements and Concept Review;

· Architecture Review;

· Detailed Design Review;

· Prototype and Design Verification Review;

· Production Readiness Review;

· Final Release Review.

Each review must evaluate requirements, interfaces, technical risks, verification plans, component selection, manufacturability, testability, configuration control and release evidence.

Decisions, actions, owners and deadlines must be documented. Material actions must be closed before the product proceeds to the next approval stage. Unresolved product, schedule, quality or technical issues will be escalated to the Chief Product Officer.

Product Introduction and Manufacturing

Ensure products move efficiently from design through verification and into production.

Work closely with Advanced Manufacturing to establish design-for-manufacture and design-for-test requirements.

Confirm that manufacturing documentation, test equipment, production software, configuration baselines and engineering evidence are complete before production release.

Support prototype and production bring-up.

Manage engineering changes, component lifecycle risks and product obsolescence.

Use manufacturing and field feedback to improve future designs.

Engineering Quality and Release Readiness

Ensure Engineering produces complete, tested and documented release candidates.

Build quality into the engineering process rather than relying on Quality Assurance to identify incomplete work.

Maintain appropriate requirements, testing, design-verification, documentation and configuration-control practices.

Provide traceable evidence for independent Quality Assurance review.

Apply controls appropriate to each product. Physical products require controlled design baselines and production readiness, while cloud services may use automated deployment and progressive release.

Maintain suitable security practices across hardware, firmware, software and development infrastructure.

People and Resource Management

Manage Engineering Managers and senior engineering leaders.

Set objectives and conduct regular performance reviews.

Develop future leaders and address capability gaps or sustained underperformance.

Allocate engineering resources according to agreed product and programme priorities.

Prevent conflicting priorities or informal reassignment of engineering resources.

Plan headcount, recruitment, tools, licences, cloud services, prototypes, training and specialist suppliers within agreed budgets.

Relationship with the Chief Technology Officers

The Director will work closely with the CTO of Engineering and the CTO of Software & Intelligence.

The CTOs provide technical strategy, policies, standards, engineering governance, specialist advice and technical coaching across their respective domains.

The Director remains accountable to the Chief Product Officer for the organisation, resourcing and delivery of the Software and Electronics Engineering function. Where CTO-led technical work requires engineering effort, the Director will ensure that it is appropriately planned, prioritised and resourced alongside direct product work.

The Director and CTOs will collaborate on significant technical decisions, capability development and cross-product engineering issues. Material disagreements on technical direction, standards, risk or priority will be escalated through the Chief Product Officer where required.

Working Relationships

The Director will work closely with the Chief Product Officer, Product Management, Programme Management, Advanced Manufacturing, Quality Assurance, Operations, Supply Chain, Security, the CTO of Engineering, the CTO of Software & Intelligence and other engineering leaders.

Product Management defines customer needs, product priorities and requirements.

Programme Management owns the integrated programme plan and milestones.

Engineering owns the technical solution, development work, verification evidence and engineering readiness.

Quality Assurance provides independent review and confirms whether agreed assurance criteria have been met.

The CTOs provide technical direction and governance; the Director ensures that required engineering work is incorporated into plans and delivered.

The Director will also work closely with the Director of Electrical Machines as an equal partner in the development and application of coherent engineering processes across Product Engineering.

Decision Authority

Within agreed company plans, budgets, technical policies and engineering standards, the Director will have authority to:

· lead and organise the Software and Electronics Engineering function;

· allocate engineering resources;

· establish engineering and new-product-introduction practices;

· approve routine technical and delivery decisions;

· recruit within approved plans;

· manage performance and recommend promotions;

· establish teams and specialist leadership roles;

· select appropriate engineering methods and development tools.

Long-term product direction, company technology strategy and material departures from established technical policies or standards require appropriate executive approval.

Measures of Success

Success in the role will include:

· Engineering Managers operating with clear authority and accountability;

· UK and India teams functioning as one engineering organisation;

· regular direct engagement with the India-based Electronics Engineering and Computer Science teams;

· effective collaboration with Product Management in reviewing Market Requirements and Product Requirements;

· power electronics, electronics, firmware and software teams delivering integrated products to agreed schedules;

· formal cross-functional design reviews operating consistently;

· improved schedule forecasting, risk visibility and on-time delivery;

· faster and more dependable introduction of new products into Manufacturing, Customer Support and Quality Assurance;

· products reaching Quality Assurance complete, documented and ready for independent review;

· appropriate reliability and MTBF goals being established with Product Management;

· a scalable organisation with clear leadership, responsibilities and career development;

· reduced dependence on executive intervention in routine engineering decisions.

Candidate Profile

The successful candidate will have:

· significant engineering and engineering-leadership experience, with a record of dependable delivery;

· experience managing Engineering Managers or senior technical leaders;

· a record of scaling or restructuring a multi-team engineering organisation;

· leadership experience covering physical products, electronics and software;

· practical knowledge of power electronics, PCB development, hardware and firmware integration, prototyping, verification, EMC and EMI, manufacturing release and configuration control;

· strong technical judgement and the ability to assess evidence, challenge assumptions and involve specialists when required;

· experience leading geographically distributed teams;

· the willingness and ability to travel regularly to India.

Experience with connected devices, embedded-to-cloud products, motor control, propulsion systems, telemetry, cloud platforms, automated testing, aerospace, defence, automotive, robotics or industrial systems would be valuable.

title: HARP Program Manager
description:
Summary:

The HARP (Health and Recovery Plan) Program Manager is responsible for the overall daily operations, development, and quality oversight of the HARP program, including Community Oriented Recovery and Empowerment (CORE) Services. The Program Manager ensures that program operations are consistent with the agency’s mission, vision, policies, quality standards, and applicable New York State Office of Mental Health (OMH) requirements. The Program Manager provides leadership and supervision to program staff, including recruitment, training, scheduling, performance management, and ongoing professional development.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

Administrative and Program Operations

  • Oversee the daily operations and overall functioning of the HARP/CORE program.
  • Provide program information, data, reports, and operational updates to the Director and Executive Leadership as requested.
  • Attend monthly OMH meetings and other required regulatory or program-related meetings.
  • Maintain current knowledge of OMH regulations, CORE requirements, program standards, and regulatory changes.
  • Monitor program performance and budget in collaboration with the Director of Managed Care Services.

Provider Relations and Support

  • Support providers with Electronic Health Record (EHR) access and system-related issues.
  • Provide guidance and consultation to providers regarding service planning, goal development, and documentation requirements.
  • Consult with providers regarding client needs, concerns, barriers to service, and other program-related issues.
  • Oversee the assignment and distribution of client cases to appropriate CORE providers.
  • Facilitate provider meetings focused on education, communication, problem-solving, and ongoing support.

Managed Care Organization (MCO) Relations

  • Attend MCO-led meetings and participate in required program and operational discussions.
  • Develop and maintain positive, collaborative working relationships with MCO representatives.

Staff Supervision and Management

  • Provide daily supervision and oversight of CORE Specialists and Peer Support Providers.
  • Provide direction, coaching, and redirection as necessary to ensure effective job performance and adherence to program expectations.
  • Oversee staff scheduling and coverage to ensure continuity of services.
  • Review and approve time sheets and time-off requests.
  • Monitor staff attendance, performance, productivity, and compliance with program requirements.
  • Participate in the recruitment, interviewing, hiring, onboarding, and training of program staff.
  • Identify training needs and coordinate or provide ongoing staff education and professional development.
  • Promote a positive, collaborative, and accountable work environment.

Billing and Revenue Functions

  • Collaborate with the Billing Department to support timely, accurate, and compliant billing for CORE services.
  • Conduct final review and approval of provider documentation and service notes.
  • Sign and approve service notes as required.
  • Ensure documentation is complete and billing-ready prior to submission or processing.
  • Monitor documentation and billing processes to identify and address issues that may affect revenue or compliance.

Quality Assurance and Compliance

  • Receive, review, and process referrals for HARP/CORE services and distribute referrals to the appropriate program or provider.
  • Conduct monthly quality assurance reviews of identified program processes and documentation.
  • Monitor compliance with OMH regulations, agency policies, contractual requirements, and CORE program standards.
  • Identify trends, deficiencies, and opportunities for improvement and implement corrective actions as appropriate.

Electronic Health Record (EHR) Management

  • Serve as the program’s EHR super user and maintain current knowledge of system functionality affecting HARP/CORE operations.
  • Provide EHR training, technical guidance, and ongoing support to program staff and providers.
  • Oversee daily EHR functions, including:
  • Entering new clients into the system.
  • Discharging or closing services for former clients.
  • Maintaining accurate client demographics and program information.
  • Reviewing and signing provider documentation.
  • Ensuring required information is complete and accurate.
  • Conduct ongoing reviews to ensure data integrity and accuracy.
  • Identify and resolve EHR-related issues that may affect service delivery, documentation, billing, or compliance.

Education and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Human Services, Behavioral Health, Social Services, or a related field required.
  • Previous supervisory or program management experience preferred.
  • Knowledge of HARP, CORE Services, OMH regulations, and behavioral health service delivery preferred.
