title: Receiving Inspector
description:
JOB PURPOSE
In this role, you will inspect incoming units, review customer documentation, create shop travelers and identify any missing or conflicting information before work is released to Production. This position combines receiving inspection, quality documentation, customer-service coordination and administrative support.
The ideal candidate is highly organized, comfortable reviewing detailed information and able to communicate effectively with Quality, Customer Service, Production and technical personnel.
Key Responsibilities:
• Inspect incoming aircraft panels and components for visible damage.
• Photograph and document the condition of received customer property.
• Review customer purchase orders, repair instructions, part numbers, serial numbers, requested work and special priorities for accuracy and completeness.
• Create and complete shop travelers with customer requirements, aircraft information, condition details and routing instructions.
• Identify modification units and attach applicable drawings, engineering changes or customer-provided instructions.
• Identify potential warranty units and provide available prior repair or teardown information for Quality review.
• Resolve missing or conflicting part numbers, serial numbers, purchase-order information, documentation and customer requirements before releasing work to Production.
• Identify and document applicable repair classifications and certification requirements according to approved procedures.
• Enter or scan received-unit information and maintain complete electronic and hard-copy receiving records.
• Update capability information or route new part numbers for review in accordance with company procedures.
• Mark special shipping containers with the applicable work-order number and document container requirements.
• Communicate receiving discrepancies and documentation concerns to the Chief Inspector, Quality, Customer Service, Production and technical personnel.
• Maintain organized records and assist with related Receiving and Quality administrative work
SAFETY REQUIREMENTS
• Will participate in and support safety initiatives, safe work practices, and compliance.
• Will participate in safety activities, including immediately reporting hazards, unsafe work practices, and accidents/injuries.
• Will follow all safety rules, FAA regulations, PPE compliance, and equipment operation requirements.
WORKING CONDITIONS
Physical Demands: Requires sitting or standing for extended periods of time. Requires frequent walking, bending, and reaching to shoulder level. Requires occasional squatting, lifting, carrying, pushing, or pulling weight up to 20 pounds. Requires repetitive hand movement. Requires eye-hand coordination and manual dexterity. Requires corrected vision and hearing to normal range.
Equipment Operated: Ability to operate office machines and equipment and troubleshoot problems with equipment.
Work Location: Velocity Aerospace – Burbank, CA
Protective Equipment Required: None
Potential Hazards: Exposure to materials identified on Material Safety Data Sheets.
JOB SPECIFICATIONS
Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:
• High school diploma or equivalent.
• One to three years of experience in receiving, inspection, quality administration, repair-order entry, aviation parts, manufacturing or technical customer service.
• Strong attention to detail when reviewing part numbers, serial numbers, purchase orders and customer requirements.
• Ability to follow controlled procedures and complete accurate records.
• Ability to identify visible damage and clearly document findings using written notes and photographs.
• Strong organization, follow-through and ability to manage multiple incoming units and changing priorities.
• Professional written and verbal communication skills.
• Proficiency with Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, scanning and basic work-order or ERP systems.
• Ability to handle customer property and small components carefully while maintaining traceability.
• Relevant education or training may be considered in place of some experience.
Preferred Qualifications:
• Aviation, aerospace, FAA Part 145 or regulated-manufacturing experience.
• Receiving-inspection or quality-inspection experience.
• Experience creating work orders, shop travelers or repair documentation.
• Experience reviewing customer purchase orders, traceability records, warranty information or certification requirements.
• Familiarity with aircraft part numbers, technical drawings, engineering changes or repair classifications.
• Experience handling customer-owned components or property.
Education/Training: Degree or training required for role
Experience: At least 2 years of related experience in aerospace or related field preferred.
Certificates/Licenses: None
Compensation: $18-24 per hour

title: Cell Development Engineer
description:
Your role

Cell Development Engineer is responsible for contributing to the development of advanced Li-metal battery cells, integrating electrochemical design, materials engineering, mechanical design, safety, and failure analysis.

This position plays a vital role in supporting the Cell Design team in all aspects of cell development, from concept definition to validation and qualification, ensuring alignment with customer requirements and company objectives.


Main functions

Electrochemical Design and Materials Engineering:

  • Support the optimization of cell chemistry, electrode formulations, and processing parameters to meet performance targets.
  • Analyze electrochemical data (cycling, rate capability, EIS, DCIR, dQ/dV, GITT etc.) to understand performance and degradation mechanisms.
  • Establish correlation between materials properties, electrode processing, and cell performance.

Mechanical Design and Cell Integration:

  • Support the development of cell designs (e.g., pouch cell drawings and BOMs), including dimensions, tolerances, and stack configuration.
  • Assist in mechanical characterization activities such as cell swelling, pressure optimization and thermal behavior of the cell
  • Collaborate with production team to ensure compatibility of designs with manufacturing processes.
  • Participate in validation activities to ensure proper integration of cells into modules and packs.
  • Conduct and contribute to PFMEA (Process FMEA) and DFMEA (Design FMEA) activities to identify, assess, and mitigate potential risks in cell manufacturing and design.

Cell Safety and Failure Analysis:

  • Assist in defining and evaluating safety aspects of cell design, including materials selection and operating limits.
  • Participate in abuse testing such as thermal stability, nail penetration, external short circuit, and pressure testing.
  • Work closely with the cell design engineer to select the most relevant cells for teardown, investigation failure modes and documentation of findings
  • Support implementation of corrective and preventive actions to improve performance, reliability, and safety.


What we offer

At BasqueVolt, we welcome the best talent from around the world:

  • International Environment: Join a diverse team of young professionals with more than 19 nationalities, fostering a positive intercultural atmosphere.
  • Relocation Package: We assist you in making your move to Spain as smooth as possible, offering support in all immigration and bureaucratic processes (health system, accommodation, bank appointments, traffic license, scholarship, and anything you may need!).
  • Supportive Onboarding: From day one, we will guide you through everything about the company, ensuring seamless integration.
  • Work-life balance: We embrace flexibility, remote work and promote a healthy work-life balance.
  • Summer Schedule: Enjoy reduced hours during the summer and celebrate shorter Fridays throughout the year.
  • Health and Well-being: Enjoy company-paid life insurance, additional health benefits, Spain's free education and healthcare systems and options for exemptions on taxes.
  • Training programs: We encourage employees to keep learning. We offer English and Spanish lessons too.


Interested? Here is our recruitment process

  • Initial Contact: Your first interaction will be with our People team.
  • Technical Interview: Meet the department manager for a technical interview. We aim for a swift process, potentially involving two interviews.

Are you ready to be part of the future of energy storage? Apply now and let's shape the future together at BasqueVolt!



Requirements

Education:

  • Master’s or PhD degree in Engineering or related field. Background in electrochemistry, materials science, or mechanical engineering.

Experience:

  • Cell Development Engineer must have proven track-record of 3–5 years of experience in battery cell development.
  • Previous experience in electrode processing, pouch cell design, failure analysis, and correlation between cell design and electrochemical performance.
  • Hands-on experience in electrode preparation, cell assembly/disassembly, electrochemical testing (cycling, rate, EIS, DCIR, dQ/dV, GITT), and data analysis for coin and pouch cells.
  • Understanding of mechanical aspects of cell design, including swelling behavior, pressure, and structural considerations.
  • Experience with safety testing and basic understanding of cell safety and thermal runaway mechanisms.
  • Familiarity with engineering design tools (e.g., NX, SolidWorks or equivalent) is a plus.

Skills & Languages:

  • Strong technical and analytical skills, and result-oriented mindset.
  • Fluent in English.

title: Electrical BIM Engineer (MCF/ Data Centres)

About the Role:

The Diet Clerk plays a vital role in supporting the dietary services within healthcare or institutional settings by ensuring accurate and efficient management of patient dietary information and meal orders. This position is responsible for maintaining detailed records of dietary restrictions, preferences, and nutritional requirements to facilitate proper meal planning and delivery. The Diet Clerk acts as a liaison between patients, dietary staff, and healthcare providers to ensure that all dietary needs are met in compliance with medical guidelines and organizational policies. Attention to detail and strong organizational skills are essential to manage multiple tasks, including data entry, communication, and coordination of meal services. Ultimately, the Diet Clerk contributes to the overall well-being and satisfaction of patients by supporting the delivery of safe, nutritious, and appropriate meals tailored to individual dietary needs.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • High school diploma or equivalent.
  • Basic computer proficiency, including experience with data entry and common office software.
  • Strong attention to detail and organizational skills.
  • Effective communication skills to interact with patients, healthcare staff, and dietary personnel.
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive patient information in compliance with HIPAA regulations.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Previous experience working in a healthcare or food service environment.
  • Familiarity with dietary terminology and nutritional guidelines.
  • Experience using dietary management or electronic health record (EHR) systems.
  • Customer service experience, particularly in a healthcare setting.
  • Certification in food safety or related training.

Responsibilities:

  • Accurately input and update patient dietary information, including allergies, restrictions, and preferences, into the dietary management system.
  • Coordinate with nursing staff and dietitians to verify and clarify dietary orders and ensure compliance with prescribed nutritional plans.
  • Prepare and distribute meal tickets or labels to kitchen staff based on patient dietary requirements and daily meal schedules.
  • Respond promptly to inquiries from patients, staff, and dietary personnel regarding meal options, substitutions, and special dietary needs.
  • Maintain organized records and documentation related to dietary services, including meal counts, special requests, and inventory tracking.
  • Assist in monitoring food service operations to ensure adherence to health and safety standards and report any discrepancies or concerns.
  • Support the dietary team in administrative tasks such as scheduling, ordering supplies, and compiling reports on dietary service activities.

Skills:

The Diet Clerk utilizes strong organizational and data management skills daily to ensure accurate recording and updating of patient dietary information, which is critical for safe meal preparation and delivery. Effective communication skills are essential for coordinating with healthcare providers, dietary staff, and patients to clarify dietary needs and resolve any issues promptly. Proficiency with computer systems and software enables the Diet Clerk to efficiently manage meal orders, generate reports, and maintain records. Attention to detail ensures that dietary restrictions and preferences are correctly implemented, minimizing the risk of errors that could affect patient health. Additionally, problem-solving skills help the Diet Clerk address unexpected challenges, such as last-minute dietary changes or supply shortages, to maintain smooth dietary service operations.

title: Product Manager Level I
description:
Position Summary


The Product Manager, Data Products owns the strategy, roadmap, and delivery of data and analytics products built on the organization's Snowflake data platform and delivered through Power BI and related reporting tools. This role partners with data engineering, business stakeholders, and analytics teams to define data product requirements, prioritize the backlog, and ensure data products deliver trusted, actionable insights that drive business decisions. The Product Manager serves as the primary link between business needs and the underlying data platform, balancing stakeholder demand with data quality, governance, and platform capacity.



Primary Duties & Responsibilities

Data Product Strategy & Roadmap

  • Define and maintain the product vision and roadmap for assigned data products and analytics platforms.
  • Identify opportunities to deliver new datasets, dashboards, and self-service analytics capabilities.
  • Prioritize backlog items based on business value, data quality, and stakeholder needs.
  • Partner with data engineering and architecture teams to align the roadmap with Snowflake platform capacity and capabilities.

Requirements & Data Modeling Collaboration

  • Translate business requirements into clear data product requirements, user stories, and acceptance criteria.
  • Partner with data engineers to define source-to-target mappings, data models, and transformation logic within Snowflake.
  • Ensure data definitions, business logic, and calculations are documented and consistently applied across reports and dashboards.
  • Validate data outputs for accuracy, completeness, and business relevance prior to release.

Dashboard & Reporting Delivery

  • Own the roadmap and prioritization of Power BI dashboards, reports, and self-service analytics tools.
  • Partner with report developers and business stakeholders to design intuitive, actionable dashboard experiences.
  • Establish and enforce standards for dashboard design, performance, and usability.
  • Coordinate user acceptance testing (UAT) and rollout of new reports and dashboards.

Stakeholder Management

  • Serve as the primary product owner and point of contact for business stakeholders requesting data and analytics capabilities.
  • Facilitate intake, prioritization, and communication of data product requests.
  • Present roadmap updates, data product performance, and adoption metrics to business and technology leadership.
  • Build strong relationships with data engineering, BI development, and business analytics teams.

Data Governance & Quality

  • Partner with data governance and security teams to ensure appropriate access controls, data classification, and compliance requirements are met within Snowflake.
  • Monitor data quality and work with engineering teams to resolve data issues impacting downstream reporting.
  • Support definition and maintenance of a data catalog and business glossary for data products.
  • Promote adoption of governed, trusted data sources over ad hoc reporting.

Adoption & Continuous Improvement

  • Track usage, adoption, and satisfaction metrics for data products and dashboards.
  • Gather stakeholder feedback and incorporate it into future roadmap planning.
  • Identify opportunities to improve platform performance, cost efficiency, and data delivery speed.
  • Champion data literacy and self-service analytics adoption across the organization.

Other

  • Perform other duties as assigned.



Qualifications


  • Required:
  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Data Analytics, Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field.
  • 4+ years of experience in product management, business analysis, or data/analytics roles, including direct experience delivering data or BI products.
  • Hands-on experience working with Snowflake or a comparable cloud data warehouse platform.
  • Hands-on experience building or managing Power BI reports, dashboards, or semantic/data models.
  • Strong SQL skills for data exploration, validation, and requirements definition.
  • Experience translating business requirements into data models, reports, and analytics solutions.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to work across both technical and business audiences.
  • Preferred:
  • Experience with Agile/Scrum product delivery.
  • Power BI or Snowflake certification.

title: Controller
description:
Position Overview:

Under the direction of the Chief Financial Officer, the Controller is responsible for overseeing accounting operations and financial reporting across the organization. The Controller leads the day‑to‑day financial management functions and compliance. The Controller will provide strategic financial insight to support organizational goals.

The ideal candidate is a collaborative and experienced accounting leader who understands the unique financial, reimbursement, operational, and regulatory environment of healthcare and is comfortable balancing strategic oversight with hands-on financial leadership in a non-profit organization.

Essential Responsibilities:

  • Oversee monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements prepared by the Finance team, ensuring accuracy, completeness, and compliance
  • Lead budgeting, forecasting, and long-range financial planning processes in collaboration with the CFO and senior leadership
  • Deliver actionable financial analysis and strategic insights and recommendations to the CFO and executive leadership
  • Develop and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) to assess financial and operational performance
  • Ensure effective internal controls, risk management practices, and regulatory compliance frameworks are in place
  • Oversee cash flow, liquidity, and capital allocation strategies
  • Partner cross-functionally with service lines and operational leaders to support business initiatives, financial discipline, and cost optimization
  • Ensure compliance with all leases, mortgages, contracts and other contractual requirements and covenants including timely monitoring, documentation and communication of financial obligations to the CFO.
  • Assist CFO in financial components of contract negotiations and vendor agreements, optimizing cost structures and mitigating financial risk
  • Provide leadership, mentorship, and strategic direction to the Finance team without direct involvement in routine transactional work
  • Act as primary liaison with auditors and external advisors, overseeing audit readiness and execution, compliance with all tax filing and cost reporting requirements

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance Accounting, or related field (Master’s Degree preferred)
  • CPA certification required
  • 12–15+ years of progressive finance experience, including leadership roles
  • Strong knowledge of financial reporting, forecasting, and analysis
  • Experience overseeing accounting functions through direct reports
  • Healthcare finance experience and knowledge of patient revenue cycles required
  • Advanced proficiency in financial modeling and financial systems
  • Excellent analytical, communication, and presentation skills
  • Demonstrated ability to operate at both strategic and oversight levels

Key Competencies:

  • Strategic thinking and business acumen
  • Ability to delegate effectively while maintaining strong financial oversight
  • Strong problem-solving and decision-making skills
  • Executive presence and ability to influence senior stakeholders
  • High integrity and professional ethics

Work Environment & Expectations:

This role emphasizes strategic leadership and financial oversight. The Controller is expected to maintain a high level of confidentiality, exercise sound judgment, and support organizational priorities in a dynamic environment.

Success Measures:

  • Accuracy and timeliness of financial reporting (through effective oversight)
  • Strength and reliability of financial planning and forecasting
  • Integrity and alignment of revenue data across finance and patient financial services
  • Effectiveness in vendor negotiations and cost management outcomes
  • Strength and stability of banking and financing relationships
  • Audit readiness and compliance outcomes
  • Development and performance of the finance team and functions
  • Contribution to strategic decision-making and organizational growth

Notes:

  • Must pass FBI and/or CORI background check prior to starting employment.
  • This is a full-time, exempt position.
  • This position requires current COVID-19 and season influenza, unless an exemption is granted based on medical or religious grounds.

title: Weld Trainer PM-ELROY
description:
Job Title: Welder Trainer

Revision Date: 11/13/2024
Department: Varies  FLSA: Hourly Non-Exempt

Position Description

At Wabash, Welder Trainers play a vital role in developing the skills and knowledge of both new and existing welders. This position focuses on hands-on instruction, technical coaching, and safety leadership to ensure all welders are trained to meet Wabash’s high standards for quality, safety, and performance.

The Welder Trainer supports the company’s mission by providing structured training on carbon steel, stainless steel, and aluminum welding techniques, guiding welders through qualification testing, and reinforcing best practices in workmanship and productivity.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

- Conduct hands-on training sessions for new hires and current employees on Wabash welding standards, techniques, and safety procedures.
- Evaluate welders’ skills through visual inspection and testing to ensure compliance with company and customer specifications.
- Prepare, administer, and document qualification and certification weld tests as required for various product lines.
- Provide individualized coaching and feedback to welders to improve technique, quality, and efficiency.
- Collaborate with supervisors, coordinators, and the quality team to identify training needs and skill gaps.
- Maintain accurate training records and ensure all employees meet qualification requirements before placement on the production floor.
- Reinforce company safety policies and ensure trainees understand and follow proper PPE and safe work practices.
- Assist in updating training materials, weld procedures, and instructional resources as standards evolve.
- Demonstrate professional conduct and serve as a positive role model for all welders.
- May perform other duties as assigned to support plant operations and workforce development.

Tools & Equipment

- Oxy / Acetylene Torch
- Engineering Prints
- Work Instructions
- Hand Tools and Tape Measure
- Hoist / Crane
- MIG Welder (GMAW – including Pulse Transfer)
- TIG Welder (GTAW)
- Stick Welder (SMAW – limited use)
- Plasma Cutter / Gouging
- Grinder / Sander
- Respirator / ADF or PAPR Hood

Qualifications

- Strong written and verbal communication skills; ability to give clear instruction.
- High School diploma or GED equivalent preferred.
- Excellent interpersonal and leadership skills required.
- Must be able to operate and demonstrate all major welding processes used at Wabash.
- Must be a Level 3 or higher qualified welder with thorough knowledge of company welding standards.
- Ability to read and interpret blueprints, weld symbols, change orders, and SOPs.
- Proficient in basic math and measurements (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, fractions, decimals).
- Strong problem-solving and mentoring abilities.
- Must be able to use or learn required computer applications for training records and documentation.

Knowledge, Training, Skills and/or Experience

Previous experience as a welder, welding instructor, or lead is highly desirable. At Wabash, we provide structured onboarding for new trainers to ensure confidence in both our teaching methods and company standards.

Upon hire, Welder Trainers will complete orientation and specific trainer preparation to become effective technical coaches on the production floor.

Benefits

- Vacation
- Paid Holidays
- Excellent Medical, Dental, and Vision Coverage
- 401(k) with Company Match
- Tuition Reimbursement Program

Working Conditions / Environment

The work environment includes exposure to heat, fumes, moving mechanical parts, and vibration typical of a manufacturing plant. Safety and PPE compliance are critical. The noise level can be high at times, and temperatures may vary.

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

All employees on the production floor must wear required personal protective equipment (PPE).

Physical Demands

As a Welder Trainer, you’ll regularly stand, walk, lean, push, climb, bend, kneel, stoop, and handle welding tools throughout the shift. You must be able to lift and/or carry up to 50 pounds and work in confined spaces when necessary. Strong hand-eye coordination, dexterity, and visual focus are required for weld demonstration and evaluation.

Behavioral Attributes

- Identifies training needs and provides constructive feedback to improve performance.
- Takes initiative, follows through on tasks, and promotes a culture of learning.
- Communicates clearly and confidently with welders and leadership.
- Shares knowledge openly to help others work safer and more efficiently.
- Adapts well to changing production and training priorities.
- Plans and organizes training sessions to meet departmental goals.

Leadership Attributes

- Embrace Diversity and Inclusion – Solicit and respect the input of others, celebrate differences, and strive for transparency and inclusiveness.
- Seek to Listen – Actively listen to reach the best solution and make the strongest decisions.
- Always Learn – Strive to improve; never quit or settle for the status quo.
- Be Authentic – Demonstrate honesty, energy, and grit in everything you do.
- Win Together – Collaborate, seek alignment, and excel at cross-group communication to succeed as one team and One Wabash.

Affirmative Action / EEO Statement

Wabash is committed to providing equal employment opportunity for its associates and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, veteran status, disability, or any other protected status under applicable law.

All employment decisions are based on legitimate, neutral criteria, and all policies are applied equally to similarly situated associates.

Title: Specialist- Reconciliation FLSA Status: Non-Exempt

Location: Production Job Family: Supply Chain

Reports to: Manager- Warehouse/Assistant Manager- DC Career Track/Level: SP2

Job Summary:

Responsible for reconciling inventory within ERP M3, focusing on identifying, analyzing and resolving inventory discrepancies driven by production transactions, process deviation and system activity. Works closely with Inventory and Operations to ensures accurate material usage, movement and aligns physical with M3 records.

Essential Position Functions:

1. Reconcile inventory discrepancies in M3 related to manufacturing, production reporting, and material consumption.

2. Analyze and correct production variances, including yields, scrap, rework, issuing, and backflush errors.

3. Investigate root causes of inventory discrepancies by reviewing production orders, BOMs, and transactions.

4. Partner with Production, day DC Warehouse Inventory, and Receiving Warehouse to resolve discrepancies and maintain inventory accuracy.

5. Ensure accurate and timely processing of production‑related inventory transactions in M3.

6. Support end-of-production-day inventory close by reconciling manufacturing inventory and open production orders.

7. Identify process gaps or system issues impacting inventory accuracy and recommend corrective actions to the appropriate Department and/or Leadership.

8. Maintain reconciliation documentation to support audits and internal controls.

9. Monitor variance trends and escalate recurring or systemic issues to Operations and Business Process teams.

10. Support the month‑end inventory close by reconciling manufacturing inventory and open production orders.

11. Performs special projects and other related duties, as assigned.

Education and Experience:

• High School Diploma / GED

• Some college or Technical Training/Certificate

• 3-5 years’ experience in the food manufacturing environment, warehouse inventory management, manufacturing reconciliation

• ERP experience

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

• Knowledge of production reporting, inventory consumption and its processes

• Proficient in Microsoft Excel (basic formulas, data review and reporting) required.

• Basic PC and 10-key skills are required.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills.

• English/Spanish bilingual is a plus.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills are required.

Physical Demands and Working Conditions:

• Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk working on a computer required while in the office.

• Prolonged periods performing repetitive actions.

• Repetitive hand, wrist, and finger activities.

• Must be able to lift items up to 30 lbs.

• Must wear required food safety items such as smocks, hair nets, beard nets and waterproof boots or shoe covers.

• In areas where hearing protection is required, must be able to wear appropriate hearing protection.

• The environment may be wet or dry, and temperatures may range from 0°F to 110°F.

• Office, production, and warehouse environment.

• Business demands may require overtime and/or evening or weekend scheduling.

Exempt only: This position is eligible for a bonus based on company goals/performance.

title: Field Supervisor
description:
About Us

At American Engineering Testing (AET), we believe that people are the heart of innovation. We create an environment that values teamwork, curiosity, and continuous improvement while delivering innovative engineering and consulting solutions. As a 100% employee-owned firm, we deliver comprehensive testing, analysis, and design to reduce uncertainty in construction projects and offer rewarding work, exceptional training, and career development opportunities.

Job Summary

The Field Supervisor at American Engineering Testing, Inc. (AET) is responsible for overseeing the day-to-day technical operations on projects, ensuring the project is completed safely, on time, and within budget by being the interface between client and technicians acting as a source matter expert when called upon. Will be able to interpret project plans as well as demonstrate exceptional leadership, communication, and problem-solving skills. Direct and oversee staff activities in accordance with the company’s plan. Assist in developing department technical capability and facilitating growth. Assist in the management of department financials. Responsible for providing work direction and daily supervision of assigned department staf


Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Reasonable accommodations or workable solutions may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions.

  • Assign and coordinate daily project schedules for field staff based on workload, testing complexity, certifications, and project scope.
  • Provide technical guidance and quality control on field procedures including soils, concrete, asphalt, aggregate, and specialty materials testing.
  • Perform or assist with complex field investigations, sampling procedures, and test observations.
  • Review and approve field documentation including daily field reports, timesheets, expenses, and mileage logs.
  • Support the use of AET’s systems (e.g., QEST, Dynamics) for accurate project tracking and reporting.
  • Serve as a point of contact for field-level project inquiries, coordinating with project managers and clients to resolve concerns or technical clarifications.
  • Ensure that client specifications, contract requirements, and industry standards (e.g., ASTM, AASHTO, MnDOT) are consistently met on all active job sites.
  • Support the development and delivery of accurate and timely testing results and project documentation.
  • Mentor, coach, and train new and junior technicians in proper field methods, safety procedures, and client interaction.
  • Conduct regular performance check-ins and annual reviews; support employees with development goals and certifications (e.g., ACI, NICET, MnDOT).
  • Help manage field onboarding and certifications tracking, working closely with Department and HR teams.
  • Lead field team meetings or tailgate talks to reinforce safety, project updates, and process improvements.
  • Monitor and support project productivity, technician utilization, and overtime management.
  • Assist with maintaining project and department profitability targets through scheduling, quality, and cost control.
  • Help track prevailing wage compliance, WIP status, and project documentation accuracy in collaboration with project managers.
  • Enforce AET’s health and safety practices on all job sites; conduct spot checks and incident follow-ups as needed.
  • Uphold QA/QC standards through review of field practices, calibrations, and proper documentation.
  • Promote a positive team culture rooted in safety, respect, professionalism, and accountability.

Supervisory Responsibility

  • This position has full day-to-day supervisory responsibility over field staff, including performance management, training, and day-to-day operational oversight.

Required Qualifications and Education Requirements

  • High School Diploma or equivalent required.
  • Minimum 3 years of hands-on experience in construction materials testing or related engineering services.
  • 0–2 years of direct supervisory experience required.
  • Valid driver’s license and acceptable driving record.

Preferred Skills

  • Associate or bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Construction Management, or Geology preferred.
  • Field certifications such as ACI Field Testing Grade I, NICET, or equivalent.
  • Strong working knowledge of field standards and test methods (ASTM, AASHTO).
  • Experience using project tracking systems such as QEST or Microsoft Dynamics.
  • Excellent communication and team leadership skills, with the ability to train and motivate technicians.
  • Proven ability to manage shifting priorities in a high-volume, fast-paced field environment.

Pay Transparency

Base compensation is expected to be in the range of $31.00 and $41.00 per hour based on skill set and experience. AET offers a comprehensive benefits package, including health benefits, insurance, Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP), long term savings, paid time off, and professional development opportunities. The selected candidate must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. without requiring visa sponsorship now or in the future.

Work Environment

This job operates in a professional office environment and in locations that feature rough terrain typical of construction sites and must be able to enter and work in facilities that include limited accessibility, heights, moving machinery, and other conditions typical of industrial facilities.


Physical Demands

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk or hear. The employee frequently is required to stand; walk; use hands or fingers, handle or feel; and reach with hands and arms. The employee is occasionally required to sit; climb or balance, and stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 10 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus


Other Duties

Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties, or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.


Third Party Disclosure

Notice to Third Party Agencies: AET does not accept unsolicited resumes from third party recruiting firms. Absent a signed Service Agreement by AET’s Chief People Officer (CPO), AET reserves the right to pursue and hire these candidates without financial obligation to recruiters or agencies.

title: Water Treatment Tech.-TEC060
description:
Position Summary
This is an entry level position. Under direct supervision, train on and perform a variety of jobs necessary for the operation and maintenance of water treatment plants and appurtenant structures. As a treatment technician, learn to use physical and chemical conventional water treatment techniques to become proficient at providing an adequate supply of safe, high-quality water to the public. As an asset management technician, learn to maintain plant equipment and structures such as chemical feed/storage, piping, valves, basins, and reservoirs.
Supervisory Responsibilities
This position does not have formal supervisory responsibilities over other employees.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities
All Technicians must be able to perform safety sensitive functions; provide appropriate first response to emergencies and spills including those involving hazardous materials, wear respirators including self-contained breathing apparatus as required. They may be required to perform on-call duty, work shifts, weekends, holidays, and overtime as directed, and work outdoors in a variety of weather
conditions. Technicians report to two or more Denver Water treatment plants. All team members perform other duties as assigned and cross train as needed.
Other responsibilities depending on team assignment (T=Treatment and AM = Asset Management) are set forth below:
* T: Learn and become proficient at determining and changing plant flows to meet system demands. Operate necessary computer equipment to coordinate plant operations.
* T: Learn and become proficient at controlling quality and quantity of finished water by regulating filter operations as required. Maintain proper chemical dosages and feed equipment settings for influent and effluent plant flows.
* T: Learn and become proficient at performing laboratory tests on influent and effluent water such as turbidity, alkalinity and hardness, chlorine residual, ammonia residual, fluoride concentration, pH, odor, and coagulant dosage tests. Develop written operating procedures.
* AM: Learn to and become proficient at repairing and maintaining equipment such as pumps, compressors, chemical feed equipment, electric, hydraulic and pneumatic control equipment, chlorinators, valves, and gauges.
* AM: Learn to and become proficient at performing preventative maintenance, installation, fabrication, correction, adjusting plant equipment, and modify existing systems to accommodate plant needs.
* AM: Learn to and become proficient at performing preventative maintenance, installation, fabrication, correction, adjusting plant equipment, and modify existing systems to accommodate plant needs. Equipment encountered includes, but is not limited to, pumps, compressors, chemical feed equipment, electrical, hydraulic and pneumatic control equipment, valves and gauges.
The following disciplines fall under this job description:
Treatment Tech: Under direct supervision, learn and become proficient at performing a variety of duties necessary to the operation of treatment facilities and appurtenant structures. Uses physical, chemical and biological conventional and advanced treatment techniques to provide an adequate supply of safe, high-quality water to the public and other end-users. Performs process control laboratory analyses. Uses SCADA to manage and control operations. Provides routine metrics and data analytics.
Asset Management Tech; Under direct supervision, learn and become proficient at performing a variety of laboring, semi-skilled, and skilled duties related to managing and maintaining assets at treatment plants. Install, maintain, demolish, troubleshoot, and repair mechanical systems throughout the treatment facilities. Install and maintain small process pumps, valves, motors, compressors, piping systems, gauges, pneumatics, hydraulics, and other related systems.

title: Optician
description:
VISION TO LEARN

Optician

Location: Philadelphia, PA

Compensation: $24-$28/HR

Position Title: Optician

Employment type: Full Time + benefits

Vision To Learn seeks compassionate, mission-driven opticians who want to make a tangible impact on children’s lives. As part of a mobile clinical team, you’ll provide high-quality eye screenings and help deliver glasses to students in underserved communities—removing vision barriers that affect learning and long-term opportunities. If you’re motivated by service, inspired by teamwork, and excited to practice opticianry in a meaningful, community-focused setting, Vision To Learn offers a rewarding way to use your skills to change lives.

For more information about career opportunities and to see the impact of our work, please visit our website

Qualified applicants please apply through this direct link or through our website:


About Vision To Learn

Vision To Learn is a nonprofit 501(c)(3) organization providing vision screenings, eye exams, and glasses to K–12 students in underserved communities across the U.S. at no cost to them or their families. Using mobile vision clinics—optometric exam rooms on wheels—we bring essential eye care directly to schools and community centers so every child can see clearly and learn confidently.

Since 2012, Vision To Learn has provided more than 3.8 million vision screenings, 800,000 eye exams, and 650,000 pairs of glasses to children in need across the nation. Our mission is simple: if you can’t see, you can’t learn.

Who We Are

We are friendly, high energy, knowledgeable, and quality-oriented professionals committed to Vision To Learn’s mission. We approach our work with a value system of service excellence, empathy, integrity, open communication, empowerment, and an eagerness to help the communities we serve.

We are looking for an Optician like you to join our team with a positive, proactive attitude, and commitment to our mission.


Position Description

Vision To Learn is currently seeking a qualified candidate for a full-time Philadelphia, PA Optician. Work hours are Monday thru Friday with 2-3 Saturdays per year. The Optician will primarily work during school hours.

Key position responsibilities include

Patient Responsibilities

  • Oversee assigned inside lane eye exams operation. An inside lane is an interior eye exam operation with portable optometric equipment inside of a school or community building with a licensed optometrist. The inside lane may transition to a mobile clinic operation in the future.
  • Oversee assigned mobile eye clinic operation
  • Conduct eye exam pre-tests, maintain optimal professional standards
  • Take measurements, fit and adjust frames for patients according to written optical prescriptions
  • Assist patients with frame selections to ensure optimal fit and patient satisfaction
  • Complete and prepare daily reports, and meet deadlines
  • Make follow-up calls to patient caregivers for feedback
  • Conduct vision screenings using a Welch Allyn Spot Check Vision Screener
  • Dispense glasses to large group of student patients
  • Study and follow Vision To Learn health and safety protocols


Clinic Responsibilities

  • Maintain optimal driver safety standards when driving, parking, and using the vehicle
  • Setup the clinic, monitor and replenish inventory, and ensure all patient and administrative paperwork facilitates an efficient workflow each workday
  • Load, secure, inspect and fuel vehicle as necessary
  • Keep vehicle and internal work areas clean and organized at all times


Inside Lane Responsibilities

  • Transport inside lane eye exam equipment in personal vehicle to and from schools and community organizations.
  • Setup and breakdown the inside lane operation, monitor and replenish inventory, and ensure all patient and administrative paperwork facilitates an efficient workflow each workday.
  • Maintain optimal driving when commuting to and from school and community organizations, in particular with inside lane eye exam equipment.
  • Keep the inside lane operation work areas clean and organized at all times.
  • Operate mobile clinic as needed.

Additional responsibilities as needed


Who You Are

  • Ability to display exceptional interpersonal skills when interacting with children, site contacts, patient families, and in all internal/external work interactions
  • Desire to work in a fast-paced, dynamic environment and have technical skills
  • Desire to be cross trained to expand your skillset
  • Self-starter who is confident to implement Vision To Learn protocols and embrace a remote setting with limited supervision
  • Excellent organizational and prioritization skills
  • Strong interpersonal and written communication skills
  • Able to lift up to 30 lbs. and to exert well-paced mobility for an 8-hour shift including standing, walking, bending and squatting

Qualifications

  • Optician Diploma; Optician Certification (COA, COT, NCLE, and ABO) preferred, but not required
  • Valid driver's license required, with a good driving record and familiarity with greater Philadelphia area geography, including Philadelphia, Delaware, and Chester counties, and with phone GPS; driving transcript must be provided
  • Successful track record of working with children and diverse types of people
  • Must pass company and applicable background checks and drug test
  • Experience using Microsoft Office – Outlook, Excel, Word; ability to quickly learn EHR reporting, and project management systems is a plus
  • Spanish skills a plus


Successful candidates will have a proven track record for patient care, with positive, proactive attitudes who are dedicated to our mission. Vision To Learn is a rapidly growing organization and team players are critical to our collective success.


Vision To Learn is committed to a diverse staff and to a culture that holds equity as a value and a priority. VTL welcomes applicants who bring a variety of perspectives, experiences, and competencies. People of color, women, people with disabilities, and LGBTQIA+ persons are strongly encouraged to apply. title: Transfer Center Specialist
description:
Regional West Medical Center is seeking a detail-oriented and highly organized Transfer Center Specialist to support patient flow through efficient coordination of interfacility transfers. This role serves as the central communication hub between referring providers, transport teams, and hospital departments, ensuring safe, timely, and seamless patient movement.

A Day in the Life of

Your day starts the moment you log in—phones, alerts, and requests are already coming in. As the central hub for patient movement, you quickly begin coordinating incoming and outgoing transfer requests, ensuring every detail is captured and routed efficiently.

Throughout the day, you’re in constant communication with transport teams, including ground EMS and air medical services. You track locations, provide updates, and ensure everyone stays informed as patient needs evolve. At the same time, you’re working behind the scenes to secure and communicate bed assignments, making sure the receiving team is prepared when the patient arrives.

Between calls, you carefully document each transfer interaction in the EHR and transfer systems, maintaining accurate, real-time records that support continuity of care and regulatory compliance.

In critical moments, especially with air transport, you may also review and communicate weather conditions, helping ensure safe travel for both patients and transport crews.

By the end of your shift, you’ve handled dozens of moving pieces—each call, each coordination, each decision contributing to timely care for patients who need it most. And while you may not always see the patients face-to-face, your impact is felt in every safe, successful transfer.

Qualifications

Education

  • High school diploma or equivalent required
  • Preferred: EMT, LPN, or RN education or certification
  • IAMTCS certification preferred

Experience

  • At least 2 years of healthcare experience preferred
  • Familiarity with medical terminology and hospital workflows
  • Experience with phone, radio, or dispatch communication systems preferred
  • Experience with emergency procedures, navigation systems, or aviation support is a plus

Skills

  • Excellent communication and multitasking abilities

You'll work alongside leaders across Operations, Engineering, Quality, Finance, and Program Management while developing a high-performing team that delivers measurable business impact.

About the team

At Novanta Precision Medicine, we're helping shape the future of healthcare. Our cutting-edge photonics, vision, motion control, and automation technologies enable life-changing medical innovations, empowering customers to push the boundaries of what's possible in diagnosis, treatment, and patient care.

  • Partner cross-functionally with Operations, Engineering, Quality, Finance, and Program Management to support new product introductions, cost reduction initiatives, and long-term business objectives.

  • Lead supplier performance management and risk mitigation activities, leveraging market intelligence, analytics, and business insights to drive continuous improvement and operational excellence.

Required Experience, Education, Skills, Training and Competencies

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Supply Chain, Engineering, or a related field required; MBA or advanced degree preferred.

  • 12+ years of progressive leadership experience in supply chain, procurement, strategic sourcing, commodity management, or supplier management within a manufacturing or technology environment.

  • Demonstrated success leading executive-level supplier negotiations, strategic sourcing initiatives, and long-term supplier partnerships that deliver measurable business value.

  • Strong business acumen and analytical capabilities, with expertise in strategic sourcing, commodity management, spend analytics, supplier performance management, and supply risk mitigation.

  • Exceptional communication, relationship-building, and influencing skills, with the ability to engage effectively with stakeholders ranging from individual contributors to executive leadership and supplier C-suite executives.

  • Proven ability to lead, coach, and develop high-performing teams while collaborating across functions to achieve business objectives.

  • Proficiency with ERP and procurement systems, Microsoft Excel, and data-driven decision-making tools.

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to lift and carry light materials, including laptops, documents, and product samples, with or without reasonable accommodation.

title: Franchise Business Consultant - Fargo
description:
Our Story: It's no surprise that our story is a little unconventional. After all, Papa Murphy's brought an entirely new approach to the pizza industry. But our unique idea is a simple one. Position Summary:
As a Franchise Business Consultant (FBC), your primary responsibility is to provide comprehensive guidance and support to franchisees within an assigned area helping promote the successful operation of their businesses and growth of the brand. You will act as the primary liaison between the franchisor and franchisees, working to uphold brand standards and improve operational execution, marketing execution, sales growth, and the profitability of stores. Your role will involve regular travel to various franchise locations, where you will assess performance, offer strategic advice, and facilitate training and development initiatives.
Primary Accountabilities
Franchisee Relationship Management:
- Cultivate and nurture personal relationships with franchisees while aligning with brand and corporate objectives.
- Independently provide comprehensive guidance and expert advice to franchise personnel on revenue generation, cost controls, marketing, purchasing, and compliance.
- Lead the seamless opening of franchise restaurants, offering advisory support and facilitating team implementation from opening plan to grand opening.
Strategic Support and Development:
- Evaluate business organizations within the restaurant industry and recommend best practice procedures and ideas to key stakeholders throughout the system.
- Collaborate with franchisees in developing short- and long-term strategic plans consistent with the brand's goals and financial success.
- Lead franchisees in business growth through evaluation and strategic development recommendations, identifying opportunities and reviewing economic models.
- Review franchisees' economic reports and make key recommendations to the Director of Operations in the development of action plans for cost control areas.
- Maintain regular communication and meetings with the Director of Franchise Operations, providing insights into key issues affecting financial health and operational integrity.
- Improves franchisee capabilities by helping leverage company tools, available resources, and best practices across business functions especially in finance, marketing, and operations.
Leadership:
- Build trust and credibility with supervisors, peers, and franchisees through active participation in round table discussions and workshops.
- Take independent, prompt and appropriate action to address performance issues or conditions in troubled areas, proactively managing decisions that impact the company.
- Effectively prioritize and inform the Director of Franchise Operations of significant issues, recommending potential solutions to challenges as they arise.
Training and Development:
- Develop, coach, and mentor franchisees, assisting in the formulation of action plans for improvement and financial success.
- Affect the formulation of franchisee training programs through strategic insight and advice that aligns with operational needs.
- Ensure the effective implementation of new policies and procedures and evaluate their impact at franchisee locations through regular restaurant visits.
Guest and Associate Relations:
- Help address and resolve guest complaints promptly, ensuring a quality brand experience.
- Interact with guests as needed to answer questions and alleviate concerns, maintaining high standards of customer service.
Auditing:
- Ensure adherence to all Standard Operating Procedures and conduct audits, including relating to food safety, to maintain operational excellence.
- Complete and review Brand Standard Assessments with franchisees and operators, utilizing them as tools for operational improvement and development.
Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities:
- Education: This position requires college degree or equivalent combination of education and experience.
- Experience: A minimum of 5 years' experience in QSR environment.
- Skills/Competencies/Certifications:
- ServSafe certification required.
- Exhibit a strong sense of initiative and the ability to work unsupervised, while troubleshooting and problem solving with an entrepreneurial spirit.
- Fully understands key performance drivers of restaurant businesses.
- Flexible thinker capable of addressing diverse restaurant issues.
- Strong business acumen with demonstrated knowledge of maximizing unit level economics.
- Excellent communication and relationship building skills.
- Ability to lead, influence and develop organizational capability as well as achieve results with a diverse group of stakeholders.
- Microsoft Office Skills: Outlook, PowerPoint, Word and Excel.
- Familiarity with Tableau, and a deep knowledge of restaurant Point of Sale systems preferred.
- Experience working with franchisees or in a franchised organization is preferred.

Other Requirements:
- Ability to travel a minimum of 75% with overnight stays required.
- Valid Driver's license.
- Ability to work flexible and/or weekend hours.
- Occasional on-site attendance for corporate meetings and events.
What we bring to table:
- Salary range: $75,000-$100,000. Actual offer may vary from posted hiring range based on location, work experience, and/or education.
- Competitive insurance benefits including medical, dental, vision, HSA, and FSA (dependent care/medical)
- Company paid life, accidental death & dismemberment, and long-term disability insurance

ISAT Total Support /Tomarco is a leading provider of seismic engineering consulting services and the related products and hardware used for nonstructural seismic bracing and the support of Mechanical, Electrical, and Piping systems. Our focus is geared toward building utility systems within the commercial and industrial construction markets. Our primary focus includes but is not limited to, HVAC, mechanical, piping, distributed electrical systems, plumbing, process piping & fire protection contractors.

Headquartered in Southern California, ISAT also has offices in Northern California, Nevada, Arizona, Oregon, Washington, Utah, Georgia, North Carolina, Chicago, Atlanta, New Zealand, New York, Texas, and Puerto Rico. Additional expansion is expected.


SUMMARY AND PURPOSE:

As an Assistant Project Manager, you’ll work closely with a Project Manager mentor, supporting various project tasks, including customer billing, modeling, coordination, point loads, and custom engineering. This role is ideal for a detail-oriented professional eager to develop project management skills through hands-on experience and mentorship. You’ll gain exposure to essential functions in project coordination, documentation, communication, and technical support, building a foundation for future project management opportunities.

RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE POSITION

  • Manage smaller projects under direct guidance from a mentor, with all work reviewed.

  • Develop basic proficiency in AutoCAD, Revit, and Navisworks.
  • Acquire foundational knowledge of codes governing seismic engineering, including ASCE-7, IBC, UFC, and CBC.
  • Prepare quotations for suspended distributed utilities and basic custom engineering.
  • Maintain an organized and tidy workspace.
  • Perform additional duties as assigned by management.

QUALIFICATIONS AND SKILLS:

  • Bachelor’s degree in supply chain management, industrial engineering, or a related field, or equivalent work experience.
  • Ability to read, analyze, and interpret technical documents, business journals, and regulations.
  • Proficient in writing business correspondence and presenting information to various stakeholders.
  • Effective oral and written communication skills across all organizational levels.
  • Strong organizational skills with attention to detail, file management proficiency, and the ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines.
  • Basic mathematical skills for calculating variances, commissions, and financial ratios; experience with software for programming calculations.
  • Willingness to learn software applications such as AutoCAD, Revit, and Navisworks.
  • Basic knowledge or willingness to learn industry codes, including ASCE-7, IBC, UFC, and CBC.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
  • Effective communication and interpersonal skills to collaborate across teams.

description:

Randa Apparel & Accessories is one of the world’s leading fashion clothing and accessories companies, operating across 11 countries with a portfolio of 30+ iconic brands, including Haggar, Levi’s, Tommy Hilfiger, Calvin Klein, Totes, Isotoner, and Columbia Sportswear. From the #1 dress pant brand in North America to the #1 belt and wallet, RAA sets the standard for excellence and innovation

At Haggar Men’s Apparel, we create products with purpose—combining quality, comfort, innovation, and value to strengthen our position as the market share leader in Men’s Pants and Tailored Clothing and one of America’s leading menswear brands.

As a Designer, you will join a small, entrepreneurial team with the opportunity to make a visible impact through meaningful ownership of your category, contributing a strong design point of view, product expertise, and collaborative leadership.

Working closely with the Director of Design, you will translate broad seasonal direction into specific, commercially compelling designs for your category—driving concepts through development and execution while making sound decisions on your line with a high degree of independence.

This role is ideal for a designer with strong apparel experience who thrives in a fast-paced environment, can balance creativity with commercial relevance, and brings demonstrated success partnering with mills, factories, and cross-functional teams to drive innovation, solve problems, and deliver products with impact.

Essential Job Functions:

MUST INCLUDE PORTFOLIO

  • Design & Concept Development:
    • Own the translation of seasonal direction into specific product ideas for your category, driving concepts, fabrications, product updates, line edits, and newness that align with market trends, brand strategy, and business goals.
    • Stay connected to the competitive landscape through store visits, online research, and ongoing trend awareness.
    • Create clear, compelling presentation materials and trend tools using PowerPoint and Adobe Illustrator to communicate product concepts, seasonal direction, and business opportunities.
    • Present the product story with confidence and clarity to internal partners, leadership, and retail customers, using strong visual and verbal communication skills to influence decisions and build alignment.

  • Technical Sketching & Product Specification:

    • Translate broad design direction into accurate flat sketches and CADs that clearly communicate product intent, construction, and key details for development and execution.
    • Prepare, update, and maintain technical sketches and product specifications in Adobe Illustrator with accuracy and attention to detail.

  • Design Package Completion

    • Lead fabric and trim development, sample ordering, and prototype follow-up through direct communication with mills, factories, and cross-functional partners, driving innovation and ensuring progress against seasonal timelines.
    • Ensure design packages, including sketches and BOM details, are complete, accurate, and delivered on schedule to support product development, technical design, and vendor execution.

  • Approvals & Production Readiness

    • Manage approvals for materials and color components, including labdips, handlooms,knit-downs, and strike-offs, ensuring design intent and timing are maintained throughout development.
    • Lead final sample reviews and approvals within the scope of the role to help ensure products are ready for production with design intent intact.
    • Coordinate cross-functionally and participate in weekly fittings to solve issues quickly, keep development moving forward, and support timely execution of the line.

  • Fittings & Execution:

    • Communicate design and fit intent clearly to Technical Design partners and participate actively in fittings to ensure the product is executed as intended.
    • Maintain clear documentation of updates and design decisions across product development tools and systems.

  • Minimum Qualifications

    • 3+years of apparel design experience, preferably in menswear
    • Bachelor’s degree in Apparel Design or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience
    • Experienced manager in managing development directly with overseas mills, factories, and global partners
    • Knowledge of apparel construction and manufacturing processes
    • Strong understanding of trends, consumer insights, and the competitive landscape, with the ability to translate direction into a commercially relevant product
    • Working knowledge of color evaluation processes and terminology, including visual and digital color review
    • Understanding of retail math and the ability to balance creativity, innovation,cost, and margin goals
    • Experience working in PLM or similar product development systems
    • Demonstrated success driving innovation and development with mill and factory partners
    • Proficiency in Adobe Illustrator, Photoshop, PowerPoint, Word, and Excel
    • Strong presentation skills with the ability to communicate product concepts and seasonal direction to internal partners, leadership, and retail customers
    • Ability to thrive in a dynamic environment, manage multiple priorities, make sound decisions, and adapt quickly to changing business needs
    • Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and follow-through
    • Portfolio that demonstrates original design work, creative thinking, and technical capability

  • Bonus Qualifications

    • Experience in Men’s Apparel and Tailored Clothing is a plus
    • CLO3D and YPLM experience is a plus

What we Offer:

  • Competitive base salary.
  • Three weeks of paid time off within the first year of employment.
  • Company-provided life insurance, short-term disability, long-term disability, and paid parental leave.

title: [LTA-TRO] SENIOR/ EXECUTIVE/ DATA ENGINEER - TRANSPORT AI PROGRAMME
description:
What the role is:

(LTA-TRO) Senior/ Executive/ Data Engineer - Transport AI Programme, LTA Singapore


What you will be working on:

Singapore's land transport network moves millions of people every day. As AI reshapes what's possible in transport operations, the Land Transport Authority is investing in AI capabilities that will meaningfully improve how the network is sensed, managed, and optimised - for commuters, operators, and public officers alike.

AI systems are only as good as the data that powers them. As a Data Engineer in LTA's Transport AI Programme, you will design, build, and maintain the data infrastructure and pipelines that enable AI models and applications to access high-quality, timely, and trustworthy data. You will work across LTA's rich transport data ecosystem - spanning real-time sensor feeds, transit operations data, traffic systems, and road infrastructure - to ensure that data is reliably ingested, transformed, governed, and made available for AI development and production use.

This role reports to the Transport AI Programme Deputy Director and works closely with AI software developers, the AI architect, infrastructure engineers, and industry partners on joint data integration efforts.

Key Responsibilities
  • Design, build, and maintain scalable data pipelines that ingest, transform, and serve structured and unstructured data from diverse transport data sources, including real-time streams and batch feeds.
  • Develop and manage data models, data catalogues, and feature stores that support AI model training, evaluation, and inference across transport use cases.
  • Ensure data quality, consistency, and lineage across the data platform, implementing validation checks, monitoring, and alerting to detect and resolve data issues early.
  • Implement data governance practices in line with Singapore Government data classification requirements, including access controls, data masking, anonymisation, and audit logging for sensitive transport and personal data.
  • Work with the AI Architect and Infrastructure Engineer to design data infrastructure that is performant, cost-efficient, and aligned with LTA's cloud and hybrid environment.
  • Collaborate with data scientists and AI developers to understand data requirements for model development, and translate these into reliable, production-grade data products.
  • Support the integration of external data sources from industry partners, ensuring that data exchange meets LTA's standards for security, quality, and interoperability.
  • Contribute to the development of shared data platforms and reusable data assets that can be leveraged across multiple AI use cases within the programme.
  • Monitor and maintain data pipelines in production, supporting incident response and continuous improvement of data reliability and freshness.

What we are looking for:

  • Knowledge in Computer Science, Data Science, Business Analytics or a related field, with at least 3-6 years of relevant professional experience. Candidates will be assessed based on their experience and may be considered at the intermediate or senior level.
  • Proficiency in Python and SQL is expected, along with hands-on experience with modern data pipeline frameworks such as Apache Spark, Apache Kafka, dbt, Airflow, or equivalent.
  • Experience with cloud data platforms (such as AWS Glue, Azure Data Factory, Google Dataflow, or Databricks) and data warehousing or lakehouse architectures is important.
  • Familiarity with real-time or streaming data processing is a strong advantage, particularly given LTA's operational context involving live sensor and transit data.
  • Experience building feature stores or data pipelines specifically for ML/AI workloads is highly desirable. Knowledge of data governance frameworks, data quality tooling, and metadata management practices will set candidates apart.
  • Experience working in regulated, government, or critical infrastructure environments - particularly where data sensitivity and access controls are paramount - is a plus.
  • Comfortable working in cross-functional teams and collaborating with both technical and non-technical stakeholders to translate operational data needs into robust engineering solutions.
  • Strong communication skills to explain technical concepts to both engineers and non-technical stakeholders. Inclination to work in a collaborative, fast-moving Agile environment. Strong in communication with the ability to explain complex technical concepts clearly to diverse audience

As part of the shortlisting process for the role, you may be required to complete a medical declaration and / or undergo further assessment.


About Land Transport Authority

The Land Transport Authority (LTA) is a statutory board under Ministry of Transport that spearheads land transport developments in Singapore. We are seeking dynamic, energetic, highly motivated, passionate and qualified professionals to join us.Many opportunities & challenges await those who are keen on an exciting career to realise our commitment to envision & implement an integrated transport system.

description:
*Applications from this recruitment may be considered for future Water Treatment Technician full-time and Limited Term Employment (LTE) positions. LTE positions are project/program based and typically have a predetermined expected end date.

Working for Denver Water offers a rewarding and comprehensive employment experience marked by exceptional benefits and a strong organizational culture. These principles guide every aspect of the organization, fostering a collaborative and purpose-driven environment where employees are empowered to make a meaningful impact on the community and the future of water sustainability.

Water Treatment Tech

This is an entry level position. Under direct supervision, train on and perform a variety of jobs necessary for the operation and maintenance of water treatment plants and appurtenant structures. As a treatment technician, learn to use physical and chemical conventional water treatment techniques to become proficient at providing an adequate supply of safe, high-quality water to the public. As an asset management technician, learn to maintain plant equipment and structures such as chemical feed/storage, piping, valves, basins, and reservoirs.

Water Treatment Sr. Tech

Under general supervision, perform a variety of duties essential to the operation and maintenance of two or more water treatment plants (including potable and recycled). As a Senior Technician maintain plant equipment and structures such as chemical feed/storage, instrumentation, piping, valves, basins, and reservoirs to ensure safe, adequate, and reliable delivery of high-quality water.

Asset Management Tech: Under direct supervision, learn and become proficient at performing a variety of laboring, semi-skilled, and skilled duties related to managing and maintaining assets at treatment plants. Install, maintain, demolish, troubleshoot, and repair mechanical systems throughout the treatment facilities. Install and maintain small process pumps, valves, motors, compressors, piping systems, gauges, pneumatics, hydraulics, and other related systems.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

All Technicians must be able to perform safety sensitive functions; provide appropriate first response to emergencies and spills including those involving hazardous materials, wear respirators including self-contained breathing apparatus as required. They may be required to perform on-call duty, work shifts, weekends, holidays, and overtime as directed, and work outdoors in a variety of weather conditions. Technicians report to two or more Denver Water treatment plants. All team members perform other duties as assigned and cross train as needed.

  • Learn and become proficient at determining and changing plant flows to meet system demands. Operate necessary computer equipment to coordinate plant operations.
  • Learn and become proficient at controlling quality and quantity of finished water by regulating filter operations as required. Maintain proper chemical dosages and feed equipment settings for influent and effluent plant flows.
  • Learn and become proficient at performing laboratory tests on influent and effluent water such as turbidity, alkalinity and hardness, chlorine residual, ammonia residual, fluoride concentration, pH, odor, and coagulant dosage tests. Develop written operating procedures.

Additionally, Water Treatment Sr. Techs are responsible for the following:

  • Utilize plumbing, mechanical, and construction skills and monitoring technology to perform preventative and predictive maintenance on treatment plant equipment, basins, piping, and chemical feed systems. Clean basins, piping, and chemical tanks in preparation for inspection and repairs.
  • Lead and support internal maintenance projects including planning, ordering parts, creating job plans and completion of project.
  • Maintain and update records in Maximo asset management tracking system.
  • Assist specialized trades personnel in making major and/or specialized repairs to equipment. Assist contractors in coordination of plant upgrades.
  • Must be able to read and interpret engineering drawings and equipment O&Ms to assist with process troubleshooting, repairs, and plant upgrades.
  • Monitor systems for alarms, adjust, and provide appropriate response.
  • Operate and maintain chlorination equipment for pre-treatment, filtration, and disinfection systems. Maintain Risk Management Program (RMP) compliance through training, proper use of PPE and annual mandatory inspection, repair and replacement of chlorination equipment and instrumentation. Must complete initial 40-hour RMP training and meet the annual 8-hour RMP training requirements.
  • Perform calibration of chemical feed equipment. Order chemicals and take delivery of bulk chemicals.
  • Perform facility inspections of treatment processes, equipment, instrumentation, storage tanks and grounds. Make visual inspections of facility processes, equipment, instrumentation, and facility grounds.
  • Perform complex plant start-ups and shutdowns, including emergency shutdowns.
  • Assess project risks and develop job hazard analysis (JHA) and adhere to Denver Water’s safety practices and policies.
  • Will assist in training new technicians. Will create and/or update SOPs and other training documents.
  • Must be able to perform safety sensitive functions.
  • Perform related duties as required.
  • May be required to perform on-call duty, work shifts, weekends, holidays, and overtime as directed, and work outdoors in a variety of weather conditions.
  • Operate and maintain solids handling systems.
  • Provide appropriate first response to emergencies and spills including those involving hazardous materials. Wear respirators including self-contained breathing apparatus as required.

The Career Services Coach is responsible for timely and accurate documentation in CampusVue of all active students, graduates and employer communication. In addition, the Career Services Coach will be responsible for tracking all unplaced graduates including the graduate’s employment criteria needs.

  • Conduct outbound connect activity, as needed, to ensure ongoing communication between graduates and team

  • Provide guidance to students and graduates and always maintain a high level of professional standards

  • Coordinate and conduct scheduled resume preparation, interview techniques, job search/research, and other professional development sessions

  • Provide availability and opportunities to conduct One-on-One coaching sessions with students and graduates

  • Assist in proactive job search efforts by providing job leads, resources and online application assistance to generate employment opportunities in addition to working with the job orders received from the Business Solutions Consultants if applicable

  • Conduct community and employer outreach to identify viable employment opportunities for students and graduates within their chosen field

  • Support the team’s efforts in completing Employment Verification documents and accurate data entry of all information.
